api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IGroupFinderQueueService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Service interface for the dungeon group finder's queue: who is waiting for a group, and the one operation that turns waiters into a party with an instance. public interface IGroupFinderQueueService Remarks The queue is shared by every scene server on a world server, and every one of them runs the same matching pump against it. Nothing here assumes a single matcher: the methods that change a row's state are single statements or single transactions whose WHERE clauses re-assert the state they expect, so two servers acting on the same rows at once produce one winner and one no-op rather than a character in two groups. One clock. Every heartbeat, queue time and match time is stamped by the database's clock, and every staleness test is made against it in SQL; callers pass how OLD a heartbeat may be, never a moment. The rows are written by one scene server and judged by every other, so a moment computed from the caller's own clock compared two machines' clocks: a server running 30 s behind had waiters nobody else counted, and at 60 s behind its rows were swept from under it every sweep. All methods return DatabaseResult or DatabaseResult<T>. Write operations go through the BaseService execution wrappers for transient-failure retry and exception mapping. Methods CountWaitingAsync(long, SceneType, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) Counts the live waiters for one dungeon at one difficulty. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> CountWaitingAsync(long worldServerId, SceneType sceneType, string sceneName, int difficulty, TimeSpan staleAfter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long World server to count on. sceneType SceneType Kind of instance. sceneName string Scene. difficulty int Difficulty or format index. staleAfter TimeSpan Rows whose heartbeat is older than this are not counted. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> How many are waiting. CountWaitingAsync(long, IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderQueueKey>, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) Counts the live waiters for several keys at once. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyDictionary<GroupFinderQueueKey, int>>> CountWaitingAsync(long worldServerId, IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderQueueKey> keys, TimeSpan staleAfter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long World server to count on. keys IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderQueueKey> What to count. Repeated keys are counted once. staleAfter TimeSpan Rows whose heartbeat is older than this are not counted. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyDictionary<GroupFinderQueueKey, int>>> One entry per distinct requested key, ALWAYS present: a key nobody waits under maps to 0. Remarks The pump's count: one statement for every key its waiters are queued under, where it used to run CountWaitingAsync(long, SceneType, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) once per key, in series. DeleteAsync(long, bool, CancellationToken) Removes a character's queue row. Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> DeleteAsync(long characterId, bool onlyIfWaiting, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterId long Character to remove. onlyIfWaiting bool True to leave a Matched row alone. A player who presses Leave in the instant after their group formed has already been placed in a party, and quietly deleting the row would leave them in that party with no transfer coming; the caller must refuse instead. False when the row's job is done — the transfer has been dispatched — or when the character is gone. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> True when a row was removed. DeleteReturningAsync(long, CancellationToken) Removes a character's queue row whatever its state, and reports what was removed. Task<DatabaseResult<GroupFinderQueueData?>> DeleteReturningAsync(long characterId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterId long Character to remove. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<GroupFinderQueueData?>> The removed row, or null when the character had none. Remarks For the disconnect path. Whether the row was still waiting or already matched decides what else has to happen — a matched character who logged out before being moved holds a seat in a party that will never see them, and must be taken out of it — and reading the row first would race the matcher on another scene server. DELETE ... RETURNING answers atomically: if the matcher's transaction holds the row, this waits for it to commit and then removes, and reports, the matched row. DeleteStaleAsync(TimeSpan, int, CancellationToken) Removes rows whose heartbeat is older than staleAfter. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> DeleteStaleAsync(TimeSpan staleAfter, int maxRows = 256, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters staleAfter TimeSpan Rows whose heartbeat is older than this are eligible. maxRows int Upper bound on rows removed in one call. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> Rows deleted. Remarks Bounded per call so a large backlog drains across several sweeps rather than in one long statement. Matched rows are reaped too: a matched character whose server died was placed in a party it will never be transferred into, and the party system's own absent- member handling takes it from there. EnqueueAsync(long, long, SceneType, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) Puts a character in the queue for one dungeon at one difficulty, or moves their existing entry to it. Task<DatabaseResult<long>> EnqueueAsync(long worldServerId, long characterId, SceneType sceneType, string sceneName, int difficulty, TimeSpan staleAfter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long World server the character belongs to. characterId long Character queuing. sceneType SceneType Kind of instance: the shared value cast in — 2 (Group) for a dungeon, 3 (PvP) for an arena. sceneName string Dungeon or arena scene they want to play. difficulty int Index into the template's list: a dungeon's difficulty or an arena's format. staleAfter TimeSpan A matched row whose heartbeat is older than this is treated as abandoned and re-pointed like a waiting one. Without this a character whose scene server died between the match and the transfer could never queue again until the stale sweep happened to reach them. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<long>> The row's ID, or 0 when the character is already matched and nothing changed. Remarks A character already waiting for something else is re-pointed rather than refused — pressing Find Group at a second entrance means "this one instead", and their place in line restarts. A character whose row is already Matched cannot be moved: the group they were placed in is real, and their scene server is about to transfer them into it. EnqueueGroupAsync(long, SceneType, string, int, long, IReadOnlyList<long>, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) Queues a pre-made group together, all or none. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> EnqueueGroupAsync(long worldServerId, SceneType sceneType, string sceneName, int difficulty, long groupId, IReadOnlyList<long> characterIds, TimeSpan staleAfter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long World server the group belongs to. sceneType SceneType Kind of instance being queued for. sceneName string Scene they want to play. difficulty int Format index into the template's list. groupId long Identity of the pre-made group; the party id. characterIds IReadOnlyList<long> Every member, including the one who pressed the button. staleAfter TimeSpan Stale heartbeat age, as for EnqueueAsync(long, long, SceneType, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken). cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> Rows written, equal to the member count on success. A StaleState failure, with nothing written, when a member is already matched elsewhere: the group queues together or not at all. Remarks Every member gets a row carrying the same groupId, in one transaction: a member whose row is live-matched already refuses the whole group, so a party cannot end up half in one queue and half in another. Members already waiting for something else are re-pointed exactly as EnqueueAsync(long, long, SceneType, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) re-points a single character. FetchBackfillOpeningsAsync(long, CancellationToken) The arenas and formats that have a seat to backfill right now: a live match with an open backfill window, a ready instance, and a team short of its size. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderQueueKey>>> FetchBackfillOpeningsAsync(long worldServerId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long World server to look on. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderQueueKey>>> The arena keys (scene type PvP, scene name, format) with an opening, each once. Remarks A plain read, no locks: the pump's check before TryBackfillArenaSeatAsync(long, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken), whose transaction locks and scans, and which used to run for every arena key with local waiters on every pump whether or not any window was open. A key this reports is only a candidate; the transaction re-decides everything under its lock. PulseAsync(IReadOnlyList<long>, CancellationToken) Refreshes the heartbeat on the rows of characters connected to the calling scene server, and returns those rows as the refresh left them. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderPulseData>>> PulseAsync(IReadOnlyList<long> characterIds, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterIds IReadOnlyList<long> Characters to pulse; duplicates and non-positive ids are ignored. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GroupFinderPulseData>>> The rows that exist. Characters with no row are simply absent. Remarks A row whose heartbeat stops is excluded from matching by TryFormGroupAsync(long, string, int, int, TimeSpan, SceneType, byte, byte, CancellationToken) and CountWaitingAsync(long, SceneType, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) and eventually removed by DeleteStaleAsync(TimeSpan, int, CancellationToken). That is the only defence against a scene server dying with waiters on it: nothing else would ever remove them, and a group formed around a character nobody can reach is a party of four with an empty slot that never fills. One statement, UPDATE ... RETURNING. The pump needs both the heartbeat and the rows — which of its characters were matched, by itself or any other server, and which were removed underneath it — and used to spend a round trip on each. A row matched into a party also carries the character's membership, read in the same statement, because the pump honours the match only while they are in that party and tells them the rank they hold; that used to be one more round trip per matched row, in series. ReleaseClaimAsync(long, long, CancellationToken) Returns a character claimed by TryClaimForInstanceAsync(long, long, long, CancellationToken) to the waiting state, when the join it was claimed for could not be completed. Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> ReleaseClaimAsync(long characterId, long instanceId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterId long Character to release. instanceId long Instance the claim named; a row matched to anything else is left alone. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> True when a row was released. TryBackfillArenaSeatAsync(long, string, int, TimeSpan, CancellationToken) Seats the longest-waiting eligible waiter for an arena in a live match of that arena and format that has a vacated seat and an open backfill window. Task<DatabaseResult<ArenaBackfillData>> TryBackfillArenaSeatAsync(long worldServerId, string sceneName, int format, TimeSpan staleAfter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long sceneName string format int staleAfter TimeSpan cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<ArenaBackfillData>> Remarks One transaction: the match row is locked, the vacancy re-counted under the lock, the oldest waiter locked and bound to the instance, and a new seated member row inserted. Ranked matches take waiters from the same (ranked) format only, because the format is what the queue row records. TryClaimForInstanceAsync(long, long, long, CancellationToken) Marks one waiting character as matched into an existing instance, for the late-join path that fills empty slots in runs already open. Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> TryClaimForInstanceAsync(long characterId, long partyId, long instanceId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterId long Waiting character. partyId long Party that owns the instance. instanceId long Instance being joined. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> True when the row was waiting and is now matched. Remarks The status is re-asserted in the WHERE: a row that another server has already matched is not touched, so a character cannot be handed to two runs at once. The caller adds the character to the instance's party after this succeeds, and calls ReleaseClaimAsync(long, long, CancellationToken) if that is refused. TryFormArenaMatchAsync(long, string, int, int, int, int, TimeSpan, int, ArenaRatingSource, ArenaComposeOptions, CancellationToken) Forms an arena match from the longest-waiting eligible players, keeping pre-made groups together, opening the instance and writing the match and its seats, all in one transaction. Task<DatabaseResult<ArenaMatchFormedData>> TryFormArenaMatchAsync(long worldServerId, string sceneName, int format, int templateId, int teamCount, int teamSize, TimeSpan staleAfter, int maxCandidates = 128, ArenaRatingSource ratingSource = default, ArenaComposeOptions composeOptions = default, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long World server to form the match on. sceneName string Arena scene to open. format int Format index into the template's list, matched exactly. templateId int Arena template ID recorded on the match. teamCount int Teams to fill. teamSize int Seats per team. staleAfter TimeSpan Waiters whose heartbeat is older than this are not eligible. maxCandidates int How many waiters to lock and consider. Clamped to a sane range. ratingSource ArenaRatingSource composeOptions ArenaComposeOptions cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<ArenaMatchFormedData>> The match, or a result whose Formed is false when no full match could be composed. Remarks The arena counterpart of TryFormGroupAsync(long, string, int, int, TimeSpan, SceneType, byte, byte, CancellationToken), with the same guarantees: the candidates are row-locked with plain FOR UPDATE, eligibility is re-asserted inside the transaction, and either everything is written or nothing is. Composition — which waiter sits on which team — is decided by ArenaMatchComposer on the locked candidates, so the transaction has nothing to decide and the rule is testable on its own. Eligibility here is the arena's: a seat in a match that has not ended, or a usable dungeon or arena instance held by the character, excludes them. Party membership does not, because arenas are the place a party queues together. The instance row is written private with no owning party; the match row is what says who is in it. It is still inserted under the one-instance guard, against every seat. TryFormGroupAsync(long, string, int, int, TimeSpan, SceneType, byte, byte, CancellationToken) Task<DatabaseResult<GroupFinderMatchData>> TryFormGroupAsync(long worldServerId, string sceneName, int difficulty, int groupSize, TimeSpan staleAfter, SceneType sceneType, byte leaderRank, byte memberRank, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerId long sceneName string difficulty int groupSize int staleAfter TimeSpan sceneType SceneType leaderRank byte memberRank byte cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<GroupFinderMatchData>>

api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IGuildApplicationService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Service interface for the guild recruitment directory and its application queue. public interface IGuildApplicationService Methods ApplyAsync(long, long, string, int, int, CancellationToken) Submits an application, refusing duplicates, non-recruiting guilds and full guilds. Task<DatabaseResult> ApplyAsync(long guildId, long characterId, string message, int maxCapacity, int maxPendingPerCharacter, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild applied to. characterId long Applying character. message string Applicant message. maxCapacity int Guild member cap. maxPendingPerCharacter int Most outstanding applications one character may hold. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult> Success, or one code per refusal: NOT_FOUND (no such applicant, or the guild is gone or not recruiting), ALREADY_MEMBER (the applicant is already in a guild), CAPACITY_EXCEEDED (the guild is full), QUOTA_EXCEEDED (the applicant holds the most outstanding applications allowed) and ALREADY_EXISTS (an application to this guild is already pending). Remarks Every one of those conditions is tested inside the INSERT. Checking them in application code and inserting afterwards is a time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap the applicant controls the timing of: apply to a guild with one seat left, twice, from two clients. DeleteAsync(long, long, CancellationToken) Deletes one application by ID. Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> DeleteAsync(long applicationId, long guildId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters applicationId long Application ID. guildId long The guild the caller believes the application belongs to. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<bool>> True when a row was actually removed. Remarks The guild is part of the WHERE clause, not merely validated beforehand: it is the last line that stops an officer of one guild resolving another guild's application by ID. The boolean result is what the accept path uses to claim the application exactly once — two officers pressing Accept simultaneously, only one of whom gets true. DeleteManyByCharacterAsync(long, CancellationToken) Deletes every application a character has outstanding. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> DeleteManyByCharacterAsync(long characterId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterId long Character ID. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> The number of rows removed. Remarks Run when a character joins any guild. An application that outlives the applicant's guildless state is an accept waiting to fail. FetchAsync(long, CancellationToken) Fetches one application by ID. Task<DatabaseResult<GuildApplicationData?>> FetchAsync(long applicationId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters applicationId long Application ID. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<GuildApplicationData?>> The application, or null. FetchManyAsync(long, int, CancellationToken) Fetches the pending applications for one guild, oldest first. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildApplicationData>>> FetchManyAsync(long guildId, int limit, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. limit int Maximum rows to return. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildApplicationData>>> The pending queue. SearchDirectoryAsync(string, int, CancellationToken) Searches the recruitment directory. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildDirectoryEntryData>>> SearchDirectoryAsync(string searchTerm, int limit, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters searchTerm string Optional case-insensitive term matched against name, blurb and tags. limit int Maximum rows to return. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildDirectoryEntryData>>> Matching recruiting guilds with their current member counts.

api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IGuildLogService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Service interface for the append-only guild activity log. public interface IGuildLogService Remarks Deliberately does not implement the shared IPersistAction/IFetchManyByKeyAction shapes. Those describe a row that is written, re-read and updated under a version; a log row is written once and never touched again, and its read is "the most recent N", which the key-based fetch contracts have no way to express. Methods AppendAsync(GuildLogData, CancellationToken) Appends one row to a guild's activity log. Task<DatabaseResult> AppendAsync(GuildLogData entry, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters entry GuildLogData The event to record. ID is ignored. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<DatabaseResult> A DatabaseResult indicating success or failure. FetchRecentAsync(long, int, CancellationToken) Fetches a guild's most recent log rows, newest first. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildLogData>>> FetchRecentAsync(long guildId, int limit, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. limit int Maximum rows to return. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildLogData>>> The most recent rows, newest first. PruneAsync(long, int, CancellationToken) Deletes log rows beyond the most recent keep for one guild. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> PruneAsync(long guildId, int keep, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. keep int Number of newest rows to retain. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> The number of rows removed. Remarks An unbounded append-only table attached to a long-lived guild grows without limit and nothing else in the schema would ever remove from it. Trimming to a fixed depth is what makes the feature safe to leave running for a year.

api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IGuildRankService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Service interface for a guild's editable rank ladder. public interface IGuildRankService Remarks The rank rows are the authority for what a member may do. Nothing in this interface takes a requester: authorisation is the server's job and it happens before these calls, against the rows FetchManyAsync(long, CancellationToken) returns. A storage service that also decided permissions would be two responsibilities with one test surface. Methods DeleteAsync(long, byte, CancellationToken) Deletes a rank row, refusing while any member still holds it. Task<DatabaseResult> DeleteAsync(long guildId, byte rankOrder, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. rankOrder byte The rank position to delete. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult> Success; IN_USE while a member still holds the rank; NOT_FOUND when there is no such rank; VALIDATION_ERROR only for a malformed request. Remarks The occupancy test and the delete are ONE statement. Split across two round trips, a member could be moved into the rank between them and end up holding a rank that no longer exists — which reads back as no permissions at all, quietly, forever. EnsureDefaultsAsync(long, IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData>, CancellationToken) Creates the default rank ladder for a guild if it does not already have one. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> EnsureDefaultsAsync(long guildId, IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData> defaults, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. defaults IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData> The rows to seed, in any order. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> The number of rows actually inserted. Remarks IDEMPOTENT. Every row is inserted with ON CONFLICT (guild_id, rank_order) DO NOTHING, so running this against a guild that already has ranks changes nothing and returns zero. That is what makes it safe to call on every guild read, which is in turn what makes the migration of existing guilds require no migration step at all: a guild created before rank rows existed grows them the first time anybody looks at it, with the permissions its old enum ranks implied. FetchManyAsync(long, CancellationToken) Fetches every rank row for a guild, ordered by rank order ascending. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData>>> FetchManyAsync(long guildId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData>>> The guild's rank ladder. FetchManyAsync(long[], CancellationToken) Fetches the rank ladders of several guilds in one query. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyDictionary<long, IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData>>>> FetchManyAsync(long[] guildIds, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildIds long[] The guilds to read. Non-positive and repeated IDs are ignored. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyDictionary<long, IReadOnlyList<GuildRankData>>>> One entry per distinct requested guild, ALWAYS present, each ladder ordered by rank order ascending exactly as FetchManyAsync(long, CancellationToken) orders it. A guild with no rank rows maps to an empty list; seeding it is the caller's decision, as it is for the single-guild read. InsertAsync(GuildRankData, int, byte, CancellationToken) Inserts a new rank at a position, moving everything already at or above it up one rung. Task<DatabaseResult> InsertAsync(GuildRankData rank, int maxRanks, byte maxRankOrder, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters rank GuildRankData The rank to insert. Its rank order is the POSITION it takes. maxRanks int Maximum rank rows one guild may own. maxRankOrder byte Highest legal rank order, which bounds the shift. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult> A result indicating success or failure. Remarks Why this inserts rather than fills a hole. A guild is seeded with three CONTIGUOUS ranks — member 1, officer 2, leader 3 — and a rank may only be created strictly below the creator's own seat. A leader at order 3 therefore has orders 1 and 2 to choose from and both are taken, so a "create at a free position" service could never add a rank to a guild that had not already had one removed. Making room is the operation; finding a gap was never going to find one. Membership rows move with the ladder. character_guild.rank holds the same order byte, so every member at or above the insertion point is shifted by the same one rung, in the same transaction. Relative standing is what the whole permission model compares, and it is preserved exactly: a member who outranked another before the insert still does, and the leader — defined as the highest order that exists — is still the same character. The shift is applied one row at a time, highest first. (guild_id, rank_order) is UNIQUE and PostgreSQL checks it per row rather than at statement end, so a single SET rank_order = rank_order + 1 over the whole range raises a duplicate key the moment the planner happens to reach a row whose target is still occupied. Descending, each target has just been vacated. Twelve ranks is the cap, so this is at most eleven statements for something a guild does once in a while. UpdateAsync(long, byte, string, long, long, CancellationToken) Updates one rank's name and permission mask. Task<DatabaseResult> UpdateAsync(long guildId, byte rankOrder, string name, long permissions, long incomingVersion, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. rankOrder byte The rank position to update. name string New display name. permissions long New permission bit mask. incomingVersion long The authoritative, monotonic version for this update. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult> A result indicating success or failure.

api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IGuildService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Service interface for guild management operations. Provides async methods for guild creation, deletion, and retrieval. public interface IGuildService : IExistsByKeyAction<string>, IPersistAction<string, long?>, IDeleteByKeyAction<long>, IFetchByKeyAction<long, GuildData?>, IFetchByKeyAction<string, GuildData?> Inherited Members IExistsByKeyAction<string>.ExistsAsync(string, CancellationToken) IPersistAction<string, long?>.PersistAsync(string, CancellationToken) IDeleteByKeyAction<long>.DeleteAsync(long, CancellationToken) IFetchByKeyAction<long, GuildData?>.FetchAsync(long, CancellationToken) IFetchByKeyAction<string, GuildData?>.FetchAsync(string, CancellationToken) Remarks Write operations (Persist*, Delete*) in this service use execution strategies to ensure transient database failures are automatically retried according to the retry policy configured on the DbContext. Execution is wrapped by BaseService for retries and exception mapping. All methods return DatabaseResult or DatabaseResult<T> to provide structured error information through the DatabaseException system, helping distinguish between: - Validation failures (invalid parameters) - Business rule violations (name already exists) - Database errors (connection issues, constraint violations, timeouts) - Entity not found errors - Unexpected runtime errors Name lookups are case-insensitive by using a normalized field (e.g. name_lowercase) in the database. Methods FetchExistingIdsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<long>, CancellationToken) Which of the given guilds still exist. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyCollection<long>>> FetchExistingIdsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<long> guildIds, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildIds IReadOnlyCollection<long> The guilds to look for. cancellationToken CancellationToken Token to cancel the operation. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyCollection<long>>> The subset of guildIds that still exist. Remarks For the scene servers' update pump. A disbanded guild's row goes, and its guild_updates row goes with it by cascade, so the pump — which only ever learned of changes through that row — never heard that the guild was gone, and its members on every other server kept a guild that no longer existed (issue #267). The pump asks this instead. FetchNameAsync(long, CancellationToken) Fetches the name of a guild by ID. Task<DatabaseResult<string?>> FetchNameAsync(long guildId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<string>> A DatabaseResult<T> containing the guild name on success, or null if the guild was not found. Returns a failure result on database errors. Remarks This method uses LINQ (FirstOrDefaultAsync with AsNoTracking) and automatically benefits from the retry policy configured on the DbContext without requiring explicit execution strategy wrapping. FetchNamesAsync(IReadOnlyList<long>, CancellationToken) Fetches the names of a set of guilds in one query. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyDictionary<long, string>>> FetchNamesAsync(IReadOnlyList<long> guildIds, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildIds IReadOnlyList<long> Guilds to resolve. Duplicates and non-positive IDs are ignored. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyDictionary<long, string>>> The name of each guild found, by ID. A guild that does not exist is absent. A failure result on database errors. Remarks For the scene servers' batched name lookups: every guild name a client asked for in one frame, resolved together instead of one query per guild (hot-path audit M18). Bounded internally as well as by its caller, because it answers a request a client controls the timing of. PersistMessageOfTheDayAsync(long, string, CancellationToken) Updates the message of the day for a guild. Task<DatabaseResult> PersistMessageOfTheDayAsync(long guildId, string messageOfTheDay, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildId long Guild ID. messageOfTheDay string The new message of the day text. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult> DatabaseResult indicating success or failure. PersistNoticeAsync(long, string, CancellationToken) Updates the notice text for a guild. api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface ILeaderboardService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Read-only ranking of characters by a number the game already stores. public interface ILeaderboardService Remarks Nothing here writes. Every source is owned by the system that writes it — the arena match coordinator for ratings, the character save for attributes and achievements — and a leaderboard is only a way of reading it across characters. Eligibility is decided in the SQL, not by the caller. A deleted character (a soft delete: the row stays with a renamed name) and a character on a banned account are never ranked, and neither is anyone on a staff account unless the query asks for them. Ranks are computed over the eligible rows only, so removing somebody closes the gap they leave rather than leaving a hole in the numbering. One rank definition, used twice. A page ranks its rows with RANK() ordered by score, and a standing is one plus the eligible characters with a strictly higher score — the same number by construction, so a character looked up on its own is given the rank it would carry on the page. Rows with equal scores share a rank; the order among them is fixed (fewer games first on the arena board, then character id) so pages never overlap or skip. Callers are expected to cache: these are ordered reads over whole tables' worth of rows, served cheaply by an index but not free. The scene server holds the results for a short time and shares one read between every player who asks in that window. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<LeaderboardPageData>> FetchStandingAsync(LeaderboardQuery, long, CancellationToken) One character's rank and score on a board, wherever it falls. Task<DatabaseResult<LeaderboardStandingData>> FetchStandingAsync(LeaderboardQuery query, long characterId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters query LeaderboardQuery Which board. characterId long The character. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<LeaderboardStandingData>> Remarks Succeeds with Ranked false when the character is not on the board, which is an ordinary answer and not a failure.

api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IMaintenanceService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Maintenance windows: locking a set of servers, draining them, and stopping them together. public interface IMaintenanceService Remarks This service sequences the two controls that already exist; it does not reimplement them. Every server is locked and scheduled through SetShutdownAsync(long, DateTime?, CancellationToken) and SetShutdownAsync(long, DateTime?, CancellationToken), which write locked = true and shutdown_at_utc in one statement. Nothing here opens a connection to a process. What makes a window durable is that it is fully actuated when it starts. The drain is not a timer somebody has to keep running: the deadline is an absolute instant written onto each server's own row, and each server counts down to it inside its own process, warning its players as it goes. An operator can start a twenty minute drain, close their laptop, and the shard still goes down on time with the panel switched off. That is the whole reason the plan is rows. What is not automatic is the bookkeeping. AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken) is what moves an operation from Draining to ShuttingDown to Completed, and it only runs when something calls it — every read here calls it first, so the status is correct whenever anybody looks. With nothing polling, a finished window whose targets are long gone will still read "Draining" until the next person opens the page. The servers stopped on time regardless; it is the record that is late. Hosting this on a timer is one IHostedService that calls AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken) every few seconds. Cancelling does not unlock anything. CancelAsync(long, string, string, CancellationToken) clears the deadline column and nothing else, because that is all the underlying primitive does — the lock that scheduling applied stays applied. A cancelled window therefore leaves every target closed to new arrivals, and every caller has to say so, or a shard is left where nobody can log in and the cause is nowhere near where anyone will look. Methods AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken) Brings every live window up to date with what its servers' rows now say, and finishes writing any target the start did not manage to write. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> How many live windows were brought up to date. Remarks Idempotent and safe to call concurrently: it re-derives each target's status from the server's own row rather than stepping a state machine forward, so two callers racing reach the same answer. Every read on this service calls it. Concurrency rests on row locks, not on the re-derivation alone. Each target's write and the record of it are one transaction holding that target's row lock, and the derivation locks every live target before reading, so it never sees a server written but the write unrecorded. An unwritten target is failed only once ShutdownGraceSeconds past its deadline — the instant the write step itself stops trying — so a zero-second drain is not failed by a pass that runs before its first write lands. It is not what makes a shutdown happen — the servers do that from the deadline on their own rows — so a deployment with nothing calling this still takes its shards down on time. What it costs is that the record only catches up when somebody looks. CancelAsync(long, string, string, CancellationToken) Clears the scheduled shutdowns. The targets stay locked. Task<DatabaseResult<MaintenanceOperationData>> CancelAsync(long operationId, string cancelledBy, string reason, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters operationId long The window to call off. cancelledBy string The operator account cancelling it. Recorded. reason string Why. Mandatory. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<MaintenanceOperationData>> The cancelled window. Every target whose LockWrittenUtc is set is still locked, and the caller must say so. Remarks A server that has already read its deadline and begun stopping does not come back because the column was cleared; the returned notes say which targets were past that point. The clears and the record are one transaction under the targets' row locks, so a concurrent AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken) cannot write a deadline back between them: a write already in flight is cleared here, and a later one finds the target cancelled. FetchAsync(long, CancellationToken) One window, with per-target progress. Task<DatabaseResult<MaintenanceOperationData>> FetchAsync(long operationId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters operationId long The window to read. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<MaintenanceOperationData>> Remarks Advances it first, so what is returned reflects the servers as they are now. ListAsync(int, CancellationToken) Windows, newest first, each with its targets. Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<MaintenanceOperationData>>> ListAsync(int limit = 50, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters limit int How many to return. Clamped by the service. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<IReadOnlyList<MaintenanceOperationData>>> Remarks Advances every live window first, so the listing is current. StartAsync(string, string, string, int, IReadOnlyList<MaintenanceTargetRequest>, CancellationToken) Plans a window, locks every target immediately, and schedules the shutdown for the end of the drain. Task<DatabaseResult<MaintenanceOperationData>> StartAsync(string name, string startedBy, string reason, int drainSeconds, IReadOnlyList<MaintenanceTargetRequest> targets, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters name string What to call it, for the listing. startedBy string The operator account planning it. Recorded. reason string Why. Mandatory. drainSeconds int How long players get. Zero stops at the next pulse. targets IReadOnlyList<MaintenanceTargetRequest> The world and scene servers to take down. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<MaintenanceOperationData>> The planned window, with each target's outcome. Remarks The plan is committed before any server is touched, so a crash between the two leaves a visible half-written window rather than a locked shard with no record. AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken) finishes the writing on its next pass. A target that cannot be written is recorded as Failed and the rest of the window continues. Refusing the whole window because one server's row had gone would leave an operator to do the other eleven by hand, which is the thing this exists to prevent. A transient failure is not a refusal: the target stays pending, its note says why, and every AdvanceAsync(CancellationToken) retries it until ShutdownGraceSeconds past the deadline, after which it is Failed as never written. Refused outright when: the reason is empty; there are no targets; the drain is negative or beyond a day; a named server does not exist; or a named server is already inside a live window, since two plans would fight over one deadline column. Safe to retry after a lost commit: the plan carries a request key taken once per call, and an attempt that finds its own key already written returns that window rather than counting it as the live window its servers clash with.

api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IPlotService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll Reads and writes ownership of authored plots of land. public interface IPlotService Remarks Every method that changes ownership reports how many rows it affected, and the caller is expected to check it. The counts are the only way to tell a claim that succeeded from one that lost a race, and treating zero as success would sell one plot to two players. Methods BackfillTaxDueAsync(long, DateTime, CancellationToken) Gives a first due date to character-owned plots that have none. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> BackfillTaxDueAsync(long worldServerID, DateTime firstDueUtc, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerID long The world whose land to backfill. firstDueUtc DateTime When those plots should first fall due. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> How many plots were given a due date. Remarks Land claimed while tax was switched off is stored with no due date, and the sweep only looks at plots that have one. Turning tax on afterwards would therefore never touch any of it: those plots would be free forever, and the difference between a founding player and a later one would be permanent. Only rows with no date are touched, so this cannot reset a plot that is already being billed — running it repeatedly is safe, which matters because it runs on every scene resolve. Character-owned only. Guild land is deferred rather than charged until a treasury exists, so giving it a date would only make every sweep pick it up and push it along again. ChargeTaxOfflineAsync(IReadOnlyList<PlotTaxCharge>, int, DateTime, int, int, CancellationToken) Bills a batch of due plots to owners nobody is hosting, in one transaction. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotTaxChargeResult>>> ChargeTaxOfflineAsync(IReadOnlyList<PlotTaxCharge> charges, int currencyTemplateID, DateTime ownedElsewhereRetryUtc, int ledgerReason, int ledgerState, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters charges IReadOnlyList<PlotTaxCharge> One entry per plot, as the sweep read and priced them: each carries its own amount and next due date, because a bill covers every period that plot has fallen behind by. An owner may appear only once. currencyTemplateID int The attribute template tax is paid in. ownedElsewhereRetryUtc DateTime When a plot whose owner a server is holding may next be tried (stored as tax_next_attempt_utc). ledgerReason int The ledger reason recorded for each payment (CurrencyMovementReason.LandTax). ledgerState int The ledger state recorded for each payment (CurrencyMovementState.Absorbed). cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotTaxChargeResult>>> One result per distinct plot in charges. Remarks The offline charge that used to be one transaction per plot — ownership assertion, attribute read, advance, debit, lifted mark, each a round trip — as a handful of set-based statements for the whole batch. The orderings it keeps are the ones the housing README names: the bill is won before any money moves (a locked plot still holding the date the sweep read), a missed-payment mark comes off in the same commit as the payment, and an unpaid bill is marked in the commit that advanced it. A bill is paid in full or not at all. An owner is charged here only while no server holds their session, asserted under the row lock for the whole transaction, because a held owner's balance is in that server's memory and its next save would overwrite a debit made underneath it. A held owner's plot is deferred instead (OwnedElsewhere); a deleted or missing owner cannot pay and is marked like any other miss (OwnerGone), so their land reaches the end of its grace rather than staying owned forever. Never waits on a lock: a character or plot another transaction holds is skipped for this sweep. Safe to run from every scene server at once — a period produces one charge however many servers sweep it — and a retry after a lost commit reply changes nothing. Paid bills are recorded in the currency ledger inside the same commit. Nothing here marks plot_updates: a charge changes nothing another channel draws. ClearTaxDelinquencyAsync(long, CancellationToken) Clears a plot's delinquency after a successful payment. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> ClearTaxDelinquencyAsync(long plotID, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> FetchByIdsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<long>, CancellationToken) Fetches plots by ID. IDs with no row are simply absent from the result. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchByIdsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<long> plotIDs, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotIDs IReadOnlyCollection<long> cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> Remarks For the cross-channel sync, which knows exactly which plots changed and used to re-read every plot of every scene to find them. FetchByOwnerCharacterAsync(long, CancellationToken) Fetches every plot a character owns, across all scenes. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchByOwnerCharacterAsync(long characterID, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterID long cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchByOwnerGuildAsync(long, CancellationToken) Fetches every plot a guild owns, across all scenes. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchByOwnerGuildAsync(long guildID, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildID long cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchBySceneAsync(long, string, CancellationToken) Fetches every plot in one world server's copy of a scene, owned or not. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchBySceneAsync(long worldServerID, string sceneName, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerID long sceneName string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchTaxDueAsync(long, DateTime, DateTime, long, int, CancellationToken) Fetches one page of a world's owned plots whose tax has fallen due, in due order. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchTaxDueAsync(long worldServerID, DateTime asOfUtc, DateTime afterDueUtc, long afterPlotID, int limit, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerID long The world whose land to sweep. asOfUtc DateTime The moment to judge against. afterDueUtc DateTime The keyset cursor: the due date of the last plot of the previous page, or MinValue for the first page. afterPlotID long The ID of the last plot of the previous page, or zero for the first page. limit int Most rows to return. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> Remarks Bounded, because a server that has been down over a billing period comes back to every plot at once and an unbounded read would load all of them. Paged by a keyset rather than from the head, because the plots a page could not settle stay exactly where they were: a sweep that re-read from the head after each page would read them again and never reach the plots behind them. Plots whose tax_next_attempt_utc is still ahead of asOfUtc are left out — their owner is being billed by the server holding them. FetchTaxDueForOwnersAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<long>, DateTime, CancellationToken) Fetches the plots, in any world, whose tax has fallen due and whose owner is one of characterIDs. Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> FetchTaxDueForOwnersAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<long> characterIDs, DateTime asOfUtc, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterIDs IReadOnlyCollection<long> The characters the calling server holds. asOfUtc DateTime The moment to judge against. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<List<PlotData>>> Remarks The holding server's half of the sweep. A logged-in owner's balance lives in the memory of the server holding them, so only that server may charge them — and that server may be hosting nothing of the world their land is in. This asks by owner instead of by world, so where the owner happens to be playing no longer decides whether they are billed. Ignores the deferral: it exists to keep other servers from re-reading a plot that only this one can bill. At most one row per character, by the one-house index. MarkTaxDelinquentAsync(long, DateTime, CancellationToken) Records that a tax payment was missed, without disturbing an earlier miss. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> MarkTaxDelinquentAsync(long plotID, DateTime delinquentSinceUtc, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long The plot that went unpaid. delinquentSinceUtc DateTime When the first missed payment fell due. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> Remarks Only sets the mark when there is not one already. The grace period is measured from the first miss, so overwriting it on every later failure would restart the clock each period and the plot could never be reclaimed. RegisterAsync(long, string, IReadOnlyList<string>, CancellationToken) Ensures a row exists for every foundation authored in a scene. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> RegisterAsync(long worldServerID, string sceneName, IReadOnlyList<string> plotKeys, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters worldServerID long The world server whose land this is. sceneName string The scene the foundations belong to. plotKeys IReadOnlyList<string> Canonicalised keys of the foundations found in the scene. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> The number of plots that did not previously exist. Remarks Idempotent, because every scene server hosting a channel of the scene runs it on load and they all describe the same land. Plots that already exist keep the ownership they have — registration must never disturb it, or a restart would evict whoever lives there. Scoped to one world server. The same scene runs on every world, and registering it unscoped would give them all a single shared row per plot — one player's house appearing as already-owned land to everybody on every other world. ReleaseAllForGuildAsync(long, CancellationToken) Releases every plot a guild owns. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> ReleaseAllForGuildAsync(long guildID, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters guildID long cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> The number of plots released. Remarks Guilds are hard-deleted, and the owner column carries no foreign key to clean up behind them, so land held by a disbanded guild would otherwise stay claimed by an identifier that no longer resolves to anything — unclaimable, and unbuildable, permanently. ReleaseAsync(long, long, long, int, CancellationToken) Releases a plot back to the unowned pool, if the expected owner still holds it. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> ReleaseAsync(long plotID, long expectedOwnerCharacterID, long expectedOwnerGuildID, int releasedState = 0, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long The plot to release. expectedOwnerCharacterID long The character believed to own it, or zero. expectedOwnerGuildID long The guild believed to own it, or zero. releasedState int The FishMMO.Shared.PlotState the plot is left in, as its underlying integer. Defaults to Empty; reclamation passes Abandoned. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> 1 when released, 0 when somebody else owns it or it was already unowned. Remarks The state the plot lands in is the caller's to choose, because releasing is two different events wearing one name. An owner handing the deed back leaves a bare lot; a sweep taking land off somebody who stopped paying leaves a house standing empty, which renders differently and tells a passer-by a different story. TryAdvanceTaxAsync(long, DateTime, DateTime, CancellationToken) Moves a plot's tax date forward, if it still holds the date the caller charged against. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> TryAdvanceTaxAsync(long plotID, DateTime expectedDueUtc, DateTime nextDueUtc, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long The plot being charged. expectedDueUtc DateTime The due date the caller read. nextDueUtc DateTime The date the next payment falls due. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> 1 when this call advanced it, 0 when somebody else already did. Remarks The pin is what makes the tax safe to sweep from every scene server at once. Several may host the same world's scenes, they all see the same plot come due, and only the one whose expected date still matches may charge it — so a period produces one payment rather than one per server. Called before the money is taken, for the same reason a plot is claimed before it is paid for: winning the right to charge is the contended step, and a caller that loses it must not have taken anything. TryClaimAsync(long, long, long, DateTime?, int, CancellationToken) Claims an unowned plot. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> TryClaimAsync(long plotID, long ownerCharacterID, long ownerGuildID, DateTime? taxDueUtc, int claimedState = 1, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long The plot to claim. ownerCharacterID long The claiming character, or zero for a guild claim. ownerGuildID long The claiming guild, or zero for a character claim. taxDueUtc DateTime? When the first tax payment falls due, or null for untaxed land. claimedState int The FishMMO.Shared.PlotState the plot enters, as its underlying integer. Defaults to Building. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> 1 when this call took the plot; 0 when it was already owned, does not exist, or the claiming character already owns one. Remarks Exactly one of the two identifiers may be non-zero. The first tax date and the new state are set by the same statement that takes the plot, so there is no moment where land is owned but untaxed, or owned but still showing as an empty lot. Set separately, a crash in the gap would leave a plot nobody ever has to pay for, or one that every channel draws as available. A character may hold only one plot. That is asked here and enforced by a partial unique index, because this clause alone cannot stop two simultaneous claims on two scene servers. A caller that gets UNIQUE_VIOLATION back rather than a row count lost that race and should report it the same way it reports zero. TryRestoreTaxDueAsync(long, DateTime, DateTime, CancellationToken) Hands a won tax period back: moves the due date back to what it was, if it still holds the date this caller advanced it to. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> TryRestoreTaxDueAsync(long plotID, DateTime advancedToUtc, DateTime restoreToUtc, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long The plot. advancedToUtc DateTime The date TryAdvanceTaxAsync(long, DateTime, DateTime, CancellationToken) set it to. restoreToUtc DateTime The date it held before; must be earlier. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> 1 when the period was handed back, 0 when the date has moved on since. Remarks For a caller that won a period and then could not charge the owner at all (the character unreachable, the charge faulting on every attempt). Without it the period simply went unbilled: the date only ever moves forward. Pinned the same way as the advance, so it can never undo a LATER period another server has since won — that one is left alone and this returns 0. TrySetStateAsync(long, int, int, long, long, CancellationToken) Moves a plot from one lifecycle state to another, if it is still where and whose the caller thinks it is. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> TrySetStateAsync(long plotID, int expectedState, int newState, long expectedOwnerCharacterID, long expectedOwnerGuildID, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters plotID long The plot to move. expectedState int The state it must currently be in. newState int The state to move it to. Must differ from the expected one. expectedOwnerCharacterID long The character believed to own it, or zero. expectedOwnerGuildID long The guild believed to own it, or zero. cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> 1 when the plot moved, 0 when it had already moved or changed hands.

ForfeitAllAsync(long, CancellationToken) Empties a character's vault. Task<DatabaseResult<int>> RestoreEntryAsync(long characterID, int templateID, int amount, long originalPlotID, DateTime storedAtUtc, long baseFee, float feeRatePerDay, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters characterID long templateID int amount int originalPlotID long storedAtUtc DateTime baseFee long feeRatePerDay float cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> One when the row was written. Remarks The single atomic step in both retrieval and forfeiting. api/database/FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Ser.summary: Interface IQueueBoardService Namespace FishMMO.Database.Npgsql.Services.Interfaces Assembly FishMMO-DB.dll The operator's read of the two queues the shard makes players wait in, and the one write that unsticks a message. public interface IQueueBoardService Remarks A read-only service spanning two unrelated tables, separate from IEmailQueueService and IGroupFinderQueueService, for the same reason IServerBoardService is separate from the per-tier server services. Those exist to serve one process doing its job — claim the next email, form the next group — and their methods are shaped for that: DequeueNextAsync takes a row and hides it from everyone else, which is precisely what an operator looking at the queue must not do. This exists to answer "is the queue moving", which is a different question with a different shape, and folding it into them would hand a login server a method for enumerating other people's email addresses. Why the email half matters more than it looks. Account verification reaches a player through email_queue and through nothing else. If no login server is claiming rows, every new registration silently fails to complete: the site accepts the sign-up, the row is written, and the mail never arrives. Nothing anywhere raises a hand — no error is logged, because from the database's point of view nothing went wrong. The age of the oldest unclaimed row is the only signal that distinguishes that outage from a quiet Tuesday, which is why EmailQueuePage carries it and why it is computed in the same read as the counts rather than derived from the page. There is no method here that empties a queue. Not an oversight. A queue that can be cleared from a browser is how the outage above becomes invisible: the rows that prove registration is broken are the first thing somebody reaches for when the number looks alarming, and deleting them destroys both the evidence and the emails those accounts are still owed. The email half has exactly one write — RetryEmailAsync(long, CancellationToken) — and it only ever moves a row back into the queue. The group finder half has none at all: removing a queue row out from under the matching pump is how a character ends up in a party that nothing will ever transfer them into, and the safe paths for that (DeleteReturningAsync and the stale sweep) already exist on the game's own service, where the caller can deal with the consequences. Methods FetchEmailQueueAsync(EmailQueueState?, string, int, int, CancellationToken) One page of the outbound email queue, with per-state counts and the age of the oldest message nothing has picked up. Task<DatabaseResult<EmailQueuePage>> FetchEmailQueueAsync(EmailQueueState? state, string search, int page, int pageSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters state EmailQueueState? Filter to one state, or null for any. See EmailQueueState. search string Case-insensitive substring of the recipient address or the account name, or null for all. For the question "did this player's mail ever go out", which is the other reason somebody opens this page. page int 1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1. pageSize int Rows per page. Clamped by the service. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<EmailQueuePage>> Remarks The counts and the two oldest-row timestamps are computed over the whole table and are unaffected by state, search or the page: they are the alarm, and an alarm that changed when the operator narrowed a filter would be worse than none. FetchGroupFinderQueueAsync(int?, int, int, CancellationToken) One page of the group finder queue, with per-state counts. Task<DatabaseResult<GroupFinderQueuePage>> FetchGroupFinderQueueAsync(int? status, int page, int pageSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters status int? Filter by GroupFinderQueueStatus, or null for any. page int 1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1. pageSize int Rows per page. Clamped by the service. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<GroupFinderQueuePage>> Remarks Read-only, and there is no companion write. See the remarks on this interface. FetchSmsQueueAsync(EmailQueueState?, string, int, int, CancellationToken) One page of the outbound SMS queue, with per-state counts and the age of the oldest message nothing has picked up. The twin of FetchEmailQueueAsync(EmailQueueState?, string, int, int, CancellationToken). Task<DatabaseResult<SmsQueuePage>> FetchSmsQueueAsync(EmailQueueState? state, string search, int page, int pageSize, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters state EmailQueueState? Filter to one state, or null for any. search string Account-name substring, or a whole phone number. Null for all. page int 1-based page number. Values below 1 are treated as 1. pageSize int Rows per page. Clamped by the service. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<SmsQueuePage>> Remarks The counts and ages are over the whole table, as the email read's are. The body is never projected: a verification text is a one-time code. The search matches a phone number whole, never in part. The account name is a substring match as on the email board, but the number is compared after stripping spaces, dashes, dots and brackets, and only for equality. The page shows numbers masked to their last four digits; a substring search would let anyone with the page recover a masked number a digit at a time. An operator who already holds the number can still ask "did a code go to this phone". RetryEmailAsync(long, CancellationToken) Puts a claimed email back in the queue by releasing the claim on it. Task<DatabaseResult<EmailRetryResult>> RetryEmailAsync(long id, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters id long The email queue row. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<EmailRetryResult>> What happened, including a refusal. A failure result with NotFound when no such row exists. Remarks This is the only thing "retry" can mean here, and it works because of a defect. EmailQueueService.MarkFailedAsync increments attempts and records last_error but never clears claimed_at, and DequeueNextAsync only ever selects rows where claimed_at IS NULL. So a failed delivery is not retried by anything, ever, despite the entity and the interface both documenting a retry limit — the maxAttempts parameter is not read. Until that is fixed in the login server, releasing the claim from here is the only way a failed verification email is ever sent, and every row it leaves behind is an account that cannot finish registering. A row merely claimed, with no error, is retryable too. A login server that died between claiming a message and reporting on it leaves exactly that, and it is stuck just as permanently and far more quietly than a failure — nothing wrote an error, because nothing got far enough to have one. Refusing to unstick it would leave the most likely form of this outage with no remedy on the page built to surface it. What it does not do: it does not send anything — delivery is the login server's, and the row simply becomes eligible again on that server's next pass — and it does not reset attempts or clear last_error. Those are the evidence of what went wrong, and an operator pressing retry a second time needs to see that the first one came back. Two rows are refused rather than acted on, and both come back as a successful result carrying Refusal: a message already sent, and a message still unclaimed. Retrying the first would re-send mail somebody already acted on; "retrying" the second would change nothing, because it is already in line and the thing it is waiting for is a login server. Neither is a database failure, and both are worth telling the operator precisely. The read, the guard and the write are one statement, so a login server claiming the same row at the same moment produces one winner rather than a claim released out from under a delivery already in flight. RetrySmsAsync(long, CancellationToken) Puts a claimed text message back in the queue by releasing the claim on it. The twin of RetryEmailAsync(long, CancellationToken), with the same single-statement guard and the same two refusals (already sent; never claimed). Task<DatabaseResult<SmsRetryResult>> RetrySmsAsync(long id, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters id long The SMS queue row. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<DatabaseResult<SmsRetryResult>> What happened, including a refusal. A failure result with NotFound when no such row exists. Remarks SmsQueueService.MarkFailedAsync releases the claim itself while attempts remain and keeps it once they are spent, so a row that reads as failed is one the drain has given up on. Releasing it grants exactly one more attempt: attempts is not reset, so a further failure gives up again. A claimed row with no error — a drain that died mid-send — is retryable too.
