api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.ObserverStreami.summary: Class ObserverStreamingPolicy Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Tunables and pure decision functions for per-observer streaming: how far a character is visible from (scaled by local density), which observed characters a client receives at full rate, and what reduced rate the rest get. public static class ObserverStreamingPolicy Inheritance object ObserverStreamingPolicy Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Two levers, both server-side. The first is the observer range: FishNet's DistanceCondition is cloned per object, so its distance can be changed at runtime per character. It is left at the authored value by default — a crowd is bounded by VisibilityBudget, which cuts by relevance rather than by distance — but can still be shrunk with local density; see RangeScaleAtHighDensity. The second is the observer cap: of everything a client can see, only the FullRateObserverCap most relevant characters send every unreliable update; the rest are sent every Nth, with N chosen by distance. Relevance favours characters in combat, then party and guild members, then proximity. Everything here is pure and static so it can be unit-tested without a network, and so the scene server can override the numbers from its configuration at startup (ApplySetting(string, string)). Reliable sends are never rate limited — see IObserverSendFilter. Properties ByteBudget Bytes per second each viewer may spend on observed characters' unreliable updates (their transforms); 0 = no byte budget (counts and intervals alone, as before). See FitByteBudget(List<BudgetSlot>, int, int, byte). public static int ByteBudget { get; set; } Property Value int CombatWeight Relevance weight for a character currently in combat. Kept above PartyWeight + DistanceWeight so a fighter at the edge of range still outranks an idle party member standing next to the viewer. public static float CombatWeight { get; set; } Property Value float DensityRadius Radius, in metres, within which other characters count towards local density. public static float DensityRadius { get; set; } Property Value float Remarks The count is taken from a 3×3 block of cells this size — a deliberate superset of the disc, but roughly 2.9× its area, so LowDensity and HighDensity are reached by a crowd about a third as dense as their names suggest. That bias is part of why the shrink is off by default; anyone re-enabling it should calibrate against the box, not the radius. DistanceWeight Relevance weight for proximity: a character at distance 0 scores this, one at the viewer's full observer range scores 0. public static float DistanceWeight { get; set; } Property Value float EngagedFullRateBudget How many characters inside the engagement radius receive every tick. public static int EngagedFullRateBudget { get; set; } Property Value int Remarks The engagement exemption exists so lag compensation can rewind to a real tick sample, and without a budget it is unbounded: thirty players inside 40 m is thirty full-rate streams. The top entries by relevance keep every tick; the rest inside the radius fall to every second tick, which costs them a compensation accuracy of one tick — around 3 cm at walking speed, against the six ticks the distance band would otherwise have given them. EngagedOverflowInterval Interval applied to engaged characters beyond EngagedFullRateBudget. Clamped to MaxSendInterval. public static byte EngagedOverflowInterval { get; set; } Property Value byte EngagementRange Radius, in metres, inside which a character's transform is sent to an observer at FULL rate regardless of any distance or cap throttling. public static float EngagementRange { get; set; } Property Value float Remarks This is what makes lag compensation honest. A throttled transform reaches the observer every 3, 6 or 8 ticks, and the client interpolates across that gap — so what it renders is a position that existed on no server tick, and no rewind can reproduce it. Inside this radius the observer receives every tick, so the pose it saw IS a tick sample and the rewind lands exactly on it. It is a floor, not the whole rule: ResolveEngagementRange(float) widens it to cover a character's own longest ability, up to EngagementRangeCeiling. Everything beyond keeps the bandwidth saving, which is where most of it lives — exempting a 40 m disc out of a 100 m observer range leaves 84% of the observed area still throttled. With the budget in place the shrink bought no bandwidth a crowd could notice and cost the authored 100 m range: at scale 0.5 a busy town quietly became a 50 m world, then a 25 m one at the old floor, which is the culling the 2026-09-08 audit was asked to remove. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.ObserverStreami.summary: Class ObserverStreamingRegistry Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Server-side scheduler that applies ObserverStreamingPolicy to every registered character: scales each one's observer range by local density, and for every viewing client ranks what it can see and rate limits everything beyond the cap. public static class ObserverStreamingRegistry Inheritance object ObserverStreamingRegistry Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Characters register from CharacterPredictionController.OnStartServer — players, monsters, pets, and the service NPCs built on the same prefab stack — because their NetworkTransform and other per-tick traffic is what an observer's bandwidth is spent on. Static classified objects (world items, waypoints) have no such hook and are adopted by ObserverBudgetCondition on first evaluation, so that every classification can be budgeted; they cost a position read per pass and nothing on the wire. Runs one pass every RescheduleIntervalTicks ticks off FishNet.Managing.Timing.TimeManager.OnPostTick. A pass is O(entries) for density (uniform grid) plus, for ranking, each viewer against the objects in the grid cells within reach of it (the widest admitting range and the AI's declared proximity reach) and every wide-range object, with entries grouped by Unity scene so characters in different scenes never compare positions. Before the grid it was every viewer against every object: at 200 players and 700 characters, ~140k pair evaluations per half second. Fields MinimumHiddenTicks Least time, in ticks, a character the byte budget took out of view stays out before the budget may let it back in: 3 s at 30 Hz. The mirror of MinimumVisibleTicks: at the budget's edge a crowd otherwise left and came back every few seconds, and each return was a full spawn. Never applies to a pinned character (party, target, a fight) or to one within the viewer's engagement range, which come back at once. public static uint MinimumHiddenTicks Field Value uint MinimumVisibleTicks Least time, in ticks, a character the budget let in stays in view before the budget may take it out again: 5 s at 30 Hz. A crowd wandering across the budget's edge otherwise spawned and despawned its members over and over, each time a full spawn (about 350 bytes) and an attribute snapshot (about 180) to the viewer for a few seconds of view. public static uint MinimumVisibleTicks Field Value uint Properties Count Number of objects currently registered — characters and budgeted statics alike. public static int Count { get; } Property Value int LastPassBudgetExcluded (viewer, observed) pairs excluded by the visibility budget in the last pass. public static int LastPassBudgetExcluded { get; } Property Value int LastPassByteEvicted (viewer, observed) pairs the byte budget left out in the last pass. public static int LastPassByteEvicted { get; } Property Value int LastPassByteSlowed (viewer, observed) pairs the byte budget slowed in the last pass. public static int LastPassByteSlowed { get; } Property Value int LastPassLimitedPairs (viewer, observed) pairs rate limited in the last pass. public static int LastPassLimitedPairs { get; } Property Value int LastPassPinned Characters pinned into a visibility budget in the last pass. public static int LastPassPinned { get; } Property Value int LastPassRangeChanges Characters whose observer range was changed in the last pass. public static int LastPassRangeChanges { get; } Property Value int LastPassViewers Viewers ranked in the last pass. public static int LastPassViewers { get; } Property Value int LongestPassMilliseconds Longest scheduling pass since the last ResetLongestPass(), milliseconds (a diagnostic, never simulation). public static double LongestPassMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double Methods Clear() Drops every registration. For tests and server shutdown. public static void Clear() Remarks Through Detach(ObserverStreamingEntry, int) rather than Unregister(NetworkObject), which takes the object and so cannot remove an entry whose object has already been destroyed — exactly the entries a shutdown is most likely to be holding. Get(NetworkObject) Returns the entry for a registered object, or null. public static ObserverStreamingEntry Get(NetworkObject networkObject) Parameters networkObject NetworkObject Returns ObserverStreamingEntry IsViewerNearCombat(int) True when the viewer's last pass found it near combat: a target it may harm, a fight it is part of, or a character in combat within its engagement range. Refreshed every pass (RescheduleIntervalTicks). public static bool IsViewerNearCombat(int clientId) Parameters clientId int Returns bool IsWithinVisibilityBudget(int, int, bool, out bool) Whether a character is inside a viewer's visibility budget. public static bool IsWithinVisibilityBudget(int viewerClientId, int observedObjectId, bool currentlyVisible, out bool hasRanking) Parameters viewerClientId int Client id of the viewing connection. observedObjectId int Object id of the character being tested. currentlyVisible bool True when the viewer already observes it; widens the budget by the hysteresis. hasRanking bool False when this viewer has no ranking yet. Returns bool True when the character is inside the budget. Remarks The budget condition's whole implementation. hasRanking distinguishes "ranked and excluded" from "no pass has run for this viewer yet" — the caller must not treat the second as a rejection, or everything stays hidden until the first pass lands. LogSummary() Logs a one-line summary of the last pass. For diagnostics. public static void LogSummary() Register(NetworkObject, ICharacter) Registers a character. Installs the entry as the object's observer send filter. public static ObserverStreamingEntry Register(NetworkObject networkObject, ICharacter character) Parameters networkObject NetworkObject character ICharacter Returns ObserverStreamingEntry RegisterObject(NetworkObject) Registers a classified object that nothing else registered — a dropped item, a waypoint. public static ObserverStreamingEntry RegisterObject(NetworkObject networkObject) Parameters networkObject NetworkObject The object to track. Returns ObserverStreamingEntry The entry, or null when the object is not classified. Remarks These have no CharacterPredictionController to register them from, so the call comes from ObserverBudgetCondition the first time the object is evaluated: that condition runs on the server for every object carrying the manager's defaults, and it already holds the NetworkObject. The first evaluation defers (the object is unranked, which is admitted) and the next scheduling pass ranks it — the same deferral a freshly connected viewer gets, and the reason neither shows as a pop-in. Only objects that declare a ClassifiedDistanceCondition are taken. Anything else has no budget to be measured against, and registering it would cost a per-pass position read for a decision that would always be "admit". RequireViewerProximity(float) Declares the farthest nearest-player distance a reader of TryGetNearestViewerDistance(NetworkObject, out float) compares against (squared, as the AI's LOD bands are authored). Within the largest one declared, the measurement is exactly the distance to the nearest player; beyond it, it is some distance beyond it (possibly NoViewerDistance), which every such comparison reads the same way. public static void RequireViewerProximity(float sqrDistance) Parameters sqrDistance float Squared distance, metres². Infinity or NaN keeps every distance exact. Remarks Each viewer only measures the objects within this reach (and its ranking ranges) instead of every object in the scene. Until anything declares a reach the measurement is exact at every distance, as it always was. The reach only grows: a reader must declare before the object it reads is first measured (an asset's load is early enough), and nothing can take reach away from a reader that already declared. ResetLongestPass() Starts a new measurement of LongestPassMilliseconds. public static void ResetLongestPass() RunPass() Runs one scheduling pass over every registered character. Public so a server can force a pass after a bulk change (a load boundary) and so tests can drive it. public static void RunPass() TryGetNearestViewerDistance(NetworkObject, out float) Distance from networkObject to the nearest player in its scene, as measured by the last scheduling pass. public static bool TryGetNearestViewerDistance(NetworkObject networkObject, out float distance) Parameters networkObject NetworkObject The object to measure from. distance float Distance to the nearest player, or PositiveInfinity when the scene holds none. Returns bool True when a pass has measured this object. Remarks The proximity primitive server-side simulation should ask, in place of NetworkObject.Observers. Observer membership answers "who is this object being streamed to", which the visibility budget bounds — a monster outside every viewer's budget has no observers and is still standing in a crowd. This answers "how close is the nearest player", which is what a leash, a wake-up or an aggro sweep actually wants to know. False when the object is not registered, or when no pass has measured it yet. Callers must not read that as "nobody is near": it is an unanswered question, and the answer arrives within one RescheduleIntervalTicks. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.ObserverSyncMod.summary: Class ObserverSyncMode Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Decides which of the two observer synchronisation systems owns a character's state. public static class ObserverSyncMode Inheritance object ObserverSyncMode Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A character's state reaches its observers one of two ways, and exactly one of them must be active at a time: Forwarded. NetworkObject.EnableStateForwarding is on, so FishNet relays the owner's replicate input and the server's whole CharacterReconcileData to every observer, and observers simulate their peers. Exact, and expensive: measured at ~2,610 B/s per observed peer against ~409 B/s for the alternative, scaling with observers times entities. Intended for small, precision-critical scenes — an arena or a tournament match. Interpolated. Forwarding is off. The reconcile goes to the owner alone, position arrives through NetworkTransform, and each controller publishes what observers actually need through its own change-gated broadcast. This is the open-world mode. Why this type exists. The two systems overlap completely. Turning forwarding on without silencing the broadcasts does not merely pay for both — for equipment and buffs it produces conflicting writes, because the reconcile path and the broadcast path build different objects for the same slot and build items carrying different identities for the same slot. Every push site and every reconcile consumer asks this type whose turn it is, so the flag is a real switch rather than a trap for whoever flips it. The flag is read live, never cached. SetStateForwarding can flip at runtime, and every FishNet send path reads the property per send, so these helpers do too. A controller that cached the answer in OnStartNetwork would keep broadcasting into a scene that had since switched modes. Methods ObserversConsumeReconcile(NetworkObject) True when this object's observers receive — and must act on — the forwarded reconcile. public static bool ObserversConsumeReconcile(NetworkObject networkObject) Parameters networkObject NetworkObject Returns bool Remarks Used by reconcile consumers that mutate observer-visible state, so a non-owner applies reconcile data only in the mode where that data is the authority for it. In the interpolated mode the same fields arrive through a broadcast instead, and letting both write is what produces duplicate effects and phantom items. ShouldBroadcastToObservers(NetworkObject) True when this object's observers are fed by discrete broadcasts rather than by the forwarded reconcile stream. public static bool ShouldBroadcastToObservers(NetworkObject networkObject) Parameters networkObject NetworkObject Returns bool Remarks A null or unspawned object answers true. Such an object has no observers to send to, so the answer is only reached by callers that then find nothing to do — and answering false would silently disable the broadcast path for a character whose NetworkObject had not been assigned yet, which is the harder failure to notice.

(2026-10-15). Sea ice was placed as separate floating prefabs, capped at 35% cover and 600 pieces of at most 18 m: on a sea the climate froze solid, about one percent of it was ever white, and the globe drew a closed cap over a scene of open water. The pack is the ice at its real concentration; the loose pieces remain for the thin ice at its edge and the bergs. It rides the tide, as a moored boat does (FloatingBoats): each chunk's root — its collider — at the still sea level of the tick (WaterQuery), the same on the server and every client, re-placed only when the level has moved. The sea has no swell any peer shares, so the colliders do not heave; the water under the pack is calmed instead (the water's ice mask reads Floes), which is what pack ice does to a sea. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PacketCompressi.summary: Class PacketCompression Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Whole-packet compression between the game client and every server, with static Huffman codes trained on real game traffic (PacketCompressionTables). Lossless: the receiver gets exactly the bytes FishNet wrote. public static class PacketCompression Inheritance object PacketCompression Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Why a static code. Game packets are small (tens to a few hundred bytes): a general compressor has no history to work with inside one, and a shared adaptive model cannot survive unreliable, unordered delivery. A fixed code both peers already hold needs neither: each packet is compressed on its own, with nothing on the wire but its bits. Wire format. One header byte: RawPacket followed by the packet unchanged, or HuffmanPacket followed by the packet's length (a 7-bit varint) and its code bits. The sender takes whichever is shorter, so a packet never grows by more than MaximumGrowth. Switched on by the tables. Installed only when both trained tables exist, and then on every peer of the same build (client, login, world and scene servers), so the two ends always agree. Until a table has been trained from a sample (the simulate report's compression lines), nothing is installed and the wire is unchanged. Fields HuffmanPacket Header: the packet's length and its Huffman bits follow. public const byte HuffmanPacket = 1 Field Value byte MaximumGrowth The most a packet can grow by: the header byte of a raw packet. public const int MaximumGrowth = 1 Field Value int RawPacket Header: the packet follows unchanged. public const byte RawPacket = 0 Field Value byte Properties Available True when this build has trained tables, so compression is installed on every connection. public static bool Available { get; } Property Value bool ToClients The code for packets from a server to its clients, or null when untrained. public static HuffmanCode ToClients { get; } Property Value HuffmanCode ToServer The code for packets from a client to a server, or null when untrained. public static HuffmanCode ToServer { get; } Property Value HuffmanCode Methods Compress(HuffmanCode, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, Span<byte>) Compresses source into destination (header included), choosing raw when the code would not be shorter. Returns the bytes written; destination must hold source + growth. public static int Compress(HuffmanCode code, ReadOnlySpan<byte> source, Span<byte> destination) Parameters code HuffmanCode source ReadOnlySpan<byte> destination Span<byte> Returns int Decompress(HuffmanCode, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, Span<byte>) Restores a packet written by Compress(HuffmanCode, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, Span<byte>). Returns its length in destination, or -1 for a damaged or unknown packet (dropped by the caller, as a corrupt datagram would be). public static int Decompress(HuffmanCode code, ReadOnlySpan<byte> source, Span<byte> destination) Parameters code HuffmanCode source ReadOnlySpan<byte> destination Span<byte> Returns int TryInstall(NetworkManager) Installs the compression layer on a network manager that has not started yet. Does nothing (and returns false) when the build has no trained tables; true when installed now or already. public static bool TryInstall(NetworkManager networkManager) Parameters networkManager NetworkManager Returns bool VarintLength(int) Bytes a 7-bit varint of value takes. public static int VarintLength(int value) Parameters value int Returns int

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PacketCompressi.summary: Class PacketCompressionTables Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll The trained code lengths for PacketCompression: 256 values (1..15) per direction, built with BuildLengths(long[]) from a byte histogram of real traffic. The scene server's simulate report logs those histograms ("Packet compression sample") and what the code would have saved on them. public static class PacketCompressionTables Inheritance object PacketCompressionTables Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Trained 2026-11-14 on the 08:17 UTC simulate run (50 simulated players in a crowd, two real players, 60 s): 1,684 packets to clients (220,410 bytes) and 1,815 to the server (192,547 bytes). On that sample the codes shrink the bytes to 84.6% and 61.9%, before the per-packet header. Retrain from a later run's histograms when the traffic mix changes; any complete code decodes correctly, a better-fitted one only compresses more. Null means untrained: compression is not installed anywhere and the wire is unchanged. Both must be set together, and the client and every server must be deployed from the same build, since each side decodes with the table the other encoded with. Fields ToClientsLengths Code lengths for packets a server sends to its clients. public static readonly byte[] ToClientsLengths Field Value byte[] ToServerLengths Code lengths for packets a client sends to a server. public static readonly byte[] ToServerLengths Field Value byte[]

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PersistentPool..summary: Class PersistentPool Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Returns network objects to FishNet's pool somewhere a scene unload cannot destroy them. public static class PersistentPool Inheritance object PersistentPool Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks FishNet leaves a despawned object wherever it was, and a spawn moves a pooled one into its target scene, so an instance that had ever been used sat in the pool inside its world scene and died with that scene when it unloaded — while the pool, and the spawner's reservation, still counted it. The spawner's own despawns were moved out of the world scenes first (hot-path audit finding L15); a corpse with no spawner, ground loot and a container placed by script still went back to the pool in place, and every one of them was lost at the unload. Every path that returns a once-spawned object to FishNet's pool goes through Despawn(NetworkManager, NetworkObject), and every path that puts one back some other way (a spawn rolled back before it happened, a prewarm) calls Keep(NetworkManager, NetworkObject), so they share one rule for where a pooled object lives: out of every world scene, in DontDestroyOnLoad, inactive until a spawn moves it into its scene again. The callers: Despawn(NetworkManager, NetworkObject): the spawner (SpawnerRuntime.Despawn); the spawner-less fallbacks NPC.ReturnToPool and Interactable.Despawn; pets (Pet.Despawn, PetSystem.DespawnPet); a boss's adds (BossScriptState.DismissAdds); and characters (CharacterSystem.SaveAndDespawnCharacter, CharacterSystem.EvictLostCharacter, and CharacterSystem.DespawnLingeringBody for a combat-logout body). Keep(NetworkManager, NetworkObject): the spawner's prewarm (SpawnerPool.Reserve) and its rolled-back spawn (SpawnerRuntime.RollBackUnfinishedSpawn); a boss add rolled back (BossScriptState.RollBackAdd); a pooled pet object with no Pet (PetSystem.SpawnAndInitializePet); and the two character paths above (EvictLostCharacter, DespawnLingeringBody) when the object was no longer spawned. Methods Despawn(NetworkManager, NetworkObject) Despawns a spawned object into FishNet's pool and keeps it out of the world scenes. Server only. public static bool Despawn(NetworkManager networkManager, NetworkObject instance) Parameters networkManager NetworkManager The network manager owning the pool. instance NetworkObject The spawned object. Returns bool True when the object was spawned and has been despawned. Keep(NetworkManager, NetworkObject) Keeps a pooled instance out of the world scenes, so no scene's unload can destroy it. public static void Keep(NetworkManager networkManager, NetworkObject instance) Parameters networkManager NetworkManager The network manager owning the pool. instance NetworkObject The pooled instance. Remarks Call for an instance that has just gone back into FishNet's pool. It is inactive there, and a spawn moves it into its target scene again, exactly as it does an instance a prewarm made. Only for FishNet's own pool, which does not place what it stores; a custom pool keeps its objects where it chooses. Only in play mode, and only for a root object, which is all UnityEngine.Object.DontDestroyOnLoad(UnityEngine.Object) accepts. Never for a scene object: FishNet does not pool one at all — it disables it in place, to be re-enabled by its own scene — and carried out of that scene it would outlive the unload and meet its own copy when the scene loads again.

Held on the pet as well as the owner's controller so the server reads it from the creature it is commanding. public int AttackPriority Field Value int OnReadID Event triggered when a pet's owner ID is read from the network payload. public static Action<long, Pet> OnReadID Field Value Action<long, Pet> PetAbilityTemplate The template defining this pet's abilities and behavior. public PetAbilityTemplate PetAbilityTemplate Field Value PetAbilityTemplate Properties MovementOrder Whether the pet is heeling or holding position. public PetMovementOrder MovementOrder { get; set; } Property Value PetMovementOrder Remarks Owner-scoped for the same reason as Stance; see WritePayload(NetworkConnection, Writer). PersistedAttributes Attribute values restored from the database, applied at spawn. public List<PetPersistedAttribute> PersistedAttributes { get; set; } Property Value List<PetPersistedAttribute> Remarks Staged rather than applied directly for the same reason PetAbilityIDs is: the pet system fills this in before ServerManager.Spawn, and the values can only be written once OnStartServer() has built the attribute controller and rolled the prefab's own bonuses over it. See FishMMO.Shared.Pet.ApplyPersistedState(). PersistedBuffs Buffs restored from the database, applied at spawn. public List<PetPersistedBuff> PersistedBuffs { get; set; } Property Value List<PetPersistedBuff> PetAbilityIDs The list of ability template IDs that this pet has learned. The name avoids shadowing Abilities (List<AbilityTemplate>). public List<int> PetAbilityIDs { get; set; } Property Value List<int> PetOwner The character that owns this pet. public ICharacter PetOwner { get; set; } Property Value ICharacter Remarks Setting it also declares the pair to the server's threat dispatcher (through OnPetOwnerChanged), so that from then on threat against either is threat against both: hit the owner and the pet answers, hit the pet and the owner answers. Clearing it (dismissal, death, pool reset) removes the link again. Any owner qualifies; an NPC handed a pet gets the same rule. Slot Which of its owner's pet slots this pet holds, for as long as it is out; the database stores the pet under it. See PetSlotRules. The server assigns it; the owner learns it from PetAddBroadcast. public int Slot { get; set; } Property Value int Stance How willing this pet is to start a fight on its own. public PetStance Stance { get; set; } Property Value PetStance Remarks Server-authoritative, and owner-scoped: the owning client learns it from PetAddBroadcast and from PetStanceBroadcast, never from the spawn payload, and never sets it locally — so a modified client cannot put its pet into a stance the server disagrees with, and an onlooker is not told what orders somebody else's pet is under. Methods CaptureKnownAbilities() Records the abilities the pet currently knows into PetAbilityIDs so they survive a despawn / re-summon cycle. public void CaptureKnownAbilities() Remarks Called by the pet system before persisting. Without it, abilities granted at summon time from the PetAbilityTemplate were never written to the database and a re-logged pet came back empty. Despawn() Returns the pet to the pool immediately, skipping the corpse decay timer. public override void Despawn() Remarks A pet's lifetime is tied to its owner rather than to a spawner, so it skips the corpse timer and despawns through the network manager directly. ReturnToPool() routes through the spawner, which a pet does not have, so the previous implementation called it and silently did nothing. A genuine override, not the new it used to be. Method hiding only applies when the caller's static type is Pet; anything holding the pet as an NPC or an ISpawnable — which is how the spawner and several death paths see it — would silently get the NPC corpse behaviour instead, leaving the pet parked in the world as an immortal, AI-disabled corpse that nothing ever collects. Pooled out of the world scene (PersistentPool), as the NPC fallback and loot are: FishNet leaves a despawned object where it was, and a pet pooled inside an instance scene died with it when the instance unloaded, while the pool still counted it. LearnAbilities(List<int>) Records the ability template IDs this pet should know. public void LearnAbilities(List<int> abilities) Parameters abilities List<int> List of ability template IDs to learn. Remarks Only records them. Call LearnPersistedAbilities() to actually teach them to the ability controller — which is the step that was missing entirely: pet ability IDs were loaded from the database, held on this list, and saved back out without ever reaching an IAbilityController, so every pet spawned with an empty spellbook and could never attack. LearnPersistedAbilities() Teaches every template ID in PetAbilityIDs to the pet's ability controller, skipping any it already knows. public void LearnPersistedAbilities() Remarks Server-only in effect: the controller is populated authoritatively and replicated, the same way NPC teaches its inspector-configured list. OnAwake() Called when the pet is awakened. Initializes the abilities list. public override void OnAwake() OnStartServer() Server spawn. Runs after OnStartServer() has taught the prefab's own ability list, and adds anything restored from the database on top. public override void OnStartServer() Remarks This is the last point at which restored state can be written and still reach clients in the spawn payload. FishNet invokes the start callbacks during SpawnWithoutChecks and only writes each observer's payload afterwards, in the observer rebuild — so anything applied here is serialised, and anything applied after ServerManager.Spawn returns is not. ReadPayload(NetworkConnection, Reader) Reads the pet's payload from the network: the owner's character ID and nothing else. public override void ReadPayload(NetworkConnection connection, Reader reader) Parameters connection NetworkConnection The network connection. reader Reader The network reader. Remarks See WritePayload(NetworkConnection, Writer) for why the orders are not here. ResetState(bool) Resets the pet's state, clearing owner, orders, and abilities. public override void ResetState(bool asServer) Parameters asServer bool Whether the reset is performed on the server. WritePayload(NetworkConnection, Writer) Writes the pet's payload to the network: the owner's character ID. public override void WritePayload(NetworkConnection connection, Writer writer) Parameters connection NetworkConnection The network connection. writer Writer The network writer. Remarks The owner ID genuinely belongs to every observer — Client.OnPetReadId resolves it to a name for the possessive line on the pet's nameplate, which everyone sees. Stance and MovementOrder are NOT written. They are the owner's private command state and no non-owner path reads them; the owner receives both — plus AttackPriority, which was never in the payload at all — in PetAddBroadcast, which the pet system sends immediately after ServerManager.Spawn on both spawn paths (a fresh summon and the database load a relog goes through). api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PetAttackBroadc.summary: Struct PetAttackBroadcast Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Client-to-server: send the pet at the owner's target. public struct PetAttackBroadcast : IBroadcast Implements IBroadcast Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks Carries the owner's pinned and hovered targets separately, each as a NetworkObject id or 0, because the owner's attack priority (see PetAttackPriority) may try them in either order. Both are claims, not orders: the server accepts one only if it resolves to a spawned character in the owner's own scene, within MAX_TARGET_DISTANCE of the owner, and passes every pet-target rule (alive, hostile by faction, not the owner or the pet). A client can therefore point but cannot name an arbitrary entity — including one it cannot see or reach — as its pet's victim. Sent in the message rather than read from the server's copy of the target frame because that copy is rate-limited and de-duplicated on the way up, so the click can beat it by up to a report interval. The server still uses its own copy for the "current" step when the message names nothing, and the highest-threat step needs nothing from the client. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PetAttackPriori.summary: Class PetAttackPriority Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll The order a pet attack command tries its three ways of choosing a victim, packed into one int so it can ride a broadcast and a settings file. public static class PetAttackPriority Inheritance object PetAttackPriority Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Three steps, each used exactly once, tried first to last until one resolves a valid target. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PetSlotRules.ht.summary: Class PetSlotRules Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll How many pets a character may keep out, and which one a new summon replaces. Pure. public static class PetSlotRules Inheritance object PetSlotRules Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Two limits apply. A character has the pet slots its Pet Slots character attribute gives it (PetSlots: one unless an archetype, an item or a buff raises it), and each summon spell carries its own maximum (MaxPets): a spell that may raise three wolves still raises one for a character with one slot. A summon past either limit replaces the oldest pet in its way rather than failing: past the spell's limit, the oldest pet of that spell; past the slots, the oldest pet of any kind. That is what a summon did when a character could only have one pet. A pet keeps the slot it was given for as long as it is out, and the database stores each pet under its slot. A slot is not a list position: when the first of two pets dies the second stays in slot 1. Fields AttributeName The character attribute that holds a character's pet slots. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PinnedTargetRul.summary: Class PinnedTargetRules Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll The rule that decides when a pinned target is released, as arithmetic on facts about it. public static class PinnedTargetRules Inheritance object PinnedTargetRules Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A pin is a promise the frame makes to the player: "this card stays up until you let go". The only things that break the promise are the target ceasing to be something a card can describe — destroyed or despawned on this client, or dead — and the target leaving the distance inside which targeting means anything at all, and the death of the player the promise was made to. Nothing else does: not the pointer moving, not a panel opening, not the pinned character walking behind a wall. Static and free of Unity types so the truth table can be pinned by a plain unit test. TargetController gathers the facts and asks; nothing else decides. Fields RELEASE_DISTANCE Distance beyond which a pin is released, in metres. public const float RELEASE_DISTANCE = 75 Field Value float Remarks Deliberately wider than TargetController.MAX_TARGET_DISTANCE, the acquisition range. A character pinned at the edge of acquisition range and drifting a step further away would otherwise lose its card at once, and a target that is being chased is, by definition, one that is trying to get away. The gap is the hysteresis. Methods ShouldRelease(bool, bool, bool, float, float, bool) Decides whether a pinned target must be released. public static bool ShouldRelease(bool isDestroyed, bool isSpawned, bool isAlive, float sqrDistance, float releaseDistance, bool isOwnerAlive) Parameters isDestroyed bool True when the target's transform no longer exists on this client. isSpawned bool True when the target's network object is still spawned on this client. isAlive bool True when the target is alive, or has no health to lose. sqrDistance float Squared distance from the local player to the target, in metres squared. releaseDistance float The release distance, in metres; zero or less means no distance limit. isOwnerAlive bool True when the player holding the pin is alive, or has no health to lose. Returns bool True when the pin must be released.

A target's or caster's position is its feet, so a burst meant to wrap the body lifts by about a metre; a ground ring keeps 0. [Tooltip("Metres above the resolved position. A character's position is its feet: ~1 wraps the body, 0 keeps a ground ring on the ground.")] public float HeightOffset Field Value float Size The effect's size in metres, or 0 to play it at the prefab's own scale. [Tooltip("The effect's size in metres (FX are authored to a 1 m cube). 0 keeps the prefab's own scale. An area effect of radius r uses 2r.")] public float Size Field Value float Remarks Ability effects are authored to fit a one-metre cube (ParticleAdjuster, "Scale Particle System to Fit Cube"), and play in the Hierarchy scaling mode, so the instance's scale is its size: an area effect of radius r sets this to 2r and fills exactly the volume it acts on. Properties IsPresentation Purely presentational: particles and nothing else. public override bool IsPresentation { get; } Property Value bool Remarks This is the one action in the project whose whole effect is a rendered object, so it is the one action that may still run on a peer whose selector declined to resolve — see IsPresentation. Methods Execute(ICharacter, EventData) Plays the FX prefab at the collision or interaction location. public override void Execute(ICharacter initiator, EventData eventData) Parameters initiator ICharacter The character initiating the action. eventData EventData The event data containing collision or interaction information. Remarks The FX is spawned wherever TryResolveSpawnPosition(ICharacter, EventData, out Vector3) lands — the impact point a CollisionEventData carries, then the event's own target, then the ability object the event belongs to, then the initiator. It used to read Collision.contacts[0]. That threw as soon as anything dispatched a hit without a Unity collision — AbilityApplyAreaAction always did, and now every ability hit does, because AbilityObject resolves them with a swept query so they can be lag compensated. The event carries the impact point directly instead. VFX instantiation is suppressed during prediction replay ticks to prevent visual spam. The instance this creates is the action's responsibility. It is placed in the scene the effect happened in rather than the active one, and is handed to FXInstanceLifetime so that it ends whether or not its prefab knows how to end itself. Both are what the action previously left to chance; see issue #258 for what that cost, and ResolveSpawnScene(ICharacter, EventData) and FXInstanceLifetime for the two halves of it.

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlayerCharacter.summary: Class PlayerCharacter Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Represents a player-controlled character in the game world, with inventory, abilities, and networked state. Implements IPlayerCharacter and extends BaseCharacter with player-specific logic, hotkeys, and event-driven behaviour. Composition: the UnityEngine.RequireComponent attributes below are the predicted core (attributes, targeting, cooldowns, items, abilities, buffs, damage, prediction) and its visuals, which stay in the core until prediction goes through Core components (Phase 6 of the core and modules plan). It is derived rather than stored because a name is not identity: RaceID is, and a name travelling separately from the id it describes is a name that can disagree with it. The template is a cache entry that ID names, so this resolves rather than holds — there is no second copy to fall out of step with RaceID. Not to be confused with IFactionController.RaceTemplate. That is a SEPARATE holding with its own id, deliberately overridable per spawn (NPCSpawnableSettings.FactionOverride → SetRaceTemplateOnSpawn) so one NPC prefab can answer for several factions. Remarks Two shapes behind a shape byte, chosen by the receiver, in the same style as the ability, buff, attribute and waypoint controllers. Everything an observer needs to DRAW a peer is unconditional; the three fields that describe where that peer is and what it is allowed to do are the owner's alone. SceneName and InstanceSceneName are read only through CurrentSceneName(), and the only client that calls it calls it on the LOCAL character (ClientMapSystem). Every observer of every peer was being sent two scene-name strings it had no reader for — and an observer is by definition already in that scene. AccessLevel has no client reader at all: the only thing that tests it is ChatHelper.TryParseCommand, whose sole caller is the server's chat system. Sending it told every observer which characters were game masters, for a byte nobody spent. RaceName used to travel here and is gone entirely. It was never assigned anywhere in the tree, so the wire value was always null, and a race name is derivable from RaceID through the template cache — which is exactly what the guild UI already does.

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotAccess.html.summary: Class PlotAccess Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Who may do what on a plot, resolved from its state, its owner, and the grants on it. public static class PlotAccess Inheritance object PlotAccess Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks One place, and a pure function, because this answer is needed in several that must agree. The server decides whether a placement is written and whether a body is pushed back out of a doorway; the client greys out the buttons it knows will be refused. If those disagreed the player would be shown a door they cannot walk through, which reads as the game being broken rather than as the house being locked. Locked by default is the rule this encodes. A plot admits its owner, and admits everybody the owner has explicitly named; it admits nobody else, and neither an unclaimed grant row nor an unrecognised permission bit can widen that. Methods AllowsEntry(PlotState, PlotOwner, long, long, PlotPermission) True when a character may cross into the plot. public static bool AllowsEntry(PlotState state, PlotOwner owner, long characterID, long characterGuildID, PlotPermission granted) Parameters state PlotState owner PlotOwner characterID long characterGuildID long granted PlotPermission Returns bool ClampGrant(PlotPermission, PlotPermission) What a character with InviteFriends is actually able to hand out. public static PlotPermission ClampGrant(PlotPermission granterHolds, PlotPermission requested) Parameters granterHolds PlotPermission What the character doing the granting holds themselves. requested PlotPermission What they are trying to give. Returns PlotPermission Remarks Nobody may grant a permission they do not hold. Without this the whole model collapses to its weakest link: a friend given only Enter and InviteFriends could grant themselves — or a stranger — the right to strip the house, and the owner's careful choice of what to trust them with would have meant nothing. An owner passes All and is therefore unclamped, which is the intended asymmetry: the owner is the source of the authority, not a holder of it. IsOwner(PlotOwner, long, long) True when a character is the plot's owner, personally or through their guild. public static bool IsOwner(PlotOwner owner, long characterID, long characterGuildID) Parameters owner PlotOwner Who holds the plot. characterID long The character asking. characterGuildID long Their guild, or zero when they are in none. Returns bool Remarks Guild membership is passed in rather than looked up, so this stays a function of its arguments and can be reasoned about — and tested — without a guild system to hand. A character with no guild can never match a guild-owned plot, which is why the zero case is rejected explicitly rather than left to compare equal to an unset owner column. Resolve(PlotState, PlotOwner, long, long, PlotPermission) Everything a character may do on a plot right now. public static PlotPermission Resolve(PlotState state, PlotOwner owner, long characterID, long characterGuildID, PlotPermission granted) Parameters state PlotState The plot's lifecycle state. owner PlotOwner Who holds it. characterID long The character asking. characterGuildID long Their guild, or zero. granted PlotPermission What the plot's access list gives them, if anything. Returns PlotPermission Remarks State is consulted before ownership, because two of the four states answer the same way for everybody. An abandoned plot admits nobody at all — there is no owner left to admit them and nothing standing on it to enter — and an empty lot is a piece of the public world that happens to be for sale, so people may walk across it and nothing more. A grant is only honoured on an Occupied plot. Rows outlive the ownership that created them: a plot reclaimed for unpaid tax and bought by somebody else must not come with the previous owner's friends still holding keys, and clearing those rows is a write that can fail or be interrupted. Ignoring them outside the one state where they apply makes that cleanup a tidiness matter rather than a security one. Sanitize(PlotPermission) Cleans a stored or received permission mask down to bits that mean something. public static PlotPermission Sanitize(PlotPermission permissions) Parameters permissions PlotPermission Returns PlotPermission Remarks Applied to everything crossing a boundary — a row read back, a request from a client — so an unknown bit is dropped at the edge rather than stored and later reinterpreted. A permission retired in a later version then stops meaning anything, instead of quietly becoming whichever permission is given its bit next. Sanitize(int) Cleans a stored or received permission mask down to bits that mean something. public static PlotPermission Sanitize(int mask) Parameters mask int Returns PlotPermission Remarks Applied to everything crossing a boundary — a row read back, a request from a client — so an unknown bit is dropped at the edge rather than stored and later reinterpreted. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotFoundation..summary: Class PlotFoundation.Registry Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Every foundation currently alive, grouped by the loaded scene it belongs to. public static class PlotFoundation.Registry Inheritance object PlotFoundation.Registry Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Keyed by the scene manager's handle, which identifies one loaded copy of a scene inside this process. Scene name alone will not do: a scene server may host scenes for several world servers at once, and each world's copy is its own land with its own owners. The handle is what the housing system resolves back to a world server. The handle is a process-local identifier and is never persisted or sent anywhere — see ISceneInstanceDetails.Handle. It is used here only to group objects that are alive in this process right now. Properties Scenes Every loaded scene that currently has at least one foundation. public static IReadOnlyCollection<SceneHandle> Scenes { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyCollection<SceneHandle> Methods ForPlot(long) Every live copy of one plot, across every loaded channel. public static List<PlotFoundation> ForPlot(long plotID) Parameters plotID long Returns List<PlotFoundation> Remarks Deliberately plural. Channels are several loaded copies of the same scene, and a plot is one row shared between all of them — so a grant, a revocation or a change of state arrives naming a plot and has to reach every copy. Applying it to the first match would leave the same house locked in one channel and open in the next. A linear walk, because the count is small: this is the foundations authored into the scenes one server happens to be hosting, not the world's land. Indexing them by plot ID would mean an index that has to be maintained through resolution, re-resolution and scene unload for a lookup that runs when somebody changes a permission. everything else about it — who owns it, whether it can be claimed at all — is resolved by the server against the database and pushed back here. Nothing about ownership is decided locally. Foundations announce themselves through PlotFoundation.Registry rather than being discovered by a scene sweep, because a sweep would have to know when a scene had finished loading and would find nothing in an additively-loaded one that arrives later. Fields DefaultHeight Height used when none is authored, in metres. public const float DefaultHeight = 12 Field Value float DefaultSize Footprint used when none is authored, in metres. public const float DefaultSize = 16 Field Value float Remarks A placeholder, not a recommendation. Returns bool Remarks Two gates, and both have to pass. The first is the standing rule — the state of the plot and whatever the owner has granted. The second is the live build session: a plot being edited is closed even to people who normally hold a key, because the ground is moving under them and a visitor standing in it is a visitor inside a wall that was not there a moment ago. The session gate is deliberately narrower than the state one. An owner may end a session without leaving Building, and their friends should not be let in the instant they stop placing things — the house is still a building site. Access that has not loaded yet admits nobody but the owner. The alternative is admitting everybody for the seconds between a scene loading and its grants arriving, and an access rule that is off during startup is an access rule a player can wait out. Remarks A no-op before the list has loaded. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotIdentity.ht.summary: Struct PlotIdentity Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll What identifies a plot of land: the scene it belongs to, and a key authored on it. public readonly struct PlotIdentity : IEquatable<PlotIdentity> Implements IEquatable<PlotIdentity> Inherited Members object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A plot is a foundation area placed in a scene by a designer, so its geometry is part of the scene asset and never needs to be stored or synchronised. Only ownership is persisted, which leaves the question of what a stored row points at. It cannot be a scene object identifier. Those are handed out fresh on every scene load and are explicitly never persisted, so a row keyed by one would attach to a different foundation after a restart. It cannot be a scene instance either: channels are several live copies of the same scene, and a plot is meant to look the same in all of them. What is left is the scene's name plus a key the designer writes on the foundation, which is stable across reloads, identical on every scene server in the cluster, and readable in a log line. Keys are canonicalised on the way in rather than stored as typed. Guild names take the opposite approach — stored as entered, with a lowercase computed column beside them — because a guild name is shown to players and has to survive round-tripping intact. A plot key is a developer-facing identifier that is never displayed, so there is no reason to keep two forms of it, and one canonical form is what stops Riverside_01 and riverside_01 from becoming two plots that look like one. Nothing in the schema enforces that — the codebase has no check constraints, and neither column can carry a foreign key because both use zero to mean "none" — so the invariant is held here instead, in a type that cannot represent a plot owned by a character and a guild at once. Rows are read back through TryFromColumns(long, long, out PlotOwner) rather than a constructor, so a row that does somehow hold both is refused at the boundary instead of being resolved by whichever column the reader happened to check first. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotOwnerType.h.summary: Enum PlotOwnerType Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll What kind of holder owns a plot. public enum PlotOwnerType Fields Character = 1 An individual character owns the plot. Guild = 2 A guild owns the plot. Unowned = 0 Nobody owns the plot. It is available to claim. Remarks The discriminator for PlotOwner. It is not itself a column: the plot row stores an owning character and an owning guild in separate columns so that "every plot this guild owns" is an indexed lookup rather than a scan filtered by a type tag. This enum is how game code reads that pair back as a single answer. Values are explicit because they reach clients as part of plot state, and a renumbering would silently change what an already-built client displays.

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotPermission..title: Enum PlotPermission | FishMMO Documentation
api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotPermission..summary: Enum PlotPermission Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll What somebody who is not the owner may do on a plot. [Flags] public enum PlotPermission Fields All = Enter | PlaceItems | RemoveItems | InviteFriends Every permission that may be granted. The mask unknown bits are cleaned against, so a client that invents a flag cannot store one and a permission removed in a later version stops meaning anything rather than silently becoming whatever now occupies its bit. Enter = 1 May pass through the plot's boundary and into the house. InviteFriends = 8 May grant other players access. Never lets a friend grant more than they hold themselves — see ClampGrant(PlotPermission, PlotPermission). Otherwise the weakest permission on the list is the only one that matters, because whoever holds it can hand themselves the rest. None = 0 No access at all. What a stranger has, and what a revoked friend goes back to. PlaceItems = 2 May place structures and decorations. RemoveItems = 4 May take structures and decorations away again. Deliberately separate from PlaceItems, and the more dangerous of the two: removal is what destroys work, and what sends things to the owner's vault where they cost money to get back. A friend helping decorate needs one; only a trusted one needs both. Remarks Flags rather than a rank, because these are not ordered. Trusting a friend to redecorate is not a superset of trusting them to bring other people round, and a server that forced them onto one scale would make every grant a choice between too little and too much. The owner is never represented here. Ownership is not a grant — it cannot be revoked by an access row, and a plot whose owner appeared in its own access list would be one bad delete away from a house its owner could not enter. PlotAccess answers for the owner separately. Stored as an integer bitmask, so the values must not be renumbered.

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotState.html.title: Enum PlotState | FishMMO Documentation
api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PlotState.html.summary: Enum PlotState Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Where a plot is in its lifecycle. public enum PlotState Extension Methods PlotStateExtensions.IsClaimable(PlotState) PlotStateExtensions.IsHeld(PlotState) Fields Abandoned = 3 Unpaid past its grace period. Unowned, closed, and claimable. The owner has been cleared and everything that was built has gone to their vault, but the lot is not Empty: it renders as an abandoned house rather than bare ground until somebody claims it. Nobody may enter one — there is no owner to admit them, and the structures that made it enterable are gone. Building = 1 Claimed, with the house going up. Closed to everybody but the owner. A plot enters this the moment it is claimed and leaves it when the owner says the house is finished. It is deliberately a persisted phase rather than the in-memory build session: the session is one person standing there with the editor open, and it ends when they walk away, whereas this survives their logging out and every channel shows it. Empty = 0 No owner and nothing built. Available to claim. Occupied = 2 Built, paid up, and open to the owner and whoever they have let in. Remarks Ownership alone cannot answer this. "Nobody owns this" covers both land that has never been claimed and land somebody lost, and those are not the same place: one is a bare lot and the other is a house whose owner stopped paying, standing empty with its contents in a vault. A channel loading the scene has to render them differently, and a player walking up to one has to be told a different thing. Persisted on the plot row rather than derived, because it is the thing channels agree on. Channels are ephemeral copies of a scene that hold no world state of their own, so a state each one recomputed from whatever it happened to have loaded would be a state that differed between them. Values are explicit and must not be renumbered: they are stored, and they reach clients as part of plot state.

api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PointOfInterest.summary: Class PointOfInterestOutline Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll A site's footprint seen from above (2026-10-18: "Towns, cities and all other points of interest need different carving besides just circles"): how far its ground reaches from its anchor toward each of a ring of evenly spaced bearings, the first due north (+z), turning east (+x) as a yaw does. Between two bearings its edge runs straight, so the footprint is a star-shaped polygon: every point of it is seen from the anchor, and a ray from the anchor leaves it exactly once. public static class PointOfInterestOutline Inheritance object PointOfInterestOutline Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks One footprint, read by everything. The pad's levelling, the keep-outs, the ways' owner marks and carve, the layout's boundary, the walls, the moat, the fields round a town and its region all read the same outline. The site's radius stays its bounding reach (no point of the outline is farther), so spacing and culling by radius still hold. An empty outline is a circle of the radius it is read with: every site planned before outlines (and every kind that keeps a disc, a bridge or a mill on its bank) reads exactly as it did. Terraced, each level is cut and filled only by the fall across its own band, and the town climbs the hill as old hill towns do. The levels are bands across TerraceAxis (up the hill), split at TerraceSteps (metres along it from the pad's centre). api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PortalActivatio.summary: Class PortalActivationRules Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll The portal activation rules as pure functions: scope × conditions × stored state → what a use of the portal does. PortalGate is the only caller in the game; tests drive these directly. public static class PortalActivationRules Inheritance object PortalActivationRules Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Unknown is not closed. A server that has not yet read a character's (or a scene's) activations from the database answers null for "is it open", and the verdict for that is NotReady, a refusal that changes nothing. Treating it as closed would let a player who already opened a portal open it again, and a portal that spends its key would take a second key for it. Requirements are any-of. One passing condition opens the portal; the key is one more alternative, tried after the conditions so a player who qualifies some other way keeps the key. A portal with no conditions and no key opens for the first player who uses it — a generated portal ships that way until a designer assigns its requirements. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PortalActivatio.summary: Class PortalActivationStore Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll The portal activations a process knows: each character's own (bit sets per scene, the waypoint shape) and the world's (one PortalWorldState per scene and index), with what the database has and has not confirmed. public sealed class PortalActivationStore Inheritance object PortalActivationStore Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Plain data, no I/O. The scene server's interactable system owns the live store, fills it from the database (RestoreCharacterPage(long, string, int, ulong), RestoreWorldScene(string, IReadOnlyList<(int Index, PortalWorldState State)>)) and drains what is dirty into it; PortalGate reads and writes it through Current. Until a server installs one, Current is a store that treats every record as loaded and keeps them in memory only — so a portal behaves the same in a harness or a sim, it just forgets on restart. Loaded is tracked separately from empty. A character with no rows and a character not read yet both have no bits; only the first may be answered "closed" (see PortalActivationRules). Likewise per scene for world rows. Persistence without versions. Character bits reuse WaypointUnlockMask: set-only bits whose database merge is an OR, so dirty is activated & ~persisted and a bit set while a write is in flight stays dirty on its own. World openings are tracked by Covers(PortalWorldState): a confirmation clears the mark only if what was written covers what is held now. A released character whose bits are still unconfirmed keeps its entry, unloaded, until a write confirms them; a reload ORs the database rows back in. Record keys. A per-character record is keyed by a string that is the scene name for portals, and the scene name plus KeySuffix for the sites a character has discovered: the same bit pages, persisted by the same rows. Main thread only. api/unity/FishMMO.Shared.PredictedAbilit.summary: Class PredictedAbilityStateHistory Namespace FishMMO.Shared Assembly FishMMO.Shared.dll Per-tick record of what the owning client predicted for its ability controller, so a reconcile can be compared against the client's state at the reconcile tick rather than against whatever the client holds now. public sealed class PredictedAbilityStateHistory Inheritance object PredictedAbilityStateHistory Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks FishNet only applies a reconcile once its tick is at least stateInterpolation + 1 ticks behind the client's local tick, and the client has already simulated every tick in between. The server's seed and ability ID in that reconcile therefore describe an older tick than the client's live currentSeed / currentAbilityID. Comparing the two directly declared a "mismatch" on every cast — the client had advanced its seed for a cast the server had not yet processed — which destroyed every owner-predicted projectile about one tick after it spawned and cleared the cast bar on every reconcile for the first RTT of every timed cast. Recording the predicted state per tick and looking up the entry for the reconcile's own tick makes the comparison like-for-like: a real misprediction is one where the client's simulation of tick T produced a different seed than the server's simulation of tick T. Fixed-size ring indexed by tick & (capacity - 1); each slot stores the tick it holds so a stale slot is never mistaken for the requested tick. Capacity must be a power of two and comfortably larger than the client's look-ahead (a few ticks) plus a full reconcile window; 128 ticks is over four seconds at 30 Hz. Constructors PredictedAbilityStateHistory(int) Creates a history ring. public PredictedAbilityStateHistory(int capacity = 128) Parameters capacity int Number of ticks retained. Rounded up to a power of two, minimum 2. Fields DefaultCapacity Default ring capacity, in ticks. Must be a power of two. public const int DefaultCapacity = 128 Field Value int Properties Capacity Ring capacity in ticks. public int Capacity { get; } Property Value int Methods Clear() Forgets every recorded tick. public void Clear() Record(uint, int, long) Records the state the client holds after simulating tick. Overwrites any earlier record for the same tick (replays re-simulate a tick and the later simulation is the one a subsequent reconcile should be compared with). public void Record(uint tick, int seed, long abilityID) Parameters tick uint seed int abilityID long TryGet(uint, out int, out long) Returns the recorded state for tick, if it is still in the ring. public bool TryGet(uint tick, out int seed, out long abilityID) Parameters tick uint seed int abilityID long Returns bool
