MerchantTemplate MoveAxisCompression Packs a movement input axis into a single signed byte, and exposes the quantisation so a producer can commit to the value it is about to send. MovementModeBits Bits of Mode. NPC Represents a non-player character (NPC) in the game. Handles attribute generation, network payloads, and spawning logic. NPCAttribute Represents an attribute for an NPC, with options for scaling, randomization, and value range. Used to define how an NPC's attribute is calculated and applied from a template. NPCAttributeDatabase ScriptableObject database for storing and retrieving NPC attributes by name. NPCGuildTemplate ScriptableObject template for defining NPC guilds, their icon, description, archetypes, and requirements. NPCLookAtInteractorAction ECA action that makes an NPC face the interacting player and transition to idle state. Add this to any NPC's OnInteractTriggers alongside the primary interaction action (e.g., SendMerchantBroadcastAction) to achieve the classic "NPC turns to greet the player" behaviour. NamedSceneObjectTargetSelector Resolves a scene UnityEngine.GameObject by name at runtime. Designed for asset-based Triggers that need to point at a specific scene object — selectors serialized on ScriptableObject assets cannot hold direct scene references, but they can hold a name string and look the object up when the trigger fires. The lookup is scoped to the context's scene (whatever scene the event's Target or Initiator lives in). If no scene context is available, the active scene is used. Names are compared exactly (case sensitive). For non-unique names, use TaggedSceneObjectTargetSelector instead, or compose this selector with per-target conditions to disambiguate. Performance: the lookup walks the scene's root objects and their descendants on every fire. For frequent triggers, cache the resolved GameObject in your scene wiring rather than depending on a name lookup. NearestTargetSelector Selects the nearest UnityEngine.GameObject to the context within a given radius and layer mask. Useful for targeting the closest enemy, ally, or object. NetHelper A static utility class providing network-related helper methods, such as fetching the external IP address and validating loopback addresses. IP address and hostname validation is delegated to the IsAddressValid(string) method. NetworkSendSchedule How often each side flushes its outgoing network data, while the simulation keeps ticking at the full tick rate: with an interval of 2, every packet carries two ticks of messages, so there are half as many packets and half the per-packet transport cost (IP, UDP and QUIC headers, which at ~58 B a packet were over half of a player's traffic). NetworkTransformDistanceLod Rate limits a FishNet.Component.Transforming.NetworkTransform's unreliable updates per observer by how far that observer is from the object, so a spectator across the zone stops paying full rate for something it can barely see while a spectator standing next to it still gets every tick. NpcCorpseModule NPC corpse decay as a module: on the server, a dead NPC's body stays for its decay time (less once it is empty) and then returns to its pool. Removing this module's declaration sends corpses back to the per-NPC tick they used before. ObservedMotion What a client reads off a character it only watches: whether it swims or climbs, from where it is. Another player's movement never runs on this client (state forwarding is off; its NetworkTransform places it) and an NPC's runs only on the server, so nothing tells this client what they are doing. Their body is animated from what can be seen instead, with the movement's own thresholds, so a watched swimmer swims where the swimmer itself does. ObserverBroadcastScope Sends a broadcast to everyone observing a character except its owner. ObserverBudgetCondition Caps how many CHARACTERS one client observes at a time, keeping the most relevant. ObserverProximityGrid A uniform horizontal grid over one scene's registered objects, so ranking a viewer reads only the objects that could be within reach of it instead of every object in the scene. ObserverStreamingEntry One registered character in ObserverStreamingRegistry: the per-observer send intervals the scheduler assigned it, the range it is currently visible from, and the cached relevance inputs (combat, party, guild) used to rank it for each viewer. ObserverStreamingPolicy Tunables and pure decision functions for per-observer streaming: how far a character is visible from (scaled by local density), which observed characters a client receives at full rate, and what reduced rate the rest get. ObserverStreamingRegistry Server-side scheduler that applies ObserverStreamingPolicy to every registered character: scales each one's observer range by local density, and for every viewing client ranks what it can see and rate limits everything beyond the cap. ObserverSyncMode Decides which of the two observer synchronisation systems owns a character's state. OpenPlotPanelAction ECA action on a plot's deed post: asks the server to describe the plot to the player who walked up to it. Server-only. PackIce A cold sea's pack ice: a mosaic of floes laid at the concentration the climate gives, merged into chunks whose colliders the server keeps and players walk on, riding the tide. Open leads run through it so a boat can always cross. Cut with the scene (IcePlacer); nothing about it is random at runtime. PacketCompression Whole-packet compression between the game client and every server, with static Huffman codes trained on real game traffic (PacketCompressionTables). Lossless: the receiver gets exactly the bytes FishNet wrote. PacketCompressionLayer The FishNet intermediate layer that applies PacketCompression to every packet both ways. Added by TryInstall(NetworkManager); never placed in a scene. PacketCompressionTables The trained code lengths for PacketCompression: 256 values (1..15) per direction, built with BuildLengths(long[]) from a byte histogram of real traffic. The scene server's simulate report logs those histograms ("Packet compression sample") and what the code would have saved on them. ParticleAdjuster Utility MonoBehaviour for adjusting and visualizing particle system shapes in the editor. PayloadVisibility Answers "is this spawn payload being written for the character's owner?" for the controllers that filter what non-owners receive. PendingSpawnerContent Marks a generated spawner the generator left empty ON PURPOSE, for a designer to fill: a world boss lair's boss (2026-10-10: the designer assigns the boss), or a role no NPC exists for yet. PercentageBonusFormulaTemplate PersistentPool Returns network objects to FishNet's pool somewhere a scene unload cannot destroy them. Pet Represents a pet NPC, including owner, abilities, orders, and network payload logic. PetAbilityTemplate ScriptableObject template for defining a pet ability, including prefab and spawn parameters. PetAttackPriority The order a pet attack command tries its three ways of choosing a victim, packed into one int so it can ride a broadcast and a settings file. PetController Controller for managing pet entities attached to a character. Handles pet state, network broadcasts, and event invocation. PetEventData ECA event data for pet summon and dismiss events. PetSlotRules How many pets a character may keep out, and which one a new summon replaces. Pure. PickupWorldItemAction ECA action that handles picking up a world item. Validates the item, applies a per-object concurrency guard to prevent duplicate pickups, creates the item, invokes OnGrantItem to grant it to the player's inventory and persist it to the database, and manages world-item state. Server-only. PinnedTargetRules The rule that decides when a pinned target is released, as arithmetic on facts about it. PlatformWork CPU field preparation: managed workers on native players, serial execution on single-threaded Web. PlayFXAction Action that plays a visual effect (FX) at a determined position, typically at the point of collision or interaction. PlayRegionAudioAction ECA action that triggers audio playback when a character enters a region. Client-only: suppressed on server and during prediction reconciliation. PlayerCharacter Represents a player-controlled character in the game world, with inventory, abilities, and networked state. Implements IPlayerCharacter and extends BaseCharacter with player-specific logic, hotkeys, and event-driven behaviour. Composition: the UnityEngine.RequireComponent attributes below are the predicted core (attributes, targeting, cooldowns, items, abilities, buffs, damage, prediction) and its visuals, which stay in the core until prediction goes through Core components (Phase 6 of the core and modules plan). Module features are not listed here: friends, party, guild, factions, waypoints, quests and archetypes are character parts their modules add at wake ([assembly: CharacterPart]), so a removed module leaves no component behind. PlayerInteractionEventData Event data for player interactions, such as talking to NPCs or interacting with objects. Carries the interactable that was triggered so ECA actions can cast it to the specific type. PlotAccess Who may do what on a plot, resolved from its state, its owner, and the grants on it. PlotFoundation A claimable area of land, authored into a scene by a designer. PlotFoundation.Registry Every foundation currently alive, grouped by the loaded scene it belongs to. PlotFoundationMesh Builds a plot's look as one mesh with four submeshes: wood, rope, stone, board. PlotFoundationVisual The look of a housing plot: its deed post, the staked rope round an empty lot, a builder's scaffold while it is a building site, a stone footing once it is a home, and a leaning post over bare stakes when it has been abandoned. Client only; built from the plot's own size. PlotStateExtensions Convenience tests over PlotState. PlotStructureTemplate A thing a player can build on a plot. PointOfInterestDiscovery Marks a point of interest's Region as discoverable: entering it the first time counts the site once for the character (DiscoverSiteAction). PointOfInterestKindOverride One kind's budget, changed from the catalogue's for one scene. Negative = keep the catalogue's. PointOfInterestKinds The point-of-interest kinds: their group, traits, map tier, display name and map marker type. PointOfInterestOutline A site's footprint seen from above (2026-10-18: "Towns, cities and all other points of interest need different carving besides just circles"): how far its ground reaches from its anchor toward each of a ring of evenly spaced bearings, the first due north (+z), turning east (+x) as a yaw does. Between two bearings its edge runs straight, so the footprint is a star-shaped polygon: every point of it is seen from the anchor, and a ray from the anchor leaves it exactly once. PointOfInterestRecord One generated point of interest: what it is, where, what it is called and what it links to. PointOfInterestSettings One scene's point-of-interest choices: asked before every cut (2026-10-10) and editable afterwards. PointOfInterestShape What a terrain shaper (a carved cave, an overhang, an arch) decided for one site when the scene was planned: kept with the plan so a repaint can build the same mesh again without planning (or carving) twice. PointOfInterestTerraces A pad's terraces (2026-10-18: hill towns): its ground levelled not to one height but to two to four, stepped up the fall line like a hillside's fields, with an earth bank between each pair and a ramp up every bank where a street climbs. PortalActivation Makes a portal — a same-scene Teleporter or a cross-scene SceneTeleporter — dormant until something activates it. PortalActivationRules The portal activation rules as pure functions: scope × conditions × stored state → what a use of the portal does. PortalGate is the only caller in the game; tests drive these directly. PortalActivationStore The portal activations a process knows: each character's own (bit sets per scene, the waypoint shape) and the world's (one PortalWorldState per scene and index), with what the database has and has not confirmed. PortalClientStates The local player's view of which portals are open, per scene, as the server last reported it. PortalGate The one place a portal use is decided: open → travel; closed and the player qualifies → activate, then travel; otherwise refuse with a toast. Server only. PortalRegistry The live portals in every loaded scene, by Unity scene handle and authored portal index. PortalSurface The face of a scene teleporter: a quad in its opening that shows the place it leads to. Both scenes cannot be loaded at once, so the view is a cubemap baked at the destination (PortalViewBaker, kept in Assets/Generated and shipped in a build-only Addressables group), looked up through the quad by view direction in the FishMMO/Portal shader: a window onto the far side with the right perspective for anything past a few metres, a swirl and a glowing rim over it. With no baked view (an editor that has not baked, a destination not yet set) only the glow shows. PredictedAbilityStateHistory Per-tick record of what the owning client predicted for its ability controller, so a reconcile can be compared against the client's state at the reconcile tick rather than against whatever the client holds now. PredictedCombatEvents Tracks combat numbers a client has drawn from its OWN predicted hits, and reconciles them against the server's combat report. PredictedRushStops The owner's memory of the rush stops its predicted hits made, by the movement tick each followed, so a replay can make them again (see EndMotionFromHit()). Pure bookkeeping, no motor. PredictionHealth The client's own prediction health over the last minute: how often the server corrected its movement by more than a centimetre, and what share of the hits it predicted the server rejected. Shown in the network overlay; the numbers every prediction fix is measured by. PremadeAbilityTemplate A complete, ready-to-use ability a merchant sells: a base AbilityTemplate with its events already chosen, at a price of its own. PropChunkLedger Which of one scene's prop collision chunks are wanted, kept by reference count: every focus point holds the chunks round the 32 m cell it stands in, and a chunk is wanted while any focus holds it. The bookkeeping half of PropColliderStreamer, with no Unity objects in it, so it is testable on its own. PropChunkLedger.Hold One focus's hold on this ledger's scene: the chunks it keeps wanted, and the cell it was placed in. PropColliderStreamer Puts a scene's baked prop collision into physics only where something can touch it: within ServerRadius of every character on the server, and within ClientRadius of the camera on the client. A chunk (CellMetres square) at a time, as one mesh: every collidable prop in it merged and cooked off the main thread, then handed to one static collider. RaceTemplate ScriptableObject template for a race: models, attributes, starting abilities, inventory and equipment for playable races, and the naming data the name generator draws on for every race. A race with Playable off exists only to name things — it has no prefab or models, is skipped by character creation, and loads no placeholder model. RandomRangeFloatValue Float value provider that returns a random float between Min and Max (inclusive). Uses the deterministic DeterministicRNG from RNG when available, otherwise falls back to Shared. RandomRangeValue Value provider that returns a random integer between Min and Max (inclusive). Uses the deterministic DeterministicRNG from RNG when available, otherwise falls back to Shared. RandomTargetSelector Selects a random UnityEngine.GameObject from all within a given radius and layer mask. Useful for random targeting effects or abilities. Region Represents a networked region in the game world. Handles region hierarchy, collider setup, and triggers region actions on player entry, stay, and exit. Membership is tracked locally in a RegionMembership<T> rather than trusting the NetworkCollider callbacks one-for-one: FishNet re-polls colliders during prediction reconcile replay (and we deliberately fire nothing while a character teleports), so callbacks that arrive while suppressed are recorded only and the resulting Enter/Exit is raised exactly once on the next non-reconciling post-tick via a raw-vs-effective diff. Stay never fires during replay. Hierarchy: a child region takes ownership of a character standing inside it. Every ancestor receives a paired Exit only if it had raised an Enter, and a parent re-Enters when the last child releases the character while it is still physically inside the parent. Parent Stay is suppressed while any descendant owns the character. RegionActionGate Authority gate for region actions that mutate gameplay state (buffs, attributes). The server is authoritative for gameplay; clients only observe the result through the normal replication/reconcile path, so these actions must never run on a client peer. RegionEventData ECA event data for region-related triggers. Carries the Region reference and whether the FishNet prediction system is currently reconciling. RegionGeometry Point-containment helpers for region colliders. Axis-aligned Collider.bounds is wrong for rotated boxes, so boxes are tested in their own local space; other convex colliders use UnityEngine.Collider.ClosestPoint(UnityEngine.Vector3); anything else falls back to bounds. RegionMembership<T> Pure, engine-free bookkeeping for which characters a Region considers "inside". Separates the two truths a region has to reconcile: Raw presence: what the underlying NetworkCollider has told us via Enter/Exit callbacks. This is updated on every callback, including during prediction reconcile replay and while a character is teleporting. Effective membership: characters for which the region has actually raised an Enter (and no Exit yet). Gameplay/visual triggers key off this set. Callbacks that arrive while suppressed (reconciling or teleporting) update raw presence only; Flush(Func<T, bool>, Func<T, bool>, Func<T, bool>, List<T>, List<T>) later diffs raw against effective and yields the Enter/Exit decisions that were deferred, each exactly once. Because Flush(Func<T, bool>, Func<T, bool>, Func<T, bool>, List<T>, List<T>) is a pure diff it also repairs any drift between the two sets (e.g. a child region releasing a character back to its parent). RemoveItemAction ECA action that removes items from a character's inventory by template. Server-only execution. RescuePoints Reads the places a character can be rescued to out of a scene's cached details. ResistanceAttributeTemplate ResourceConsumableTemplate A consumable that restores resources: a healing potion, a mana draught, a ration. ResourceTickBuffTemplate Buff template that applies periodic resource modifications (heal-over-time / damage-over-time). Each tick adds or subtracts from the current value of target resource attributes. The tick amount scales linearly with the number of stacks (base + stacks). This buff is deterministic — identical inputs produce identical state changes. RichText Utility class for formatting rich text strings with color, size, and optional prefixes/suffixes for UI display. Provides both string-returning Format methods and zero-allocation AppendTo methods for StringBuilder use. SceneBackdrop The terrain around a generated scene, out to the horizon: drawn, never walked on. SceneBoundary MonoBehaviour for defining a scene boundary. Draws gizmos for visualization and provides boundary size and offset. SceneBoundaryDetails Serializable class containing details for a scene boundary, including origin, size, and point containment logic. SceneBoundaryDictionary Serializable dictionary mapping string keys to scene boundary details. Provides logic to check if a point is contained in any boundary. SceneCaveLife The cave-life spots of every loaded scene (CaveLife), keyed by scene, offered by the scene's client-only site emitters (SceneSiteEmitters) while it is loaded: what the ambient life places its cave creatures from. SceneCaveMeshes The main object of a scene's <Scene> Caves.asset: its cave systems' rock meshes are sub-assets of it (Cave <site id> P<n>, stored unreadable, each with its collider Cave <site id> C<n>: the same triangles on positions alone, since 2026-10-20), and it keeps, per cave, the key of the inputs those meshes were built from, so a repaint or re-cut that changes nothing about a cave keeps its meshes instead of building them again. SceneCaveWater What lives on and in a cave's still water as every client draws it (2026-10-26, phase I2n-c; decision 86 (i) and its leeches, decision 97): marsh-gas BEADS rising in trails from the drowned muck and ringing out on the surface, and LEECHES swimming in it, toward whoever wades in. Pure; FishCaveWaterLife.shader mirrors it number for number (CaveWaterLife draws it). SceneClimbables The climbables of every loaded scene (Climbables), keyed by scene and filed by horizontal cell, for the climbing movement mode (both peers) and the server's NavMesh links. SceneCloudWorld A scene cut on a gas giant (Celestial.CloudWorld): islands of rock floating over a cloud deck with nothing under it. Written by the cut, kept by the server and every client, and found by scene (TryGet(Scene, out SceneCloudWorld)) by what has to know: the sky (the deck it draws below the islands), the server (who has fallen into it), the airships (the docks they sail between). SceneContentLoads The content a scene fetches for itself after it has loaded: its terrain arrays, biome templates, river flow and the like, each an Addressable load a component starts from its own lifecycle. Those run outside the scene load and outside AddressableLoadProcessor's batches, so nothing that waits on either sees them. The client's loading screen holds world entry until this is empty, so the player arrives in a finished world instead of watching ground and water arrive from the cache or the web server. SceneContentLoads.Load One fetch in flight. SceneContentLoads.Work Work a system still has to do on content that has arrived before the world looks finished (grass taking its terrains, props merging into pools). Polled, not counted: it is added once and asked each frame the loading screen is up. SceneDrip Water dripping from a cave's roof (2026-10-20, caves livened; Drip): how often a drip falls, how its drops fall, when each lands, and how its seed carries the puddle under it. One definition read by the client's drops and puddle rings (CaveDrips and its shader, which repeats FallenMetres(float), JitterOf(uint, long) and the ring constants), its sound (CaveDripPresenter) and the cave dressing that bakes the drips. SceneGlow The cold glow of faerie, rune and crystal light (2026-10-18, I6g; Glow): its tint, its soft slow pulse and when it shows. One definition read by the client's site lights (SiteLightPool) and, constant for constant, by the glowing parts of the pieces that give it off (FishStructureWeathering.hlsl FishStructureGlowLight), so a rune stone's runes brighten and dim with the light they cast. SceneGlowCaves The linked caves' boxes the glow modes read (pure; the GPU's FishGlowCaveRow mirrors RowAt(IReadOnlyList<SceneGlowCave>, Vector3, int)): found from the cave-life spots every client loads (SceneCaveLife: each spot of a linked cave carries its interior biome), so nothing new is stored. A glow whose origin is inside a box reads the box's row before any anchor disc or the biome grid. SceneMagma The molten lava of a lava tube that still runs (2026-10-20; Magma and Fumes): its light's colour and slow churn, how its seed carries the body under it, how much it sparks, the hot air over it and the haze under the roof. One definition read by the client's site lights (SiteLightPool), its embers and fumes (SiteEmbers), its heat haze (the heat shimmer) and the cave walk render. SceneNames A loaded scene's name without the garbage: UnityEngine.SceneManagement.Scene.name builds a new string on every read, and the render hooks that seed their placement from it (ambient and sea life, sea floats, the glow sky's episodes) read it every frame. SceneObject Manages registration and tracking of scene objects with unique IDs in FishMMO. SceneObjectNamer Gives a scene object a generated name — a character, city, dungeon, point of interest or legendary item name — from the name generator, using the object's race and the settings authored on the prefab. The server rolls a seed and a gender and ships those (4 + 1 bytes); every peer then regenerates the same name from the same templates, so the name itself never crosses the wire. The race comes from the object's IFactionController unless the settings override it, which is how one prefab names itself correctly at any spawner. SceneObjectNames The installed scene object name source; null without the Naming module, when every object keeps its authored name. SceneObjectNamingSettings Everything a designer sets on a SceneObjectNamer. Authored on the prefab, so it is identical on both peers and never travels over the wire. ScenePath One way through a scene: a polyline on the finished ground with its width, wear and surface along it. ScenePathField A scene's paths rasterised for the GPU: a distance field half a metre a texel, kept only in the 16 m pages a path passes through. What the terrain, the grass and the details read to draw, thin and clear a path (FishGroundPaths.hlsl). ScenePathSurfaceBinder Hands the GPU a scene's paths: the page table and atlas of its ScenePathField, baked by the cut beside the terrain, as globals the terrain, the grass and the details read (FishGroundPaths.hlsl). ScenePlotManifest The housing lots a scene cut laid, kept beside the scene's terrain. ScenePointOfInterest A generated point of interest in its scene: the transform the site stands at, and the landmark the world map draws for it. ScenePointOfInterestSettings Sits on a generated scene's "Points of Interest" root: which settings its POIs were made with, and the asset they were written to. Its editor offers Regenerate POIs. ScenePointsOfInterest The points of interest a generated scene was given, written beside its terrain as <Scene> Points of Interest.asset: the one source of truth everything else is derived from. ScenePropColliders A scene's baked prop collision: the ScenePropCollisionSets its generator wrote, streamed into physics near characters and the camera by PropColliderStreamer. One per scene, at its root; kept by server and client alike. ScenePropCollisionSet The collidable half of a scene's baked props from one source: a shared collision mesh per prototype and where each collidable prop stands. PropColliderStreamer puts colliders only where they are needed — round every character on the server, round the camera on the client — from pools, so a scene's tens of thousands of trees and rocks never all exist in physics at once. ScenePropSet A scene's baked props from one source (its scatter's trees and large props, its cliffs' rocks, its rivers' boulders): the prefabs they are made of and where each one stands. The client draws them instanced on the GPU; no prop is a scene object. SceneProps A scene's baked props: the ScenePropSets its generator wrote (scatter, cliffs, boulders), which the client draws instanced. One per scene, on a client-only object at its root. ScenePyre A way light's own open fire (Pyre, 2026-10-26, the biome suite's way lights): what its seed says of it and how bright it burns. One definition read by the client's site lights (SiteLightPool) and its flames and sparks (SiteEmbers), so the light a beacon throws and the flames over it are kindled at the same instant. SceneSiteEmitters A scene's baked emitters (Emitters: chimneys, fires, forges, lanterns), offered to the client's site lights and hearth smoke while the scene is loaded. SceneSkylight An opening in a cave's roof up to the sky (2026-10-20, caves livened; Skylight): where its emitter stands and how its seed carries the opening's height over it, and the two measures every presenter of it agrees on — how much of the sky a point under it sees (SkyShare(Vector3, float, Vector3)) and whether the sun falls on it through the opening (InBeam(Vector3, float, Vector3, Vector3)). One definition read by the client's skylight presenter (CaveSkylights: the shaft, the motes, the sky let in round it), its bounce light (SiteLightPool) and the lit surfaces' underground darkness (FishSkylights.hlsl, which mirrors these two functions line for line). SceneTeleporter MonoBehaviour for scene teleporters. Handles teleportation logic on the server and draws gizmos for visualization in the editor. SceneTeleporterCacheDictionary Serializable dictionary mapping composite keys (SceneName/TeleporterName) to scene teleporter cache entries. Used by TeleporterCache to store all known scene teleporters. SceneTeleporterCacheEntry Serializable entry representing a single scene teleporter in the TeleporterCache. Stores the teleporter name, scene, destination connection, and position. SceneTeleporterDetails Serializable class containing details for a scene teleporter destination, including target scene, position, and rotation. SceneTeleporterDictionary Serializable dictionary mapping string keys to scene teleporter details. Used to store and retrieve teleporter destinations and settings for scenes. SceneTerrainBake Holds a scene's TerrainDetailBake on a client-only object at its root (ObjectName), and lists every loaded scene's while enabled, so the client's grass and detail scatter can find a terrain's baked maps (TileOf(TerrainData, out TerrainDetailBake)), the array terrain its stored index map (IndexOf(TerrainData)), and the grass a texture set's colour copy (AlbedoOf(Texture2DArray)). SceneWaypointDetails A waypoint as harvested into the world scene details cache: what the client needs to draw it on the map without the object being streamed. SceneWaypointDictionary Serializable dictionary of a scene's waypoints, keyed by authored waypoint index. ScrollConsumableTemplate Abstract base class for scroll consumable templates, which grant abilities when consumed. Inherits from ConsumableTemplate and adds ability learning logic. SendAbilityCrafterBroadcastAction ECA action that opens the ability crafter UI for the interacting player. Broadcasts AbilityCrafterBroadcast to the owner connection. Server-only. SendArenaBoardBroadcastAction ECA action that opens the arena board panel for the interacting player. SendBankerBroadcastAction ECA action that opens the bank UI for the interacting player. Sets the character's last-interactable ID so follow-up bank transactions are associated with this banker, then broadcasts BankerBroadcast to the owner connection. Server-only. SendContainerOpenBroadcastAction ECA action that sends a ContainerOpenBroadcast to the player containing the container's current item contents. Requires the interactable to implement both IContainer and IItemContainer. Server-only. SendDungeonFinderBroadcastAction ECA action that broadcasts a DungeonFinderBroadcast to the player, opening the dungeon finder interface on the client. Server-only. SendMailboxBroadcastAction ECA action that opens the mailbox UI for the interacting player. Broadcasts MailboxBroadcast to the owner connection. Server-only. SendMerchantBroadcastAction ECA action that opens the merchant UI for the interacting player. Requires the interactable to implement IMerchant. Broadcasts MerchantBroadcast. Server-only. SerializableDictionary SerializableDictionary class definition. SerializableDictionary.Storage<T> Base class for Storage implementation. SerializableDictionaryBase Base class for SerializableDictionaryBase implementation. SerializableDictionaryBase.Dictionary<TKey, TValue> Dictionary class definition. SerializableDictionaryBase.Storage Base class for Storage implementation. SerializableDictionaryBase<TKey, TValue, TValueStorage> SerializableDictionary<TKey, TValue> SerializableDictionary class definition. SerializableDictionary<TKey, TValue, TValueStorage> SerializableDictionary class definition. SerializableHashSetBase Base class for SerializableHashSetBase implementation. SerializableHashSetBase.HashSet<TValue> HashSet class definition. SerializableHashSetBase.Storage Base class for Storage implementation. SerializableHashSet<T> ServerAddress Internal server bind address. For client-facing communication, the address is always Constants.Configuration.GameHost — use Port directly or ServerAddresses.Ports. Converted from a mutable struct to a class to avoid the pass-by-value silent data loss anti-pattern. The previous struct warning about this has been removed since the class semantics eliminate the issue: instances are passed by reference and mutations are not silently lost. ServerAddresses Serializable class containing a list of server ports and a one-time connection token for real-IP recovery on the game server. ServerItemHooks Server-installed callbacks that let shared code hand an item change to the persistence layer without referencing the server assembly. ServerPreloadLabels Addressables labels a module asks the server to load at boot, beside the core's own (Phase 4 of the core and modules plan, 2026-11-18): the World Simulation module's biome templates. The server launcher preloads the core labels and then these; a module that is not installed asks for nothing, so a core-only server preloads no label it does not have. ShaderLookup Find(string) that also finds shaders loaded from Addressable bundles. ShieldInterceptAction Sweeps a shield volume for ability objects in flight and destroys what it catches — the outward-looking half of a block. ShieldVolume The dimensions of a character's shield: a real volume standing in front of them, authored on the buff that raises it. ShowReadonlyAttribute Attribute to mark fields as readonly in the Unity inspector. Used with a custom property drawer to display fields as non-editable. Shrine Shrine interactable that applies buffs or heals health, mana, or both when a player interacts with it. Configured via a ShrineTemplate ScriptableObject asset. ShrineAction ECA action that applies healing and/or a buff from a IShrine, then sends ShrineBroadcast for client-side VFX/SFX feedback. Server-only. ShrineTemplate Template defining a shrine's healing and buff effects. Shrines can heal health, mana, or both, and optionally apply a buff on interaction. SingleTargetEventData Marks an event whose actions act on its own target only: no trigger or action selector fans it out. SitRules What can be sat on: a level top seat-high over the feet, deep enough to sit on. The World Sim walker sits by it (the game has no sitting yet). SkeletonBinder Utility for binding equipment SkinnedMeshRenderers to the character skeleton at runtime. Provides safe bone binding that does not destroy shared parent hierarchies. SkeletonBones Authoritative bone names for the master humanoid skeleton. Every character model and equipment mesh must use these exact bone names. Artists must never rename, add, or remove required bones. SkinnedMeshRendererExtensions Extension methods for SkinnedMeshRenderer, including skeleton assignment and bone cache management. SnapshotAttributeController Lightweight read-only ICharacterAttributeController backed by frozen CharacterAttribute instances. Used by SnapshotCharacter to satisfy StatScaledValue and StatScaledFloatValue lookups for detached ability objects whose caster has disconnected. Only TryGetAttribute(int, out CharacterAttribute) is functional. All mutating methods are no-ops. SnapshotCharacter Lightweight phantom ICharacter implementation that preserves a frozen snapshot of character identity and attribute data. Created when a caster disconnects so that detached AbilityObjects can continue to resolve stat-scaled calculations via StatScaledValue and StatScaledFloatValue without a live networked character. Only TryGet<T>(out T) for ICharacterAttributeController is supported. All other behaviour lookups return false, causing downstream systems (achievements, factions, etc.) to gracefully degrade. StatScaledFloatValue Float value provider that scales a character attribute's final value by a configurable factor. Reads the initiator's (or event target's) attribute and returns Attribute.FinalValue * ScaleFactor. StatScaledValue Value provider that scales a character attribute's final value by a configurable factor. Reads the initiator's (or event target's) attribute and returns (int)(Attribute.FinalValue * ScaleFactor). StateBuffTemplate Buff template that enables CharacterFlags on apply and disables them on remove. Used for crowd-control effects such as Frozen, Stunned, and Mesmerized. Flags are additive per stack: each stack enables the same flag (idempotent via bitwise OR), but removal only clears the flag when the last stack (and base) are removed. StructureKitTemplate A housing structure in carried form: what comes out of the house vault. SubclassSelectorAttribute Attribute for UnityEngine.SerializeReference fields that enables a type-selection dropdown in the Unity Inspector. Supports polymorphic serialization of plain C# class hierarchies. Apply to fields or list elements decorated with UnityEngine.SerializeReference. SwimPose How a swimmer is drawn in the water: how far it leans, how near the surface it counts as, where its body turns, and how it tips on a wave. The arithmetic behind CharacterAnimationController's procedural swim pose and the World Sim walker's figure, kept apart so both pose a swimmer the same way and the rules can be tested. Switch Switch interactable that executes a function on another script when activated. Used for opening doors, unlocking chests, stopping or engaging traps, and similar mechanisms. The target object must implement ISwitchTarget. SwitchAction ECA action that activates or deactivates an ISwitchTarget linked by the interacted ISwitch, then broadcasts the new state to the player. Toggle switches flip state each interaction; non-toggle switches only activate once (the CanInteract(IPlayerCharacter) guard prevents re-interaction on non-toggle switches that are already activated). Server-only. SwitchTargetMover A ISwitchTarget that slides and/or rotates a transform between a closed pose and an open pose — a door, a portcullis, a drawbridge, a moving platform. SwitchTargetObject A ISwitchTarget that enables and disables a set of GameObjects. TaggedSceneObjectTargetSelector Resolves scene UnityEngine.GameObjects by Unity tag at runtime. Designed for asset-based Triggers that need to target one or more pre-tagged scene objects — selectors serialized on ScriptableObject assets cannot hold direct scene references, but they can hold a tag string and resolve it at fire time. The lookup is scoped to the context's scene (whatever scene the event's Target or Initiator lives in). Results are filtered through this selector's Conditions. Tag pre-requisite: the tag must exist in Unity's Tag Manager (ProjectSettings > Tags and Layers). Using an unknown tag logs a warning and yields no targets. TargetAllianceCondition Condition that checks the alliance relationship between the initiator and the target (defender). Allows configuration for which alliance types (self, enemy, neutral, ally) the condition applies to. TargetController Controls targeting logic for a character, including raycasting, target selection, and target events. TargetOrdering Deterministic ordering, ranking and shape tests shared by every target selector. TargetSelector Abstract base class for selecting targets in an ability or event context. Implementations consume the current EventData (its Target or Initiator serve as the spatial / contextual reference) and yield one or more UnityEngine.GameObjects for triggers, conditions or actions to operate on. Asset safety: selectors are serialized inline on Trigger ScriptableObjects via [SerializeReference]. Unity cannot serialize references to scene GameObjects from asset files, so selectors intentionally hold no direct scene references. To "pick a specific scene object" from an asset-based Trigger, use NamedSceneObjectTargetSelector or TaggedSceneObjectTargetSelector — they resolve scene objects at runtime by name or tag. For inline (MonoBehaviour-hosted) triggers in a scene, prefer setting Target at the invocation site so the trigger receives the picked GameObject through standard event flow. TargetedEntitySelector Selects the caster's resolved target entity, validated by range — the EverQuest / WoW model. TeleportAction ECA action that teleports the interacting player via a ITeleporter. If the teleporter has a Target transform set, the player is moved to that world position and rotation. Otherwise the player is teleported by the teleporter's key via Teleport(string), which the character system resolves against the world scene details cache: a same-scene destination is a local move, any other is a scene transfer. Server-only. TeleportCasterAction Blinks the caster up to MaxDistance metres the way it faces, stopping short of whatever is in the way, and plays ArriveFX where it lands. Teleporter Represents a teleporter interactable that can transport players to a target location. Inherits from Interactable and provides a target Transform for teleportation. TeleporterCache ScriptableObject cache for storing all known teleporter destinations. Pre-baked by scanning world scenes for TeleporterDestination components, keyed by stable DestinationID. Must be rebuilt before WorldSceneDetailsCache to ensure teleporter connections are validated. TeleporterCacheDictionary Serializable dictionary mapping destination IDs to teleporter cache entries. Used by TeleporterCache to store all known teleporter destinations. TeleporterCacheEditor Custom editor for the teleporter cache asset. Displays cache health, highlights invalid teleporter links, and provides one-click scene navigation to broken teleporter objects for quick fixes. TeleporterCacheEntry Serializable entry representing a single teleporter destination in the TeleporterCache. Stores the stable GUID, scene, display name, position, and rotation for a destination. TeleporterDestination Represents a destination point for teleporters in the scene. Each destination has a stable DestinationID (GUID) that survives renames and moves. Used to visually indicate and mark teleporter endpoints in the Unity Editor. TemplateReferenceAttribute Marks an int or List<int> field as a template ID reference. In the Inspector, the field displays an object picker for the specified CachedScriptableObject type but serializes only the deterministic ID. TerrainArrayBinder Hands each terrain tile of a scene what the array terrain shader reads: the tile's index map (its four strongest layers per alphamap texel, baked here from its alphamaps), and the scene's baked texture arrays and layer table. TerrainArrayLayerSource One layer of a scene's terrain, in channel order, and every biome slot that painted with it. TerrainArrayLayerUse One biome's use of a terrain layer: which biome, and which of its layer slots. TerrainArrayProvenance Where each of a scene's terrain layers came from, so its art can be found again — LOCAL overrides included — every time the arrays are baked. TerrainArraySet One scene's baked terrain art: the albedo, normal and mask texture arrays the array terrain shader samples, and each layer's tiling and remaps. TerrainBoundary MonoBehaviour for defining terrain boundaries. Draws gizmos for visualization and provides boundary size and offset based on terrain data. TerrainDetailBake A scene's terrain detail maps, baked by the cut (TerrainDetailBaker, client editor): per terrain, what the client's blade grass (GrassTerrain) and GPU detail scatter (DetailScatterTerrain) used to build from the terrain data on every Play — the summed, smoothed and packed density maps, the heights, the water line and holes, the surface layers, the work items' bounds — and the terrain's index map (TerrainDetailBake.IndexMap, what the array terrain draws in a player), plus the grass's colour copies of the terrain texture sets. The client takes a terrain from here in a frame instead of reading it back over ~1,400 frames, and falls back to building it whenever an entry does not match what it would build (Version, the prototypes and their prefabs, the resolutions, the scatter's density scale) or is marked Stale. TerrainDetailBake.Albedo A terrain texture set's albedo copy for the grass's colour (GrassAlbedoTexels): every layer's mip pyramid, as the runtime read it back off the GPU. The per-layer header (tiling and tint) is the set's own, written at load. TerrainDetailBake.Grass The blade grass's maps of one terrain (GrassTerrain). TerrainDetailBake.GroundColour The ground colour map (GroundColourMap) over all of the scene's terrains: per texel the splat-weighted mean colour of the layers as the terrain draws them, and the surface normal; with what it was made from, so the client uses it only when the same terrains stand in the same places drawn with the same texture sets. TerrainDetailBake.IndexMap One terrain's index map (TerrainIndexMap) as the cut stored it: every alphamap texel's four strongest layers and their weights, two words a texel, row by row — the CPU bake from the alphamaps the cut wrote, the GPU bake's texels bit for bit. A player binds it instead of baking from the alphamaps, so a client build can leave the alphamaps out (ClientTerrainLayerStripper, which checks the map against them first). TerrainDetailBake.Scatter The GPU detail scatter's maps of one terrain (DetailScatterTerrain). TerrainDetailBake.Tile One terrain: its heights (shared by both maps' height textures) and its grass and scatter. TerrainDetailBiomes Which biome's spawn rule made each of a terrain's detail prototypes, beside the terrain (written by the scene cut's scatter, TerrainScatter). The scatter makes one prototype per rule and prefab, so the grass on a terrain is several prototypes of one prefab, each painted where its own biome grows it; with this the client knows which biome's look a prototype's blades take (Biomes.BiomeTemplate.GrassTypes), and that its healthy and dry tints are its rule's. TerrainIndexMap The terrain's index map: for every texel of a tile's alphamaps, its four strongest layers and their weights, packed into eight bytes. What the array terrain shader reads in place of the alphamaps themselves, so a scene may carry up to MaximumLayers layers at the cost of four texel reads a pixel, however many it has. TerrainIndexMapBaker Bakes a terrain tile's index map (TerrainIndexMap) on the GPU, from the tile's own alphamaps, into an R32G32_UInt render texture the array terrain shader loads. TerrainLayerTable A scene's per-layer numbers as one small float texture the array terrain shader loads by layer: column = layer, row = which number. Replaces the per-layer uniform arrays (_FishLayerST[32] and the rest). TerrainScatterModes The scatter modes a terrain's prototypes carry to the client (2026-10-26, phase SCATTER-MODES, decision 34), beside the terrain (written by the scene cut's scatter, TerrainScatter, only when some rule of the scene names a mode; a scene without one has no record at all, so nothing in it changes): a detail prototype's facing, lean and power-law size for the GPU detail scatter, and a tree prototype's lean for the tree renderer (a tree instance has no tilt of its own). Each is two words (Biomes.BiomeScatterModeWord). TerrainSnowHoleFade How much of its deep-snow lift each heightmap vertex of a terrain tile keeps near a hole in the terrain: none at a hole's edge, all of it FadeMetres away, eased between. One byte a vertex in an R8 map the array terrain shader loads at the vertex (FishTerrainSnowHoles.hlsl), handed to each tile by TerrainArrayBinder. TerrainTileLayerMap The arithmetic of per-tile terrain layers (TerrainTileLayers): which of a tile's alphamap channels it keeps, the compacted alphamaps, and how a tile's channel numbers become the scene's layer ids wherever the ground is read by layer (the index map bake, the ground colour, the grass's surface layers). Pure, so the tests run it without Unity. TerrainTileLayers Which of the scene's terrain layers a tile's alphamap channels hold, when the tile carries only the layers it paints (TerrainTileLayerMap): channel c is scene layer SceneLayers[c], the slice of the scene's texture arrays and the id its index map names. TickEventData Lightweight EventData subtype carrying a network tick for tick-aware triggers. TickPoser Poses every ITickPosed before each tick a character is simulated at: the live tick (TimeManager.OnPreTick), each tick a client replays (PredictionManager.OnPreReplicateReplay) and the live tick again after a reconcile (OnPostReconcile), each mapped to the server tick it runs at exactly as the ships are (FloatingBoats, WeatherExposureTick), then Physics.SyncTransforms once. TinyColor A lightweight color struct using byte values for R, G, B, and A components (0-255). Provides conversions, predefined colors, and utility functions for color manipulation. TinyColorExtensions Provides extension methods for the TinyColor struct. TooltipContent A tooltip as structured data: an icon, a title, and typed rows. TooltipExtensions Convenience over ITooltip for callers that want a whole tooltip in one call. TooltipPalette The colours a tooltip's tones and row kinds resolve to. TooltipPriority Standard sort priorities, so independently authored sections interleave predictably. TransformExtensions Extension methods for Unity Transforms, including bone hierarchy and child GameObject search utilities. UnequipItemAction Action that attempts to unequip an item from the initiating character. Optionally uses ItemEventData from the EventData to override the target slot and container. Server-only execution — equipment mutations rearrange persistent item ownership between containers and must never run during client prediction replay. UnityConsoleFormatter Implements ILogger to output log entries to the Unity Editor console. Also implements IConsoleFormatter to support direct colored output via Log.WritePartsToConsole. Supports Unity rich text coloring. UnityConsoleLogger Implements ILogger to output log entries to the Unity Editor console. Supports Unity rich text coloring. UnityConsoleLoggerConfig Configuration for the Unity Console Logger. Messages routed through FishMMO.Logging.Log will also appear in the Unity console if this logger is enabled and the log level is allowed. UnityLoggerBridge Bridges Unity's logging system with the FishMMO.Logging system by implementing ILogHandler. Intercepts all Unity Debug.Log messages and forwards them to the central Log manager, while also preventing Unity's default console output. Designed to be separate from core ILogger implementations. Vector3Extensions Extension methods for Vector3, providing randomization and geometric utilities for spheres and toroids. VersionBuilder Handles versioning for FishMMO builds. Provides build post-processing to write version info, and menu items for incrementing and resetting version numbers. VersionConfig ScriptableObject holding semantic versioning information for FishMMO builds. Supports parsing, comparison, and equality operations. Waypoint A discoverable fast-travel point. Interacting with it unlocks it for the character; once unlocked it appears on that character's world map and can be travelled to. WaypointRegistry Server-side index of the live waypoints in every loaded scene, by Unity scene handle and authored waypoint index. WaypointUnlockMask The waypoints a character has discovered in one scene, as a growable bit set: bit N of page N / 64 is set when waypoint N is unlocked. WaypointUnlockedCondition ECA condition: the character has discovered a particular waypoint. WeaponTemplate ScriptableObject template for weapon items, defining attack power and attack speed attributes. Inherits from EquippableItemTemplate for equipment logic. Weapons are not skinned — they attach as MeshRenderer children of the specified bone transform. WeatherExposureController Turns the weather a character is standing in into buffs — wet, chilled, wind-burnt — and does it inside the prediction replicate, so the owner sees the state change at the moment it earns it rather than a round trip later. WebFrameLoop Caps the client's render rate without taking the web player off the browser's animation frames. WildlifeBody A wild animal's body and its animation: the species' procedural mesh (WildlifeBodyMesh) under the character's mesh root, posed each frame by four shader parameters (FishMMO/Wildlife). Stands in for the humanoid CharacterAnimationController on wildlife prefabs, so the ability and damage code that triggers attacks, casts and deaths reaches it unchanged. Client only; on the server it does nothing. WildlifeBodyMesh Builds a species' procedural body (WildlifeBodySpec): one flat-shaded low-poly mesh, shared by every animal of the species, animated entirely in the vertex shader (FishMMO/Wildlife). WildlifeHarmRelation Wildlife is outside the faction system: anyone may harm it and it may harm anyone, except a pack its own members. Asked before companions: a wild animal has no party or guild. WildlifeRules The rules wildlife lives by, outside the faction system. Every check that would otherwise ask a faction asks here first: the harm rule (MayHarm(ICharacter, ICharacter, out ICharacter)) and the AI's search for something to fight or flee. WildlifeTemplate One species of wildlife: its role and the numbers its brain and body use. Referenced by the species' NPC prefab (Wildlife), so server and clients read the same values. WithinRangeCondition Passes when the evaluated character is within a distance of the initiator. WorldItem Represents an item that exists in the world and can be interacted with or picked up by players. WorldMapDefinition Everything a scene needs in order to present itself: its player-facing name, the image shown while it loads, the baked overhead map the world map draws, the world-space rectangle that map covers, and the labels and landmarks placed on it. WorldSceneDetails Serializable data structure containing configuration details for a game scene. Includes client limits, transition visuals, spawn/respawn positions, teleporters, and boundaries. WorldSceneDetailsCache ScriptableObject cache for storing and managing all world scene details in the game. Provides centralized access and rebuild functionality for scene configuration data. WorldSceneDetailsCacheEditor Custom editor for WorldSceneDetailsCache ScriptableObject. Adds a "Rebuild" button to the inspector for manual cache rebuilding. WorldSceneDetailsCacheReader ScriptableObject responsible for reading and rebuilding world scene details from Unity scenes. Scans all configured world scenes, extracts spawn positions, boundaries, teleporters, and validates destinations against the TeleporterCache. WorldSceneDetailsDictionary Serializable dictionary mapping scene names to their configuration details. Used to store and access all world scene details for the game. WorldSceneEntries The world scene entries the installed world design offers (IWorldSceneEntry), by scene name. WorldSceneScan The seam the world scene details rebuild offers to editor tooling: every world scene, while it is open. WorldSceneSettings MonoBehaviour holding per-scene server-facing configuration and the link to the scene's WorldMapDefinition. WorldSceneTrigger Inline ECA trigger data for world-scene events (scene load, day start, night start, …). Unlike the asset-based Trigger, this type is [Serializable] and lives directly on a host MonoBehaviour so designers can author scene-specific responses inline. Execution semantics — selector fan-out, condition branching, action dispatch — are delegated to RunInline(TargetSelector, List<BaseCondition>, List<BaseAction>, List<BaseAction>, EventData) so this type stays in lock-step with any future Trigger behaviour changes. WorldServerDetails Serializable class containing details about a world server, including name, port, status, and player count. WorldTick The server tick "now" means for world state every peer derives from the shared clock: tides, weather, world motion. Structs AICharacterInputs Input data supplied by an AI controller for character movement and facing. AbilityActivatedBroadcast Tells observers that a character activated an ability, with everything needed to reproduce it. AbilityActivationReplicateData Replicate data for ability activation, used internally by AbilityController. The unified CharacterReplicateData is what FishNet serializes for prediction. AbilityAddBroadcast Broadcast for adding an ability to a character, including its events. Contains the ability's instance ID, template ID, and associated event IDs. AbilityAddMultipleBroadcast Broadcast for adding multiple abilities to a character at once. Used for bulk updates or synchronization. AbilityCrafterBroadcast Broadcast for interacting with an ability crafter object. Contains the interactable object's ID. AbilityForgetBroadcast Client → server. The player asked to forget one of their crafted abilities. AbilityForgetResultBroadcast Server → owner. The answer to AbilityForgetBroadcast. AbilityForgottenObserverBroadcast Server → observers. A character forgot an ability. AbilityLearnedObserverBroadcast Tells observers that a character learned an ability, so they can draw its casts. AbilityObjectDestroyedBroadcast Tells observers that an ability object ended on the server through a collision. RequestServerListBroadcast Broadcast for requesting the list of available servers. No additional data required. RescuePoint One place a rescue can send a character to. ResourceRestoration One resource an item restores, and by how much. RespawnAtBindPointBroadcast Sent client to server when the dead player chooses to respawn at their bind point. RevokeTokenBroadcast Broadcast sent by the client during an explicit logout to ask the LoginServer to revoke its currently-held auth token before its TTL expires. The server hashes the bytes via TokenService.HashToken and matches the row in IAuthTokenService. The ambient life places its cave creatures on these and keeps them to them, so it needs no ray against the cave's rock, and the cave's floors under and over each other are no puzzle to it (the terrain's one height a place is useless underground). ScenePropSet.Prototype One kind of prop: the prefab drawn (its LOD group, meshes and materials) and the layer it draws on. ServerListBroadcast Broadcast for sending the list of available servers to the client. Contains a list of world server details. ShrineBroadcast Server → Client broadcast answering a shrine interaction. SiteDiscoveredBroadcast Server → owner: the character discovered a point of interest for the first time. TargetRank One candidate's sort keys, detached from the GameObject it came from. TargetSelectionBroadcast Tells the server which character the player's targeting frame currently shows. TerrainArrayLayerParams The numbers one terrain layer contributes to the array terrain shader, besides its textures. TerrainDetailBake.ScatterChannel TerrainDetailBiomes.Entry One detail prototype's biome. TerrainScatterModes.Detail TerrainScatterModes.Tree ToastBroadcast A short, transient message shown to one player. TokenAuthBroadcast Broadcast sent by the client to authenticate with a World or Scene server using a signed token issued by the LoginServer after SRP success. TooltipRow One row of tooltip content, kept as data rather than as formatted text. TwoFactorSetupBroadcast Broadcast sent by the server after account creation containing encrypted TOTP setup data (otpauth URI and recovery codes) for two-factor authentication. WARNING: The nonce-derivation scheme on both client and server depends on C# struct field declaration order matching FishNet serialization order. The server sends OtpauthUri first, then RecoveryCodes, and the client consumes them in that exact sequence via receiveNonceCtx.NextNonce(). If these fields are reordered, the nonce streams desynchronize and TOTP silently breaks. DO NOT reorder OtpauthUri and RecoveryCodes. WorldClockBroadcast Server → client: the world clock's anchor, and the one it is easing away from, so a client that arrives mid-correction computes the same time as everyone else. WorldSceneConnectBroadcast Broadcast for connecting to a world scene server. Contains only the port; address is always Constants.Configuration.GameHost. WorldSceneQueueLeaveBroadcast Sent by a client to the WorldServer when the player chooses to leave the scene-routing queue, immediately before it closes the connection. WorldSceneQueuePositionBroadcast Broadcast sent by the WorldServer to a client waiting to be routed to a SceneServer, with its current position in the scene-routing queue. Sent periodically at a server-configured rate. Position semantics (identical to LoginQueuePositionBroadcast): > 0 — Waiting in queue. Display the position to the user. 0 — Routed. A WorldSceneConnectBroadcast follows; dismiss the wait UI. -1 — Cancelled. The wait was abandoned and the connection is being closed. Why this exists. The World → Scene hop is the one leg of the connection pipeline that could stall indefinitely with nothing on screen but a loading overlay. A client with no scene instance to go to is held in the WorldServer's queue and re-evaluated every cycle, so the wait is legitimate — but it was completely silent, which is indistinguishable from a hang. This is the login queue's feedback channel applied to the same problem one hop later. Server-authoritative update rate: The WorldServer controls how often this broadcast is sent. Clients are passive receivers only — there is no request path. Interfaces IAbilityModifier A rule that scales one of an ability's numbers by something about where and when it is cast: the weather (the Climate and Weather module's WeatherAbilityModifier), and whatever other modules add. Also provides access to the character's skeleton root for equipment mesh binding. ICachedObject Interface for objects that support caching with a unique identifier and cache management methods. ICharacterAnimationController What a character's movement, abilities and death tell its animation. The character's own peers call it (its movement and abilities run there); a client watching someone else hears nothing from that character and reads its body off what it can see, plus the cast and death broadcasts every observer receives. Nothing here is synced. ICharacterAppearanceManager Manages character visual appearance: bone scaling for body proportions, blend shape synchronization across body and equipment, and appearance data serialization. IClearanceSwitchTarget A ISwitchTarget that turns solid where it comes to rest, and so must not be moved onto a character: a door shut on someone standing in its doorway would close its leaf around them, and the character controller would pop them out through it to whichever side was nearer. ICompanionRelation A relation that also says who are companions: never harmed, never drawn hostile, whatever anyone's toggle says. IEntityLinked An object that stands for a Core entity: a character, on each side it is spawned on. IEquipmentVisualController Manages visual representation of equipped items on a character. Handles mesh loading, skeleton binding, renderer pooling, and body region hiding. IHarmRelation One feature's say in who may harm whom: the arena's teams, wildlife, companions (party, guild, one's own pet), faction standing. HarmRule asks the relations in Order; the first that decides wins. IInteractable Interface for interactable objects in the scene, providing interaction logic and UI display properties. Used for NPCs, objects, and other entities that players can interact with. IMapMarkerIconSource Supplies a marker's icon when the marker has no authored one of its own. IModelReadyHandler Implemented by character behaviours that need to re-initialize when the character's visual model finishes loading asynchronously. api/webservers/FishMMO.ControlPanel.Auth.summary: Class PanelAuthenticationHandler Namespace FishMMO.ControlPanel.Auth Assembly FishMMO-ControlPanel.dll Turns the panel's session cookie into a ClaimsPrincipal. public sealed class PanelAuthenticationHandler : AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>, IAuthenticationHandler Inheritance object AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions> PanelAuthenticationHandler Implements IAuthenticationHandler Inherited Members AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>.InitializeAsync(AuthenticationScheme, HttpContext) AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>.AuthenticateAsync() AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>.ChallengeAsync(AuthenticationProperties) AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>.ForbidAsync(AuthenticationProperties) AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>.Scheme AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>.Options object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The access level is re-read from the account on every request rather than trusted from the session row. api/webservers/FishMMO.ControlPanel.Auth.summary: Class PanelSessionManager Namespace FishMMO.ControlPanel.Auth Assembly FishMMO-ControlPanel.dll Issues, validates and revokes Control Panel browser sessions. public sealed class PanelSessionManager Inheritance object PanelSessionManager Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The browser holds an opaque 32-byte identifier; the database holds only its SHA-256, so a database read does not yield usable sessions. The identifier is delivered as a cookie that is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict and host-scoped to the panel. Elevated sessions get shorter lifetimes than player sessions, on the principle that the blast radius of a stolen operator session is the whole shard. Constructors PanelSessionManager(IWebSessionService) public PanelSessionManager(IWebSessionService sessions) Parameters sessions IWebSessionService Fields CookieName Name of the session cookie. public const string CookieName = "fishmmo_panel_session" Field Value string Methods BuildCookieOptions(DateTime, bool) Cookie options for the session cookie. public static CookieOptions BuildCookieOptions(DateTime expiresUtc, bool isDevelopment) Parameters expiresUtc DateTime isDevelopment bool Returns CookieOptions Hash(string) Hashes a session identifier the way the store expects. public static string Hash(string sessionId) Parameters sessionId string Returns string IdleTimeoutFor(byte) Idle timeout that applies at a given access level. public static TimeSpan IdleTimeoutFor(byte accessLevel) Parameters accessLevel byte Returns TimeSpan IssueAsync(string, byte, bool, string, string, CancellationToken) Issues a session and returns the raw identifier for the cookie. The identifier is returned exactly once and never stored. public Task<(bool Ok, string SessionId, WebSessionData Session, string Error)> IssueAsync(string accountName, byte accessLevel, bool twoFactorSatisfied, string ipAddress, string userAgent, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters accountName string accessLevel byte twoFactorSatisfied bool ipAddress string userAgent string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<(bool Ok, string SessionId, WebSessionData Session, string Error)> LifetimeFor(byte) Absolute lifetime that applies at a given access level. public static TimeSpan LifetimeFor(byte accessLevel) Parameters accessLevel byte Returns TimeSpan PromoteAsync(string, byte, CancellationToken) Promotes a pending session once its second factor is proven, extending it to the account's real lifetime. public Task<bool> PromoteAsync(string hash, byte accessLevel, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters hash string accessLevel byte cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<bool> false when the promotion did not persist. Remarks The result is returned rather than discarded. Swallowing it meant a promotion could fail while the endpoint still answered "signed in", leaving the operator with a session that every subsequent policy check refused. RevokeAllAsync(string, CancellationToken) Revokes every session for an account, returning how many rows changed. public Task<DatabaseResult<int>> RevokeAllAsync(string accountName, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters accountName string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<DatabaseResult<int>> RevokeAsync(string, CancellationToken) Revokes one session. public Task<bool> RevokeAsync(string hash, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters hash string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<bool> false when the revocation did not persist. Remarks Returned rather than swallowed, for the reason PromoteAsync(string, byte, CancellationToken) gives: this used to be typed Task, which made the result unobservable, and sign-out answered success while the session row lived on. StepUpAsync(string, CancellationToken) Records a fresh step-up. public Task<bool> StepUpAsync(string hash, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters hash string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<bool> false when the step-up did not persist. TouchAsync(string, CancellationToken) Stamps activity on a live session. public Task TouchAsync(string hash, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters hash string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task ValidateAsync(string, CancellationToken) Loads a session by its raw identifier and applies the revoked, expiry and idle checks. public Task<(PanelSessionManager.Validity Result, WebSessionData Session, string Hash)> ValidateAsync(string sessionId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters sessionId string cancellationToken CancellationToken Returns Task<(PanelSessionManager.Validity Result, WebSessionData Session, string Hash)> Remarks A session past its idle timeout is revoked here rather than merely refused, so an abandoned browser cannot be resurrected by a stolen cookie inside the absolute window. A failed read is Unavailable, never Invalid. Treating the two alike made the handler delete the cookie of every operator whose request arrived during a database blip, signing the whole staff out of the panel they needed during the incident.
