guides/FishMMO-Dependencies/ThirdParty/N.title: Npgsql 5.0.18 Unity AOT compatibility build | FishMMO Documentation
guides/FishMMO-Dependencies/ThirdParty/N.summary: Npgsql 5.0.18 Unity AOT compatibility build View this file on GitHub Pinned upstream source: https://github.com/npgsql/npgsql/tree/v5.0.18/src/Npgsql License: PostgreSQL (see LICENSE). Upstream signing identity and assembly/package version are retained so the existing EF Core PostgreSQL provider remains compatible. Three upstream runtime methods are changed: NpgsqlTypeHandler<TDefault>.GenerateNonGenericValidationMethod NpgsqlSimpleTypeHandler<TDefault>.GenerateNonGenericValidationMethod NpgsqlConnector.Connect: accept SocketError.InProgress as a pending non-blocking connection, alongside WouldBlock. The two validator factories previously used Expression.Compile to create a delegate with a ref NpgsqlLengthCache argument. Unity's IL2CPP profile interprets expressions; its LightLambda.CreateCustomDelegate throws NotImplementedException("byref delegate"). This happens while opening the connection and initializing driver handlers, before any application SQL can run. Preserving more linker metadata cannot implement this missing interpreter operation. The replacement uses an ordinary C# delegate, compiled ahead of time by IL2CPP, with an immutable dispatch table of the handler's implemented interfaces. Dispatch still matches the exact boxed CLR type, preserves null/DBNull handling in the original callers, copies a mutated ref length cache back even on exceptions, and unwraps TargetInvocationException with ExceptionDispatchInfo so caller-visible exception types and stacks are preserved. Simple validators leave the cache alone. No runtime compilation of a byref expression delegate is required. Both Mono and IL2CPP use the same implementation. Reflection dispatch allocates a small argument array per non-generic validation; typed parameter paths are unchanged. The wrapper builds the original source for netstandard2.1 using the same support package versions already shipped in FishMMO Unity. Design-time tools are not added. FishMMO-Dependencies builds this project and copies its DLL over the normal NuGet Npgsql DLL only in Unity's Assets/Dependencies directory. Other .NET applications keep their existing NuGet driver. Rebuilding dependencies therefore cannot silently replace the fix with the unmodified package DLL. To rebuild only the compatibility DLL: dotnet build ThirdParty/Npgsql.UnityAot/Npgsql.UnityAot.csproj dotnet msbuild FishMMO-Dependencies.csproj -t:CopyUnityAotNpgsql After updating the DLL, rebuild the dedicated game server for the backend selected in the dashboard. Existing native IL2CPP players cannot consume a replacement managed DLL without rebuilding. Keep the server linker preservation rules as well: constructor stripping and runtime expression support were independent failures. The native IL2CPP test also exposed a separate synchronous socket compatibility issue: Unity returned SocketError.InProgress (10036) for a non-blocking TCP connect, while Npgsql accepted only WouldBlock and aborted before its existing Select/error check. Both are valid pending-connect results on this path. The adapter now accepts both and leaves the existing timeout, readiness, error and socket cleanup logic intact. Verified with Unity 6000.4.10f1: the unmodified driver reproduced the failure under Unity's AOT profile; the compatibility driver passed both framework-profile probes and actual standalone dedicated-server Mono and IL2CPP players. Checks include all 77 EF entity models, registry reads, asynchronous EF queries, tracked synthetic-row materialization, ten parameter roundtrips and validator exception propagation. No application rows were modified. The result files were not kept; FishMMO-Dependencies/Tools/DatabaseRuntimeProbe reruns the checks.

guides/FishMMO-Dependencies/Tools/Databa.title: Unity database runtime compatibility probe | FishMMO Documentation
guides/FishMMO-Dependencies/Tools/Databa.summary: Unity database runtime compatibility probe View this file on GitHub Read-only regression checks for the exact Unity Mono and AOT framework profiles. Uses Unity's Mono executable, imported EF assemblies and database configuration; it does not change any rows or start the application servers. The driver tests exercise Unicode text/length-cache writeback, integers, alternate CLR type handling, UUID, timestamp, byte array, integer array, boolean, decimal, DBNull, and propagation of the original OverflowException from a reflected validator. EF checks load the full model, query each of the three server registries, run asynchronous queries, and materialize/track a synthetic server row from a SELECT without saving or inserting it. The native harness runs these blocking diagnostic waits on a worker task so UnitySynchronizationContext remains responsive. From this directory: python3 run.py --editor /path/to/Unity/Editor/Unity # Also verify actual Linux Mono and IL2CPP standalone players (takes longer): python3 run.py --editor /path/to/Unity/Editor/Unity --native Defaults use the current game server's appsettings.json and the imported Unity Npgsql DLL. --settings, --driver and --artifacts override these paths. Existing secure database credential resolution is used; no credentials are passed on the command line or written into the report. PgBouncer/PostgreSQL must be running. The official Npgsql 5.0.18 netstandard2.1 NuGet package must be restored locally. The matching Unity Linux Mono/IL2CPP build modules must be installed for native mode. The matrix requires original Mono to pass, original AOT to reproduce the precise byref-delegate failure, and patched Mono/AOT to pass. Profile tests run the Unity AOT managed libraries under Mono to diagnose interpreter behavior; those tests alone do not verify native IL2CPP generic code generation. --native supplies that additional check in a separate temporary Unity project, leaving the real game's Editor, backend preference, and installed servers untouched. Inspect summary.json and the per-profile/player logs in the reported artifact folder. A passing probe does not assert full authenticated game-session readiness.

guides/FishMMO-DiscordBot/README.html.title: FishMMO Discord Bot | FishMMO Documentation
guides/FishMMO-DiscordBot/README.html.summary: FishMMO Discord Bot View this file on GitHub A standalone .NET 8 application that bridges a live FishMMO server with a Discord guild. The bot relays in-game chat to Discord channels and back, delivers the Discord account-verification code to players who chose Discord at registration, lets players link their Discord account to their FishMMO account, exposes administrative commands (mute, ban, kick, character lookup), and dynamically provisions per-world / per-scene channels. It runs as a long-lived service alongside the rest of the FishMMO server stack. Table of Contents Description Supported Platforms Architecture Key Components Modules (Discord-side commands) Services (long-running workers) Data Account Verification by Discord Account Links Configuration appsettings.json shape Build & Run Deployment Notes Flow Diagram Description The bot is built on the Discord.Net client library and the standard Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting generic host. It composes a fixed set of modules (command handlers) and services (background workers) through DI, reads its configuration from appsettings.json, and talks to the FishMMO PostgreSQL database directly through the shared FishMMO-DB project. Bridging is two-way: Game → Discord: ChatPollingService periodically reads new rows from the game's chat table and forwards the relayable ones to the matching Discord channel. It reads through ChatService.FetchRelayAsync with a ChatReadWindow (both in FishMMO-DB), the same window the scene servers' chat pump keeps: each read starts a commit window behind what it has settled and skips by ID what it has already handled, so a row that commits out of ID order is not skipped and no row is relayed twice. Each poll reads at most 5 pages of 200 rows, so a relay that has fallen behind catches up over several polls, and the first read starts at the database's "now", so a restarted bot does not replay history. A read that fails settles nothing and is read again on the next poll; once a batch's reads have succeeded, each row is recorded as handled before it is checked for a link code or sent, so a row whose send fails costs that one row and is never relayed twice. Discord → Game: Discord messages in a managed channel are intercepted by CommandHandlingService and written into the chat table by GameChatBridgeService, subject to RateLimiterService and BridgeBanService. The write goes through ChatService.PersistBridgedAsync, the same INSERT the scene servers use, so the row is stamped by the database clock the scene servers' chat pumps page by, not by the bot host's clock, which could stamp a row behind a window the pumps had already passed. Account verification is one-way: the game and the Control Panel issue a code, DiscordVerificationService DMs it to the player, and the player types it back into the game or the panel. Supported Platforms Target Status .NET 8.0 (Linux, Windows, macOS) Yes Docker / Linux service Recommended for production Requirement Version .NET SDK 8.0+ Discord application + bot token Required FishMMO PostgreSQL database Required (chat, accounts, links) Architecture FishMMO-DiscordBot/ ├── Program.cs # Generic host + DI composition + bot startup ├── ChatChannel.cs # Enum / mapping of FishMMO chat channels ├── Data/ # Plain DTOs / persisted bot state ├── Modules/ # Discord text command handlers │ ├── AdminModule.cs │ ├── CharacterModule.cs │ ├── CommandListModule.cs │ ├── DatabaseModule.cs │ ├── GeneralModule.cs │ ├── LinkModule.cs │ └── ModerationModule.cs └── Services/ # Long-running hosted services ├── AccountLinkingService.cs ├── BotConfigurationService.cs ├── BridgeBanService.cs ├── ChatPollingService.cs ├── ChatRelayPolicy.cs ├── CommandHandlingService.cs ├── DiscordVerificationService.cs ├── DynamicChannelManagerService.cs ├── GameChatBridgeService.cs └── RateLimiterService.cs The generic host wires IHostedService implementations for each background worker; the bot's lifetime is the host's lifetime. Configuration comes from FishMMO-Setup/<Environment>/appsettings.DiscordBot.json, which the build copies into the output directory as appsettings.json / appsettings.Production.json. Key Components Modules (Discord-side commands) Module Responsibility AdminModule Owner / admin-only commands (command permissions, diagnostics). CharacterModule char inspect / char whois — character lookup, and the game account, Discord username and linked-since date of a linked Discord user. CommandListModule help — self-documenting command list. DatabaseModule Read-only DB queries gated behind admin permissions. getaccount shows the account's Discord username, whether a Discord user is linked, whether Discord is verified, and whether the verification DM went out. GeneralModule Ping, status, server uptime. LinkModule /link issues a short-lived code the player types into game chat; /unlink removes the link. Both read and write the link in the database. ModerationModule mod kick / mod ban / mod unban on game accounts, and ban / unban for the chat bridge (uses BridgeBanService). The game-account commands need the Discord user linked to a Game Master or Admin game account, apply the Control Panel's guards (not yourself, not a peer or superior), call the same account services the panel does, and write each attempt to the admin audit log with source discord. Services (long-running workers) Service Responsibility BotConfigurationService Loads and saves botconfig.json (dynamic channels) and botdata.json (bridge bans, muted zones, command permissions, and legacy links awaiting import). AccountLinkingService Holds pending /link codes in memory, writes confirmed links to the database, caches link lookups for 60 s, and imports old botdata.json links on start. DiscordVerificationService Delivers the one Discord verification DM per account. Woken by PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY, a slow safety sweep, the gateway's Ready event and member joins. See Account Verification by Discord. ChatPollingService Reads new chat rows at a configured interval through ChatService.FetchRelayAsync and a ChatReadWindow, spots /link codes typed in game chat, and relays allowed channels to Discord. ChatRelayPolicy The allowlist of in-game channels that may be republished to Discord. GameChatBridgeService Writes Discord messages from managed channels into the game's chat table through ChatService.PersistBridgedAsync, after rate-limit and bridge-ban checks. DynamicChannelManagerService Creates / archives Discord channels for game worlds and scenes. CommandHandlingService Dispatches inbound Discord messages to Modules/ and handles command results. BridgeBanService Tracks characters and accounts banned from the bridge; consulted before forwarding. A Discord author is checked by their linked account. RateLimiterService Per-user sliding-window rate limiter for the bridge. Data Data/ holds the bot's own persisted state (BotPersistentData, bridge bans, command permissions, dynamic channel state) and in-memory DTOs such as PendingLinkVerification. LinkedAccount survives only so old botdata.json files still load; see Account Links. Account Verification by Discord A player can verify their game account by email, SMS or Discord, and any one correct code verifies it. For Discord they give their Discord username at registration, in either form Discord uses — fishfan, or FishFan#1234 for a name that still has its discriminator. The database stores it lowercase. The game or the Control Panel issues the code. The bot's only job is to carry it: players never type a code into Discord. The bot sends exactly one DM, ever Each account is sent its code once. There are no resends, and there is no command to ask for one. A delivery is claimed in the database before the bot sends it and marked delivered after, so two bot instances — or a bot racing a player who has just verified by email — cannot both send. What happens when a send fails depends on whether the message could have gone out: Outcome What the bot does Delivered Marks it delivered. Nothing is ever sent for that account again. Discord definitely refused it (a 4xx, e.g. 50007 — the member's DMs are closed or they blocked the bot) Releases it with the reason, and counts an attempt. After MaxSendAttempts (5) it stops. Discord rate-limited it (429) Releases it uncounted; it goes out on a later pass. Unknown — a timeout, a 5xx, a dropped connection Leaves it claimed and logs an error for staff. Why an ambiguous failure stays claimed. A timed-out request may already have delivered the message. Retrying it is exactly the second DM this design exists to prevent, so the bot doesn't: one DM ever beats a guaranteed delivery. Staff check with the player and resolve the row by hand. For the same reason the send turns off Discord.Net's automatic retry of timeouts and 502s; only rate limits are retried. The bot also will not DM a Discord user who is already linked to a different game account; that delivery is released with the reason and counts as an attempt. Players must join the Discord server Discord only lets a bot DM someone it shares a server with, and only lets it look a username up among that server's members. So Discord:DefaultGuildId must be the server the game's invite link sends players to. A player who isn't a member yet is recorded as waiting to join, and is sent their code the moment they join. The join is handled from the gateway's member-joined event, with a read of just that member's username, not by polling. On a delivery's very first try, if the member isn't in the local member cache, the bot makes one REST member search. After that it relies on the cache and the join event, so a player who never joins costs nothing per sweep. A username matches a member ignoring case. A bare name (fishfan) matches only a member without a discriminator, and a tagged name (fishfan#1234) needs the exact discriminator. If a name matches more than one member, the bot sends nothing and records why. A DM to the wrong person puts a verification code in a stranger's hands. Why LISTEN/NOTIFY and not polling Codes are rare and the accounts table is not small, so the bot doesn't query it on a timer. Issuing a code raises a PostgreSQL notification on fishmmo_discord_verification. The bot keeps one dedicated, unpooled connection on LISTEN (a LISTEN is session state, and the shared pool doesn't reset sessions), and runs a pass when it fires. It reconnects with capped exponential backoff, logging once per outage, and runs a pass after every reconnect, in case something was raised while it was down. A slow safety sweep (SweepMinutes, default 5) and the gateway's Ready event catch anything raised while the bot itself was down. Passes never overlap: every wake source signals one queue with a single reader, and wakes during a pass fold into one more pass. Pacing MinDmIntervalMs (default 1500 ms, never below 250) is a global minimum gap between any two DMs, sent or failed. Nothing a player does can make the bot send faster than that. Privileged intent Matching usernames against members needs the Server Members (GUILD_MEMBERS) privileged intent, enabled in the Discord developer portal. The bot already requests it and downloads the member list on connect. A pass waits until that download completes, so nobody is wrongly recorded as not having joined. Account Links A game account's linked Discord user is a database column, unique across accounts: one Discord account links one game account. A verified Discord code and a /link are the same link. /link <character> DMs the player a short-lived code. When that code appears in game chat from the named character, the bot links the character's account. Only the pending code lives in memory; the link is written to the database. If the Discord user is already linked to a different account, nothing changes and the player is told why. /unlink removes the link. The account stays verified — an unlink is not a reason to lock a player out — but the Discord channel's own proof goes. char whois shows the linked game account, Discord username and linked-since date. A link names an account, not a character. The bridge-ban check on a Discord author uses their linked account. Lookups are cached for 60 seconds, because the bridge checks the link on every message. Links this bot makes or removes take effect at once. A link made in the game or Control Panel is seen within the minute. Migrating from botdata.json. Older bots kept links in botdata.json. On start the bot imports every remaining entry into the database. It removes the entries that imported, and the ones the database refused for good (that Discord user is linked to another account, the account no longer exists, or the account already has a different Discord user), logging each refusal. Entries that failed transiently stay in the file and are retried on the next start. Configuration Configuration lives in FishMMO-Setup/Development/appsettings.DiscordBot.json and FishMMO-Setup/Production/appsettings.DiscordBot.json. The build copies them to the output directory as appsettings.json and appsettings.Production.json, and appsettings.json files in the working directory override them. appsettings.json shape { "Discord": { "DefaultGuildId": 0 }, "Npgsql": { "Host": "127.0.0.1", "Port": "5432", "Database": "fishmmo", "Schema": "public" }, "ChatPollingIntervalSeconds": 5, "ChatRelay": { "GameToDiscordChannels": [ "World", "Trade", "Region" ] }, "BridgeMessageMaxLength": 128, "DiscordVerification": { "SweepMinutes": 5, "BatchSize": 25, "MinDmIntervalMs": 1500 }, "RateLimiting": { "MaxMessagesPerWindow": 5, "WindowSeconds": 10 } } Section Notes FISHMMO_DISCORD_TOKEN (environment) Secret. Not a config key: the bot reads its token only from this environment variable, and refuses to connect without it. Discord.DefaultGuildId The Discord server the bot operates in. Must be the server the game's invite link points players to — verification DMs can only reach its members. 0 disables channel creation and verification delivery. Npgsql Database host, port, name and pool settings, read by FishMMO-DB's NpgsqlDbConfiguration through the shared NpgsqlDbContextFactory, as every other FishMMO process reads them. No credentials here: they come from FISHMMO_DB_USERNAME / FISHMMO_DB_PASSWORD or the platform secrets file (see the FishMMO-DB README). FISHMMO_DB_HOST / FISHMMO_DB_PORT / FISHMMO_DB_NAME override the host, port and name. ChatPollingIntervalSeconds How often ChatPollingService reads new chat rows. ChatRelay.GameToDiscordChannels Allowlist of in-game channels the bot may republish to Discord. Omit for the default (World, Trade, Region). See the warning below. BridgeMessageMaxLength Caps a Discord message bridged into the game. Keep at or below the game's ChatBroadcast.MaxTextLength (128) — clients discard anything longer, so a larger value makes long messages vanish rather than arrive truncated. DiscordVerification.SweepMinutes Safety sweep for verification deliveries (default 5, clamped 1–60). Not the delivery path — LISTEN/NOTIFY and member joins are. DiscordVerification.BatchSize Most pending deliveries one sweep pass reads (default 25, clamped 1–100). DiscordVerification.MinDmIntervalMs Global minimum gap between any two verification DMs (default 1500, clamped 250–60000). RateLimiting Sliding-window settings for RateLimiterService. The relay is an allowlist, and private channels are not configurable. The bot used to select every chat row except Discord's own and forward it, which meant [Tell] whispers were republished to a public Discord channel — full message body, both character names. Relaying is now opt-in per channel. Tell, Guild, Party, Discord and Command are on a NeverRelayable set and are refused even if you name them here, with an error logged; making a private channel relayable is a deliberate code change, not a config edit. Inbound Discord messages are sanitised at the bridge and again server-side, and are no longer exempt from in-game tab filtering. Production: set FISHMMO_DISCORD_TOKEN, FISHMMO_DB_USERNAME and FISHMMO_DB_PASSWORD through the environment (or the database secrets file) rather than committing them to any appsettings file. Build & Run # Restore + build dotnet build FishMMO-DiscordBot.sln -c Release # Run from source dotnet run --project FishMMO-DiscordBot/FishMMO-DiscordBot.csproj The process is intended to be supervised — restart on exit. The published output is a self-contained app suitable for systemd, Windows Service, or Docker. Deployment Notes The bot needs the MESSAGE CONTENT and SERVER MEMBERS (GUILD_MEMBERS) privileged intents enabled in the Discord developer portal. Without Server Members the gateway refuses the connection, and verification codes cannot be delivered at all. Required Discord scopes: bot, applications.commands. Required bot permissions: read/send/manage messages in the bridged channels, manage channels under the dynamic category, and (for moderation commands) timeout / ban members. The database user needs LISTEN on the FishMMO database. Point the Npgsql settings (or FISHMMO_DB_HOST / FISHMMO_DB_PORT) at PostgreSQL directly, or at a pooler in session mode. A transaction-mode pooler (PgBouncer's default) drops LISTEN, and deliveries then wait for the sweep. A delivery left claimed after an ambiguous send is logged at error level with the account name. Watch for those; each one needs a person to check with the player. Run it on the same network as the database so polling and notifications stay prompt. Flow Diagram flowchart LR subgraph Discord DUser[Discord users] DChan[Bridged channels] DDM[Direct messages] end subgraph Bot["FishMMO-DiscordBot"] Host[Generic Host] Poll[ChatPollingService] Bridge[GameChatBridgeService] Cmd[CommandHandlingService] Link[AccountLinkingService] Verify[DiscordVerificationService] Dyn[DynamicChannelManagerService] Rate[RateLimiterService] Ban[BridgeBanService] end subgraph Game["FishMMO"] DB[(PostgreSQL)] Issuers[Game / Control Panel] Players[In-game players] end Players --> DB DB -->|poll chat| Poll Poll --> DChan DUser --> DChan --> Cmd Cmd -->|allow?| Rate Cmd -->|allow?| Ban Cmd --> Bridge --> DB --> Players DUser -->|/link| Link -->|code| DDM Poll -->|code seen in game chat| Link Link -->|link / unlink| DB Issuers -->|issue code + NOTIFY| DB DB -->|LISTEN| Verify DUser -->|joins server| Verify Verify -->|claim / delivered / released| DB Verify -->|one DM with the code| DDM DDM -->|player types code| Issuers Poll -->|new world / scene| Dyn --> DChan Host --- Poll Host --- Bridge Host --- Cmd Host --- Link Host --- Verify Host --- Dyn Host --- Rate Host --- Ban

guides/FishMMO-Installer/README.html.summary: FishMMO-Installer View this file on GitHub FishMMO-Installer is a cross-platform .NET 8 console tool that automates FishMMO server dependency setup. It provides an interactive menu-driven interface to install and configure all infrastructure components required to run a FishMMO game server. It also supports a CLI-driven non-interactive mode for headless/automated deployment. Table of Contents Description Supported Platforms Menu Structure CLI / Non-Interactive Mode Key Component Versions Architecture Configuration & Environment Prerequisites Build and Run appsettings.json Example install-config.json Schema Operational checks after installation NGINX setup guide (per OS) Flow Diagram License Supported Platforms Platform Install Strategy Windows 10/11 EXE/ZIP installers + Windows services (UAC elevation) Ubuntu/Debian apt-get + systemctl Arch Linux / CachyOS pacman + systemctl RHEL / Fedora dnf / yum + systemctl Menu Structure === FishMMO Installer === 1 : Runtime & Tooling 2 : Database 3 : Web Server 4 : Unity & Build 5 : Configuration 6 : Uninstall 0 : Quit 1 — Runtime & Tooling Option Description 1 Install dotnet-ef global tool 2 Install ASP.NET Core Runtime (8.0.x) 3 Install Visual Studio Build Tools (Windows only) VS Build Tools installs the .NET desktop development and Desktop development with C++ workloads plus the Windows 10 SDK silently via the VS 2022 bootstrapper. 2 — Database Option Description 1 Configure Secrets & Environment (database, mail, service — one file; also Configuration → 3) 2 Install PostgreSQL 3 Install PgBouncer (connection pooler) 4 Install FishMMO Database (user / schema / initial EF migration) 5 Create a new EF Core database migration 6 Grant user permissions on the FishMMO database 7 Delete FishMMO Database (destructive — prompts for confirmation) 8 Configure PgBouncer (generate pgbouncer.ini, auth_query or userlist.txt, Linux only) 9 Configure Server Keys (DB-backed deployment secrets — gate secret, HMAC key, KEK) A Create Admin Account (AdminAccountInstaller: Admin, verified, two-factor enrolled, audited; needs 9 first for the TOTP master key) 3 — Web Server Option Description 1 Install NGINX (1.29.5 on Windows; the distribution package plus its stream module on Linux) and configure service startup 2 Install / Renew Let's Encrypt certificate — Linux offers the DNS challenge through the Porkbun API (default, wildcard) or the HTTP challenge 3 Deploy FishMMO nginx.conf (from FishMMO-Setup/) for your domain, plus the UDP stream blocks 4 Configure Firewall Rules (opens FirewallInstaller.DefaultPorts — 443/tcp and 7770-7999/udp; port 80 stays closed) 5 Register FishMMO Web Servers as systemd Services (Linux: IPFetch, Patcher, WebGL, Control Panel) 6 Install / Renew Local Development Certificates (Linux) 7 Point DNS Records at This Host (Porkbun): A records for api, play, game, panel via porkbun-dns-hook.py records, with a dry run and confirmation first The menu entry always opens the two default TCP ports. Port ranges and UDP rules — the game servers' 7770-7999/udp in particular — are expressed in install-config.json's firewallPorts and applied by the firewall component; see install-config.json Schema. On Windows NGINX runs as a Windows service managed by NSSM 2.24 and TLS is automated via win-acme 2.2.9.1701. On Linux NGINX is managed by systemd and TLS is automated via certbot. The web server service registration (menu 3-5) registers systemd units on Linux, with environment variables set to Production (configurable via FISHMMO_SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT). On Windows it only logs a reminder: an NSSM registration path exists in SystemdServiceInstaller.InstallWindowsServicesAsync but nothing calls it yet. 4 — Unity & Build Option Description 1 Install Unity Hub 2 Install Unity Editor 6000.6.8f1 with selectable modules 3 Build all C# projects under a selected root directory 4 Build FishMMO-Unity (Client/Server/Addressables via headless batch mode) Available Unity modules Module ID Display Name linux-il2cpp Linux Build Support (IL2CPP) linux-mono Linux Build Support (Mono) linux-server Linux Dedicated Server Build Support mac-mono Mac Build Support (Mono) mac-il2cpp Mac Build Support (IL2CPP) mac-server Mac Dedicated Server Build Support windows-mono Windows Build Support (Mono) windows-il2cpp Windows Build Support (IL2CPP) windows-server Windows Dedicated Server Build Support webgl Web Build Support android Android Build Support ios iOS Build Support Default modules installed: linux-il2cpp, linux-server, webgl, windows-mono, windows-il2cpp, windows-server (windows-il2cpp only on a Windows host; the Hub skips it on Linux) Project build scans the chosen directory recursively for .csproj files, builds dependency-order projects synchronously first (FishMMO-Dependencies → FishMMO-Logger → FishMMO-Database → FishMMO-SharedUtility → FishMMO-Auth), then runs the remaining builds in parallel. Unity build locates the Unity Editor executable via multiple resolution strategies (env var, default install path, Unity Hub CLI, filesystem probe, interactive prompt), then invokes -batchmode -nographics with the appropriate -executeMethod target from FishMMO.Shared.CustomBuildTool. 5 — Configuration Option Description 1 Configure Web Server Settings (IPFetch, Patcher, WebGL, Control Panel) 2 Configure Discord Bot Settings 3 Configure Secrets & Environment (database, mail, service, Discord token: one file) The wizard (AppSettingsInstaller) supports configuration for 5 components: Component Menu Config File Key Settings IPFetch Web Server 5-1 appsettings.json HttpPort, Npgsql connection string Patcher Web Server 5-1 appsettings.json HttpPort, Patches directory WebGL Web Server 5-1 appsettings.json HttpPort Control Panel Web Server 5-1 appsettings.json HttpPort, Npgsql connection string Discord Bot 5-2 appsettings.json Guild ID, Npgsql host/port/database/schema, chat bridge, rate limiting. No secrets: option 3 opens Secrets & Environment (5-3), which holds FISHMMO_DISCORD_TOKEN and the FISHMMO_DB_* credentials. The installer's own database connection (Host, Port, Database, Username, Password) is not part of this wizard — it is menu 2-1, DatabaseSecretsInstaller, which writes the secrets file at DatabaseSecrets.DefaultSecretsFilePath or exports the same values as environment variables. For each component, the wizard can generate: appsettings.json — base configuration (chmod 600 on Linux) appsettings.Development.json / appsettings.Production.json — environment overrides (chmod 600) ~/.config/fish/conf.d/fishmmo-secrets.fish — fish shell snippet (chmod 600) fishmmo-secrets.env — systemd / Docker .env file in the target directory (chmod 600) %USERPROFILE%\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\fishmmo-secrets.ps1 — PowerShell snippet (Windows) %USERPROFILE%\fishmmo-secrets.cmd — CMD batch snippet (Windows) All secrets files set the same environment variable format. .NET IConfiguration maps double-underscore (__) to JSON nesting — e.g. Npgsql__Password → Npgsql:Password in appsettings.json. Note: These env-var secrets files contain database credentials and web server configuration only. Application secrets (gate secret, connection token HMAC key, signing key KEK) are never stored in env files — they are generated by the SecurityKeyInstaller and stored directly in the PostgreSQL database. Client-side .generated.cs files (ClientApiSecret.generated.cs, CertificatePins.generated.cs, HostConfig.generated.cs) are written from within the Unity Editor, in FishMMO > FishMMO Dashboard > Game Settings (Write Host Config, Fetch Pins → Write Pins to File, Write Secret to File). See FishMMO-Unity/GeneratedFileTemplates/README.md. CLI / Non-Interactive Mode The installer supports a full CLI mode for automated/headless deployment. Run FishMMO-Installer --help for the full list. Usage: FishMMO-Installer Interactive menu mode (default) FishMMO-Installer --help / -h Show this help FishMMO-Installer --version / -v Show version FishMMO-Installer --component <name> Install one component interactively FishMMO-Installer --non-interactive -f cfg Unattended install from config file FishMMO-Installer --dry-run Simulate without making changes FishMMO-Installer --validate Run post-install health checks FishMMO-Installer --generate-checksums Generate SHA256 hashes for downloaded files FishMMO-Installer --quickstart Unattended install with quickstart defaults FishMMO-Installer --accept-defaults / -y Skip confirmation prompts FishMMO-Installer --list-components List available component names and exit FishMMO-Installer --log-file <path> Write log output to a file in addition to console Full flag list as parsed by CliParser.Parse, including aliases the help text omits: Flag Aliases Argument Effect --help -h, /? — Print help and exit (before any initialization) --version -v — Print assembly version and exit --list-components — — Print the component name list and exit --component -c <name> Install one component (lower-cased; ignored if the next token starts with -) --config -f <path> install-config.json path for --non-interactive (default: install-config.json beside the EXE) --non-interactive — — Run the manifest at --config unattended --dry-run — — Simulate; overrides the manifest's own dryRun to true --validate — — Run HealthChecker and exit 0/1 --generate-checksums — — Hash the files named in checksums.json and rewrite it --quickstart — — Implies --non-interactive --config templates/install-config.quickstart.json (resolved against the EXE directory; exits 1 if absent) --accept-defaults -y, --yes — InstallerProcessHelper.AcceptDefaults = true — every Y/N prompt auto-accepts --configure-server-secrets — <regions> Comma-separated region IDs; runs SecurityKeyInstaller.ConfigureDatabaseKeysAsync and exits. Without FISHMMO_PG_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD it prompts for the superuser password --log-file — <path> Adds a FileLogger to the logging config for this run Unknown flags and stray positional arguments are ignored rather than rejected. Exit codes: 0 on success; 1 for a failed component, a failed health check, a missing/unparseable config, or a failed logging bootstrap; 2 when pre-flight checks report a blocking error in a CLI mode other than --validate. Available component names Component Description dotnet-ef dotnet-ef global tool (required for database migrations) aspnet-runtime ASP.NET Core Runtime 8.0 vs-build-tools Visual Studio Build Tools (Windows only) postgresql PostgreSQL server pgbouncer PgBouncer connection pooler fishmmo-db FishMMO database, user, and initial migration nginx NGINX reverse proxy letsencrypt Let's Encrypt TLS certificate unity-hub Unity Hub unity-editor Unity Editor + modules build-projects Build all C# projects build-unity Build FishMMO-Unity player/addressables appsettings Configure appsettings.json + secrets create-migration Create a new EF Core database migration firewall Configure host firewall rules systemd-services Register FishMMO web servers as systemd services (Linux) all Run every component in dependency order Pre-flight checks The installer runs pre-flight checks at startup in all modes. In non-interactive/CLI modes, blocking errors halt installation. In interactive mode, all results are shown as warnings/logs only: Internet connectivity (pings dot.net) Disk space (minimum 5 GB recommended) System memory (minimum 2 GB recommended) Administrator / passwordless-sudo access Port conflicts on standard FishMMO ports (80, 443, 5432, 6432, 8000, 8080, 8090) Key Component Versions Component Version dotnet-ef 5.0.17 (pinned for Unity3D compatibility) ASP.NET Core Runtime Latest in 8.0 channel (hardcoded fallback 8.0.16) PostgreSQL latest via package manager (Linux) / EnterpriseDB installer (Windows) PgBouncer latest via package manager, default port 6432 NGINX 1.29.5 (Windows ZIP), package manager (Linux) Unity Editor 6000.6.8f1 (InstallationConstants.UnityDefaultVersion, overridable at prompt) win-acme 2.2.9.1701 (Windows TLS automation) NSSM 2.24 (Windows service wrapper for NGINX) Visual Studio Build Tools VS 2022 bootstrapper (aka.ms/vs/17/release/vs_buildtools.exe) Note: The .NET SDK is a prerequisite for running this installer and is not installed by it. The ASP.NET Core Runtime download URL and SHA512 hash are resolved dynamically from Microsoft's official release metadata API, providing cryptographically-verifiable integrity for the hosting bundle download. Architecture Root-level installers (one file per subsystem) File Responsibility Program.cs Entry point — environment setup, config load, interactive menu loop, CLI dispatch InstallationConstants.cs All download URLs, filenames, version strings, default config values, EF paths, monorepo layout InstallerProcessHelper.cs Shared process execution, shell detection (fish → bash → cmd), prompting utilities, Linux DotNet PATH/DOTNET_ROOT bootstrap DotNetInstaller.cs ASP.NET Runtime install and version detection, dotnet-ef tool install, EF migration/database-update commands DatabaseSecretsInstaller.cs Interactive wizard for the installer's own DB connection (username, password, host, port, database) — writes the secrets file or exports the values as env vars; uses sudo on Linux when the secrets path needs root VSBuildToolsInstaller.cs VS Build Tools silent install (Windows only) PostgreSQLInstaller.cs PostgreSQL install, database/user creation, EF migrations, permission grants, database deletion PostgreSQLHardening.cs PostgreSQL security hardening — rewrites pg_hba.conf to scram-sha-256, updates postgresql.conf (partial class of PostgreSQLInstaller) PgBouncerInstaller.cs PgBouncer install, systemd service setup, pgbouncer.ini generation with auth_query (recommended) or auth_file/userlist.txt SCRAM-SHA-256 modes SecurityKeyInstaller.cs Cryptographic key generation and storage in the database (gate secret, connection token HMAC key, signing key KEK). Client .generated.cs files are generated separately from the Unity Editor. AdminAccountInstaller.cs Database → A. Creates an Administrator through the FishMMO-DB services with the servers' own credentials, mirroring a registration: SRP salt/verifier from the fixed identity, email profile, verified, access level Admin, TOTP secret under the master KEK, recovery codes. All writes are one transaction; the result is audited (source = installer). Shows the authenticator key (QR via qrencode when installed) and recovery codes once. NGINXInstaller.cs NGINX install, Windows service registration (NSSM), Linux systemd configuration, nginx.conf deployment LetsEncryptInstaller.cs certbot (Linux) and win-acme (Windows) TLS certificate automation for NGINX UnityInstaller.cs Unity Hub and Unity Editor install via Unity Hub CLI with module selection UnityBuildInstaller.cs Unity headless builds (Client/Server/Addressables) via -batchmode -nographics with multi-strategy editor resolution ProjectBuildInstaller.cs Staged/parallel dotnet build across all discovered .csproj files with priority-based ordering AppSettingsInstaller.cs Interactive wizard to write appsettings.json, env overlays, and secrets env-var files for FishMMO web servers including the Control Panel (ConfigureAppSettings) and the Discord Bot (ConfigureDiscordBotComponent). Client security files are not generated here — use SecurityKeyInstaller (DB) + the Unity dashboard (client .generated.cs). LinuxConfigHardeningHelper.cs Atomic privileged file writes via sudo install, one-time .pre-fishmmo.bak backups, idempotent managed-marker detection Components (cross-cutting concerns) File Responsibility Components/FirewallInstaller.cs Host firewall rule creation from FirewallPortSpec values (ufw preferred then firewalld on Linux, netsh on Windows). Exposes DefaultPorts (443/tcp, 7770-7999/udp; never 80/tcp) — the list used by the menu and by any manifest that names no ports Components/HealthChecker.cs Post-install validation — .NET SDK, ASP.NET Runtime, PostgreSQL, NGINX, PgBouncer, systemd services, database connectivity, disk space Components/SystemdServiceInstaller.cs Cross-platform service installation — systemd unit files on Linux, NSSM Windows services on Windows. Covers web servers (IPFetch, Patcher, WebGL) and the AppHealthMonitor daemon Infrastructure (shared services) File Responsibility Infrastructure/CliParser.cs CLI argument parsing into CliCommand model, help/version text Infrastructure/DotNetReleaseHelper.cs Dynamic ASP.NET Core Runtime URL and version resolution from Microsoft release metadata API Infrastructure/DownloadHelper.cs File downloads with SHA256/SHA512 integrity verification, progress bars, checksum management, disk-space gating Infrastructure/InstallOrchestrator.cs Multi-component orchestration with dependency ordering, manifest-driven non-interactive installs. RunComponentAsync takes the optional InstallManifest, so the firewall and systemd-services components use the manifest's firewallPorts / webServers instead of hardcoded defaults Infrastructure/LinuxPackageManagerHelper.cs Package manager detection and command generation (pacman, apt-get, dnf, yum) Infrastructure/PlatformAbstractions.cs IPlatform interface + Windows/Linux implementations with PlatformFactory singleton Infrastructure/PreFlightChecker.cs System readiness checks (internet, disk, RAM, admin access, port conflicts) Models (data transfer objects) File Responsibility Models/CliCommand.cs Parsed CLI command record (Help, Version, NonInteractive, DryRun, Validate, GenerateChecksums, Quickstart, AcceptDefaults, ListComponents, LogFilePath, ComponentName, ConfigFilePath) Models/InstallManifest.cs Deserialized install-config.json model for non-interactive installations Models/InstallResult.cs Single component installation result (Success, ComponentName, ErrorMessage, Duration) Configuration & Environment At startup, the installer resolves the active environment name once and propagates it to all three standard variables: FISHMMO_ENVIRONMENT DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT The environment name is resolved via DatabaseConfigurationHelper.ResolveEnvironmentName() which checks (in order): FISHMMO_ENVIRONMENT env var → DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT → ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT. Defaults to "Development" if none are set. Configuration is loaded via DatabaseConfigurationHelper.BuildDesignTimeConfiguration, which: Checks the working directory for appsettings.json (operator override). Falls back to the bundled copy in the EXE directory (copied from FishMMO-Setup/Development/appsettings.Database.json at build time). Merges an optional appsettings.{Environment}.json overlay. Applies environment variables as the highest-priority source. Environment variables for non-interactive mode When running in non-interactive mode (--non-interactive or --component), some components require credentials that would normally be prompted interactively. Set these environment variables before launching to enable fully unattended operation: Variable Used by Description FISHMMO_INSTALL_ROOT all Override monorepo root path (skips auto-detection; useful for published builds) FISHMMO_LOG_LEVEL all Override console logging verbosity (e.g. Debug, Verbose). Requires restart. FISHMMO_PG_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD fishmmo-db PostgreSQL superuser password (avoids interactive prompt) FISHMMO_PG_LISTEN_ADDRESSES PostgreSQL hardening Override listen_addresses in postgresql.conf (default: localhost) FISHMMO_UNITY_EXE build-unity Path to Unity Editor executable (skips auto-detection) FISHMMO_SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT service installers Override the environment name set in systemd/NSSM service units (default: Production) FISHMMO_CLIENT_GATE_SECRET --configure-server-secrets Pre-populate the gate secret for DB storage (if unset, SecurityKeyInstaller generates one automatically). Not read directly by web servers — they load it from the DB at startup. FISHMMO_SIGNING_KEY_KEK_BASE64 --configure-server-secrets Pre-populate the signing key KEK for DB storage (if unset, SecurityKeyInstaller generates one automatically). Logging is bootstrapped from logging.json (copied from FishMMO-Setup/logging.json at build time). The FISHMMO_LOG_LEVEL environment variable overrides console verbosity at runtime without editing the file. Linux DotNet environment Before any dotnet command runs on Linux, the installer prepares the runtime environment in-process (once per process lifetime): Adds ~/.dotnet to PATH if missing Adds ~/.dotnet/tools to PATH if missing Sets DOTNET_ROOT to ~/.dotnet if it exists, otherwise /usr/share/dotnet EF Core project paths (relative to EXE output directory) Role Path EF project ./FishMMO-Database/FishMMO-DB/FishMMO-DB.csproj Startup project ./FishMMO-Database/FishMMO-DB-Migrator/FishMMO-DB-Migrator.csproj Migrations output Migrations/ (inside the FishMMO-DB project) MSBuild note: There is no stash-and-restore step. The installer's CopyFishMMODatabase target (in FishMMO-Installer.csproj) mirrors the FishMMO-Database source tree into its output directory but excludes **\Migrations\** — along with bin, obj, and .vs. Generated migrations therefore stay solely in the real FishMMO-DB project and are never copied, so an installer dotnet clean / dotnet build cycle cannot duplicate or clobber them. Unity executable resolution Unity builds resolve the editor executable in this order: Cached value from a previous successful resolve in the same session FISHMMO_UNITY_EXE environment variable (set this to skip auto-detection) Default Unity Hub install path for the configured version Unity Hub CLI (unityhub -- --headless editors --installed) output Common alternate install locations (/opt, ~/.local/share/unityhub, etc.) Interactive prompt for a user-supplied path Monorepo root detection The installer checks FISHMMO_INSTALL_ROOT first (if set), then walks up from the executing assembly until it finds a directory containing both FishMMO-Unity and FishMMO-Setup subdirectories. Falls back to ~/Dev/FishMMO-Dev if not found. If the env var path exists but is missing expected subdirectories, a warning is logged and the path is used anyway. Prerequisites .NET SDK 8+ to build and run this repository Administrator / root privileges for system-level installs Internet connectivity for downloads and package repositories 5 GB+ free disk space recommended (Unity Editor + build tools) 2 GB+ RAM recommended Install .NET SDK (if not already installed) Windows 10/11 Install from Microsoft: https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0 Then verify: dotnet --list-sdks Ubuntu/Debian sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y dotnet-sdk-8.0 dotnet --list-sdks Arch Linux / CachyOS sudo pacman -S --noconfirm dotnet-sdk dotnet --list-sdks RHEL / Fedora sudo dnf install -y dotnet-sdk-8.0 dotnet --list-sdks Build and Run The solution file is at the repository root: cd path/to/FishMMO-Installer dotnet build dotnet run --project FishMMO-Installer/FishMMO-Installer.csproj Run the compiled binary directly: Windows: Builds/FishMMO-Installer/Debug/net8.0/FishMMO-Installer.exe Linux: ./Builds/FishMMO-Installer/Debug/net8.0/FishMMO-Installer Important: logging.json and appsettings.json are copied from FishMMO-Setup/ to the output directory automatically by the build. Edit the templates in FishMMO-Setup/Development/ with your credentials before building, or use the Configuration wizard (menu 5) to apply overrides. Place a modified copy in the working directory to override the bundled defaults at runtime. Note: checksums.json is also copied to the output directory. Populate it with SHA256 hashes of your downloaded artifacts to enable integrity verification. See checksums.json below. appsettings.json Example Database operations require appsettings.json in the working directory. Non-sensitive settings (host, port, database name, pool sizes) are stored in JSON. Secrets (password) are set via environment variables — see the _comment field in each template for the env var name to set. { "_comment": "Non-sensitive defaults only. Override secrets via env vars: Npgsql__Password, Npgsql__Username", "Npgsql": { "Database": "fish_mmo_postgresql", "Schema": "public", "Username": "", "Password": "", "Host": "127.0.0.1", "Port": "5432", "CommandTimeout": 10, "ConnectionTimeout": 15, "MinPoolSize": 5, "MaxPoolSize": 100, "RetryPolicy": { "MaxRetries": 3, "BaseDelayMs": 20, "MaxJitterMs": 10 }, "QueryPerformanceTracking": { "Enabled": false, "Level": "Basic", "SlowQueryThresholdMs": 1000, "SampleRate": 0.1 } }, "ConnectionPoolHealth": { "WarningThresholdPercent": 70, "CriticalThresholdPercent": 85, "MonitoringIntervalSeconds": 60 } } Npgsql connection string format (for web servers) The IPFetch and Control Panel web servers read ConnectionStrings:NpgsqlConnection, a semicolon-delimited Npgsql DSN. The Discord bot does not: it reads the Npgsql section and the FISHMMO_DB_* credentials, like the game servers. Host=127.0.0.1;Port=5432;Database=fish_mmo_postgresql;Username=;Password=;Ssl Mode=Prefer; install-config.json Schema For non-interactive mode, create an install-config.json: { "components": ["postgresql", "fishmmo-db", "nginx", "letsencrypt"], "configureFirewall": true, "firewallPorts": [443, "7770-7999/udp"], "registerSystemdServices": true, "webServers": ["ipfetch", "patcher", "webgl"], "validateAfterInstall": true, "dryRun": false } Field Type Description components string[] Component names to install, in desired order (sorted by dependency before execution) configureFirewall bool Open firewallPorts after the components finish. Redundant when firewall (or all) is in components: that step already applies firewallPorts, and the post-install pass is skipped so rules are not added twice. firewallPorts (int \| string)[] Ports to open. A bare number is a single TCP port; a string may carry a range and protocol: "443/tcp", "7770-7999/udp" (ranges inclusive, protocol defaults to tcp). Defaults to [443, "7770-7999/udp"] if empty. Add 80 only for the Let's Encrypt HTTP challenge. registerSystemdServices bool Register webServers as systemd services after the components finish (Linux only). Redundant when systemd-services (or all) is in components, which already uses webServers; the post-install pass is then skipped. webServers string[] Web server names to register (ipfetch, patcher, webgl or fishmmo-ipfetch etc). When empty or omitted, all three are registered. validateAfterInstall bool Run health checks after installation completes dryRun bool Simulate without making changes Example templates Quickstart (minimum viable server): { "components": ["postgresql", "fishmmo-db", "nginx", "firewall"], "configureFirewall": true, "validateAfterInstall": true } Full stack (everything): { "components": ["dotnet-ef", "aspnet-runtime", "postgresql", "pgbouncer", "fishmmo-db", "nginx", "letsencrypt", "firewall", "systemd-services", "appsettings"], "configureFirewall": true, "registerSystemdServices": true, "validateAfterInstall": true } Operational checks after installation NGINX Linux: sudo systemctl status nginx sudo nginx -t Windows (PowerShell): sc.exe query "FishMMO-NGINX" PostgreSQL Linux: sudo systemctl status postgresql Windows: verify PostgreSQL service is running in Services or with sc.exe query. PgBouncer (Linux) sudo systemctl status pgbouncer sudo pgbouncer -V DotNet + EF tool dotnet --list-sdks dotnet tool list --global Confirm dotnet-ef appears in the global tools list. FishMMO web server services Linux (systemd): systemctl status fishmmo-ipfetch systemctl status fishmmo-patcher systemctl status fishmmo-webgl systemctl status fishmmo-apphealthmonitor Windows (NSSM / PowerShell): sc.exe query FishMMO-IpFetch sc.exe query FishMMO-Patcher sc.exe query FishMMO-WebGL sc.exe query FishMMO-AppHealthMonitor Services are configured with ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT, DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT, and FISHMMO_ENVIRONMENT set to Production (overridable via FISHMMO_SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT env var). On Windows, NSSM passes these via AppEnvironmentExtra; on Linux, systemd uses Environment= directives and an optional EnvironmentFile=-/etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env for database credentials. Application secrets (gate secret, HMAC key, KEK) are not set via environment — servers load them from the database at startup. Health check (built-in) FishMMO-Installer --validate This checks: .NET SDK, ASP.NET Core Runtime, PostgreSQL, NGINX, PgBouncer, systemd services, database connectivity, and available disk space. Download integrity verification The installer supports SHA256 checksum verification for all downloaded artifacts via checksums.json. This file is shipped with the installer and copied to the build output directory. Current state checksums.json contains the list of downloadable files with placeholder (empty) SHA256 checksum values and approximate file sizes. Empty checksums skip verification. To enable integrity verification, populate the file with actual hashes. Exception: The ASP.NET Core Runtime (both Windows Hosting Bundle and Linux tarball) is verified against Microsoft's published SHA512 hash from the .NET release metadata API — this happens automatically at download time, independent of checksums.json. Generating checksums Recommended: Use the built-in command after downloading artifacts: FishMMO-Installer --generate-checksums This hashes every file listed in checksums.json that is present in the working directory and writes the updated file back. Copy the result to the source directory to persist across builds. Manual method: After downloading all artifacts at least once (run the installer interactively or use --non-interactive with a config), you can also compute checksums manually: # Linux cd ../Builds/FishMMO-Installer/Debug/net8.0/ for f in *.exe *.zip; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then hash=$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1) echo " \"$f\": \"$hash\"," fi done # Windows PowerShell Get-ChildItem *.exe,*.zip | ForEach-Object { $hash = (Get-FileHash $_.FullName -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() Write-Output " `"$($_.Name)`": `"$hash`"," } Then update checksums.json in the source directory (not the bin output) so future builds include the verified hashes. NGINX setup guide (per OS) This section shows exactly where to place nginx.conf, which ports must be opened/forwarded, and verification commands. Required networking model Public internet ports to expose (host firewall and router forwarding): 443/tcp — HTTPS for api., play. and panel. 80/tcp — not needed with the DNS challenge; leave it closed so nothing unencrypted is reachable. Open it only to use the Let's Encrypt HTTP challenge (nginx then also redirects HTTP to HTTPS). 7770-7999/udp — QUIC/WebTransport game traffic. NGINX's stream module listens on these and forwards the datagrams, untouched, to the loopback-bound game servers. At minimum forward the ports actually in use: 7770 (Login), 7780 (World), 7790 upwards (one per Scene server). 443/udp — optional, HTTP/3 for play. Keep backend app ports local-only (do not forward publicly): 8000 (WebGL), 8080 (IPFetch), 8090 (Patcher), 8100 (Control Panel), 5432 (PostgreSQL), 6432 (PgBouncer). Router/NAT forwarding itself is configured on your router UI (not on the host terminal). Terminal commands below open host firewall rules only. Linux (Ubuntu/Debian + Arch/CachyOS) Order matters: certificate first, then nginx.conf. Every HTTPS server block in the FishMMO nginx.conf names the certificate, so nginx -t cannot pass before it exists. 1) Install NGINX and the stream module Web Server → 1. It installs nginx plus nginx-mod-stream (Arch, Fedora) or libnginx-mod-stream (Debian, Ubuntu); the stream module is what forwards the game's UDP ports. 2) Get the certificate Web Server → 2, choose DNS through the Porkbun API (default), enter the root domain (e.g. example.com). It issues one certificate for example.com and *.example.com, with --reuse-key, and deploys it for the game servers — see Linux game-server TLS deployment. It needs no nginx and no open port 80. Using the HTTP challenge instead, nginx must already serve the challenge directory on port 80, from a minimal config (not yet the FishMMO one): sudo mkdir -p /var/www/certbot/.well-known/acme-challenge sudo chown -R root:root /var/www/certbot sudo chmod -R 755 /var/www/certbot # port-80 server block: location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/certbot; } 3) Deploy the FishMMO nginx.conf Web Server → 3. It asks for the root domain and substitutes it for the template's fishmmo.com, checks the certificate exists, loads the stream module (writing /etc/nginx/modules.d/fishmmo-stream.conf on Arch), installs the config (backing up the old one as nginx.conf.pre-fishmmo.bak), runs nginx -t, then installs and runs /usr/local/bin/gen-fishmmo-stream-config.sh to write one UDP block per game port into /etc/nginx/stream.d/, listening on this host's LAN address (not 0.0.0.0, which would include the game servers' own 127.0.0.1 ports). Last it raises NGINX's open-file limit with /etc/systemd/system/nginx.service.d/fishmmo-limits.conf (LimitNOFILE=65535; reuseport opens one socket per worker per UDP port), restarts NGINX, and checks that UDP 7770 is really listening. 4) Open host firewall ports If using ufw: sudo ufw allow 443/tcp sudo ufw allow 7770:7999/udp sudo ufw allow 443/udp # optional, HTTP/3 sudo ufw status # 80/tcp only if you use the HTTP challenge instead of DNS If using firewalld: sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=https sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=7770-7999/udp sudo firewall-cmd --reload The menu entry (Web Server → 4) and the firewall component both open 443/tcp and 7770-7999/udp, and never 80/tcp. 5) Check NGINX sudo nginx -t sudo systemctl status nginx sudo ss -ulpn | grep ':7770' # nginx listening on the first game port 6) Router/NAT forwarding Forward these from router WAN to your Linux host's LAN IP (give it a fixed address or DHCP reservation): TCP 443 → <server_lan_ip> (TCP 80 only with the HTTP challenge) UDP 7770-7999 → <server_lan_ip> UDP 443 → <server_lan_ip> (optional) If the router's WAN address differs from what curl -4 https://ifconfig.me reports, the ISP uses CGNAT and inbound connections cannot reach you; ask the ISP for a public IPv4. Windows 10/11 1) Place your nginx.conf If installed by this installer, expected NGINX home is: C:\nginx\nginx-1.29.5 Copy config (the installer's "Deploy nginx.conf" option automates this): Copy-Item "C:\path\to\FishMMO-Setup\nginx.conf" "C:\nginx\nginx-1.29.5\conf\nginx.conf" -Force 2) Open Windows Firewall ports 80/443 On Windows the certificate comes from the HTTP challenge, so port 80 must be open for issuance and renewal (nginx answers it with the challenge files and an HTTPS redirect, nothing else). Run PowerShell as Administrator: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="FishMMO NGINX HTTP" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=80 netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="FishMMO NGINX HTTPS" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=443 netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name="FishMMO NGINX HTTP" netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name="FishMMO NGINX HTTPS" 3) Validate and restart NGINX service The installer manages the NGINX Windows service via NSSM. Service operations (install, start, stop, restart) require Administrator privileges — the installer checks this before any service operation. # Validate configuration & "C:\nginx\nginx-1.29.5\nginx.exe" -t # Restart via NSSM (preferred — handles service state correctly) & ".\nssm\nssm.exe" stop "FishMMO-NGINX" Start-Sleep 1.5 & ".\nssm\nssm.exe" start "FishMMO-NGINX" # Check service status & ".\nssm\nssm.exe" status "FishMMO-NGINX" sc.exe query "FishMMO-NGINX" Troubleshooting: Service won't start → check C:\nginx\nginx-1.29.5\logs\service-err.log (NSSM captures stderr) Port 80/443 in use → netstat -ano | findstr :80 Run installer as Administrator for all service operations If NSSM download fails, install manually from https://nssm.cc/release/nssm-2.24.zip 4) Router/NAT forwarding Forward these from router WAN to your Windows host LAN IP: TCP 80 → <server_lan_ip>:80 (the HTTP challenge) TCP 443 → <server_lan_ip>:443 UDP 7770-7999 → <server_lan_ip> (game traffic) Verify externally after forwarding From any external machine/network: curl -I https://play.your-domain curl -I --max-time 5 http://play.your-domain Expected outcome: HTTPS responds with your configured certificate HTTP times out when port 80 is closed (the DNS challenge). With the HTTP challenge it answers with a redirect to HTTPS Important FishMMO port notes Do NOT public-forward 8000, 8080, 8090, 8100. Do forward 7770-7999/udp: game traffic is QUIC over UDP and reaches the game servers through NGINX's stream module, never through 80/443. There is no WebSocket path. The public surface is 443/tcp, 7770-7999/udp and optionally 443/udp (plus 80/tcp only with the HTTP challenge). PostgreSQL hardening (scram-sha-256, listen_addresses — default localhost, overridable via FISHMMO_PG_LISTEN_ADDRESSES env var) is applied automatically during database setup on Linux. Flow Diagram flowchart TD User[Operator] -->|launches| CLI{CLI args?} CLI -->|--help/--version/--list-components<br/>--generate-checksums| Help[Print and exit] CLI -->|--accept-defaults / -y| Accept[Set auto-accept, continue] CLI -->|--quickstart| Quickstart[Unattended quickstart install] CLI -->|--validate| Validate[Health checks] CLI -->|--component X| Single[Install one component] CLI -->|--non-interactive| Manifest[Install from install-config.json] CLI -->|none| App[Interactive menu] App --> Menu{Main menu} Menu -->|1| Runtime[Runtime & Tooling<br/>dotnet-ef / ASP.NET / VSBuildTools] Menu -->|2| DB[Database<br/>PostgreSQL + PgBouncer + Server Keys] Menu -->|3| Web[Web Server<br/>NGINX + LE + Firewall + systemd] Menu -->|4| Unity[Unity & Build<br/>Unity Hub/Editor + C#/Unity Builds] Menu -->|5| Cfg[Configuration<br/>AppSettings wizard] Runtime --> Helper[InstallerProcessHelper<br/>OS-aware exec] DB --> Helper DB -->|option 9| Keys[SecurityKeyInstaller<br/>Generates & stores keys in DB] Keys -->|gate secret / HMAC key / KEK| DBSecrets[(PostgreSQL<br/>deployment_secrets<br/>connection_token_keys)] Web --> Helper Unity --> Helper Helper -->|apt / pacman / dnf / winget / choco| OS[(Host OS)] Cfg -->|writes| Settings[(appsettings.json)] Cfg -->|writes| Secrets[(fishmmo-secrets.env<br/>DB creds + web server settings only)] Unity -->|FishMMO Dashboard > Game Settings| ClientFiles[(ClientApiSecret.generated.cs<br/>CertificatePins.generated.cs<br/>HostConfig.generated.cs)] Manifest --> PreFlight[Pre-flight checks] PreFlight --> Orchestrator[InstallOrchestrator] Orchestrator -->|ordered| Components[Components installed<br/>in dependency order] Components --> Verify[Post-install validation] License See the main FishMMO repository for license information. Repair or configure local PgBouncer For the local Linux installation, a single command configures the installed service using the existing application credentials (no database password changes): sudo python3 /path/to/FishMMO-Dev/FishMMO-Installer/scripts/configure-local-pgbouncer.py --apply Replace /path/to/FishMMO-Dev with the checkout location. Run without --apply to list the planned runtime configuration changes. This requires the existing /etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env and the packaged pgbouncer account/service. It verifies application access to PostgreSQL on 5432, installs loopback PgBouncer on 6432, and tests application authentication and SELECT 1 before changing runtime settings. On a failed service/connection test it restores the previous PgBouncer files. After success it updates development templates, Unity's working-directory appsettings.Development.json, and existing .NET runtime output configurations — except the Discord bot's: its verification listener holds a LISTEN, which transaction pooling drops, so the bot always connects to PostgreSQL on 5432. When local peer authentication allows it, the tool copies the existing SCRAM verifier. Otherwise it uses the existing application password from the secrets file in the pgbouncer-owned 0600 auth file. Both modes authenticate with SCRAM; no PostgreSQL administrator password or database role changes are required. Production templates, installer settings and migration settings stay unchanged. Runtime configuration backups are private under /var/backups/fishmmo-pgbouncer. Restart any running applications afterward. Explicit environment port overrides still take precedence: runtime processes should use FISHMMO_DB_PORT=6432, while migration/admin processes should use 5432. Binaries published outside these known output directories need their runtime settings updated separately. To configure manually or use auth_query instead: Build the installer, then authenticate sudo in your terminal before opening it: sudo -v dotnet run --project FishMMO-Installer/FishMMO-Installer.csproj From the FishMMO-Installer directory, choose Database (2) → Configure PgBouncer (8). Enter the PostgreSQL superuser credentials and select backend port 5432 (or the actual PostgreSQL port). This port is independent of the runtime application port; never point the backend at PgBouncer's own listener, 6432. Choose Y for auth_query, or N to copy the application's current SCRAM verifier. The systemd service logs to the journal, so no manually created log or PID directory is needed. Auth-query mode stores only the lookup role's password in /etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt, owned by pgbouncer with mode 0600. Reconfiguration rotates that password and updates the file, repairing roles created by older installers that discarded the password. It does not change application passwords. The installer retains one-time configuration backups and checks the service restart. If application database credentials are available through DatabaseSecrets, it also connects through PgBouncer and runs SELECT 1; otherwise it reports that this test still needs to be performed. Before switching runtime connections, verify with your actual database and role: psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U fishmmo -d fishmmo -c 'SELECT 1' After that succeeds, set FISHMMO_DB_PORT=6432 in the environment of runtime servers, or update their Npgsql port settings. An existing environment variable or /etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env port override can take precedence over JSON. Keep migrations and administrative connections on PostgreSQL's direct port. Restart runtime processes to pick up their new connection settings. PostgreSQL remains on 5432; configuring PgBouncer does not automatically switch running applications. If the service or connection test fails, inspect: sudo systemctl status pgbouncer --no-pager sudo journalctl -u pgbouncer -n 50 --no-pager Linux game-server TLS deployment Web Server → 2 first asks which ACME challenge to use: DNS through the Porkbun API (default). Enter the root domain; the certificate covers example.com and *.example.com. The first run asks for a Porkbun API key and secret (create them at https://porkbun.com/account/api with DNS permission, and turn on API Access for the domain under Domain Management → Details). They are stored root-only in /etc/letsencrypt/fishmmo-porkbun.ini; later runs offer to reuse them. The hook, /etc/letsencrypt/fishmmo-porkbun-hook.py (source: FishMMO-Installer/Resources/porkbun-dns-hook.py, Python standard library only), creates the _acme-challenge TXT record, waits with dig until every Porkbun nameserver serves it, and deletes it afterwards. Certbot stores the hook commands in the renewal configuration, so renewals are unattended. It needs no nginx and no open port 80. HTTP on port 80. List every host name; nginx must already serve /.well-known/acme-challenge/ from the web root. Both issue with --reuse-key: release clients pin the certificate's public key, and a new key at each renewal would lock them out. The action then deploys the certificate to /etc/fishmmo/certs/fullchain.pem and /etc/fishmmo/certs/privkey.pem, matching the LoginServer, WorldServer and SceneServer configuration defaults. It prompts for an existing OS account that runs the game servers and adds it to fishmmo-certs. Start a new login session (or restart the service) to acquire that membership. Other game-server accounts must also belong to this group. Directories are root-owned and group-accessible (0750); certificate and key files are 0640. The private key is never made readable to all users. If the directory held a local development certificate, its marker is removed so the development action can never overwrite the real certificate. A root-owned Certbot deploy hook at /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/fishmmo-certificates validates that the certificate is unexpired and matches the key, then publishes both through an atomic current symlink switch. Unrelated certificate renewals are ignored. Previous release directories remain available for recovery. The installer enables certbot.timer or certbot-renew.timer when supplied by the distribution; otherwise it installs a twice-daily fishmmo-certbot-renew.timer. Successful renewal also tests and reloads nginx when it is active. Restart running game servers after renewal, since WebTransport loads its certificates at startup; the hook does not interrupt running game sessions automatically. It does not issue localhost development certificates. Selecting Let's Encrypt staging still produces an untrusted test certificate. Running the updated installer is required to deploy these changes on an existing machine; rebuilding a Unity server alone does not install host certificates. Local development certificates (Linux) Choose Web Server → 6: Install/Renew Local Development Certificates, or run FishMMO-Installer --component dev-certificates. This requires OpenSSL and sudo; it does not require nginx, public DNS, port forwarding, or Let's Encrypt. Choose the OS account that runs the game servers (for example jim). Choose Y when asked to trust the development CA if you want native clients on this machine to connect. The trust decision is local to this machine; other client machines need the public CA certificate imported separately. This component is deliberately excluded from --component all. The action creates a persistent, root-only local CA in /etc/fishmmo/dev-ca/ and issues an ECDSA P-256 leaf certificate valid for 13 days with SANs for localhost, 127.0.0.1, and ::1. It installs the certificate and key at the existing server configuration paths /etc/fishmmo/certs/fullchain.pem and /etc/fishmmo/certs/privkey.pem, with group access for the selected server account. It refuses to overwrite unmanaged/production certificates or a production renewal hook. No certificate validation is disabled. No Unity server rebuild is needed. Start a new login session, then restart Unity and running game servers so they receive the new group membership and certificates. Keep the API/WebGL local HTTP settings; this certificate action does not reconfigure nginx or web servers. For WebGL, supply the printed SHA-256 fingerprint via the client's WebTransport.SetServerCertificateHashes(...) before connecting. It is the leaf certificate's DER hash, not the API SPKI pin from the Dashboard's Certificate Pins section. The fingerprint is also saved to /etc/fishmmo/certs/server-certificate.sha256. Browser certificate hashes must be provided even if you trusted the local CA on the host. The installer does not yet automatically inject this fingerprint into WebGL builds. Rerun the same action before the 13-day certificate expires, restart servers, and update WebGL hashes after rotation. The CA is retained so native clients do not need to trust a new CA each time. Previous leaf releases are retained for recovery. The public CA is /etc/fishmmo/certs/development-ca.crt; never copy the CA private key or the server private key to clients. For testing generation without sudo or system changes, the source script supports bash FishMMO-Installer/Resources/InstallDevelopmentCertificates.sh --generate-only /tmp/fishmmo-dev-certs-test.

guides/FishMMO-Logger/README.html.summary:
FishMMO-Logger View this file on GitHub FishMMO-Logger is a small, configurable, JSON-driven logging library used by every headless FishMMO server (LoginServer, WorldServer, SceneServer, WebServers, DiscordBot, AppHealthMonitor) and by the Unity client builds. It exposes a static Log facade, a typed LogLevel enum, a structured LogEntry, and a plug-in model for sinks (ILogger + ILoggerConfig). Two built-in sinks are shipped — File (with rotation) and Email (via SMTP) — and you can register additional sinks at runtime. The library is netstandard2.1, has no dependency on Unity or EF Core, and is safe to reference from any FishMMO project. Table of Contents Description Supported Platforms Architecture Key Components Configuration logging.json shape File logger options Email logger options Initialization Example Extending — Adding a Custom Sink Build Flow Diagram Description The logger is intentionally small and synchronous-friendly. Application code calls Log.Info("Category", "message") (or Warn, Error, Critical, Debug, Trace); the call is dispatched to every configured sink that satisfies the configured minimum level. Log.Initialize(...) reads a JSON configuration file, parses it via a polymorphic ILoggerConfigConverter, and instantiates each registered sink type. The same library is used to centralize email alerts on Error / Critical log lines from production servers, and to write rotating per-server log files that the patcher service exposes to the operator dashboard. Supported Platforms Target Status .NET Standard 2.1 Yes .NET 8.0 servers Yes (via netstandard2.1 multi-target) Unity 6.6 Yes (referenced as a managed DLL in Assets/Dependencies/) Dependency Notes System.Text.Json Configuration parsing System.Net.Mail (BCL) Email sink Architecture FishMMO-Logger/ ├── Log.cs # Static facade — Initialize, Info/Warn/Error/... ├── LogEntry.cs # Immutable struct: timestamp, level, category, message, exception ├── LogLevel.cs # Trace < Debug < Info < Warning < Error < Critical ├── LoggingConfig.cs # Root config object loaded from logging.json ├── LoggingManagerConfig.cs # Per-logger envelope (Type + Config) ├── ConsoleFormatter/ # ANSI / plain-text console formatting helpers └── Logger/ ├── ILogger.cs # Sink contract: Task LogAsync(LogEntry entry) ├── ILoggerConfig.cs # Config contract per sink type ├── ILoggerConfigConverter.cs# System.Text.Json polymorphic converter └── Types/ ├── File/ # FileLogger + FileLoggerConfig (rotation, append) └── Email/ # EmailLogger + EmailLoggerConfig (SMTP) Application code only depends on Log and LogLevel. Everything else is internal plumbing that lets the JSON configuration round-trip into concrete sink instances at startup. Key Components Type Responsibility Log Static facade. Initialize(path), RegisterLoggerFactory(name, factory), Info/Warn/Error/Debug/Trace/Critical(category, message [, exception]), Shutdown(). LogEntry Structured payload passed to each sink — timestamp, level, category, message, optional Exception. LogLevel Ordered enum used for filter comparisons. LoggingConfig Root config object (LogLevel + Loggers[]). LoggingManagerConfig Polymorphic envelope { "Type": "File", "Config": { ... } } parsed by ILoggerConfigConverter. ILogger Sink contract — Task LogAsync(LogEntry entry). ILoggerConfig Sink-config contract — discovered by reflection / explicit registration. ConsoleFormatter Optional helper that formats LogEntry with ANSI colors for terminal output. Logger/Types/File/FileLogger Append-or-truncate file sink with byte-size based rotation. Logger/Types/Email/EmailLogger SMTP sink (typically filtered to Error / Critical). Configuration The logger is driven by a single JSON file (canonically logging.json) loaded via Log.Initialize("logging.json") at process start. The file binds to LoggingConfig. logging.json shape { "LogLevel": "Info", "Loggers": [ { "Type": "File", "Config": { "FilePath": "logs/app.log", "Append": true, "MaxFileSizeMB": 10 } }, { "Type": "Email", "Config": { "MinimumLevel": "Error", "SmtpServer": "smtp.example.com", "Port": 587, "EnableSsl": true, "Username": "alerts@example.com", "Password": "********", "From": "alerts@example.com", "To": "ops@example.com", "Subject": "FishMMO Log Alert" } } ] } Field Description LogLevel Global minimum level. Sinks may raise it further. Loggers Array of { Type, Config } pairs. Type must match a registered factory (built-in: File, Email). File logger options Field Description FilePath Path to the log file (created if missing). Relative to working directory. Append true to append; false to truncate on startup. MaxFileSizeMB Optional rotation threshold. Rolled file is renamed with a timestamp suffix. Email logger options Field Description MinimumLevel Per-sink override of the global level (recommended: Error or Critical). SmtpServer SMTP host. Port SMTP port. EnableSsl true for TLS. Username / Password SMTP credentials. Treat as secret. From / To Envelope addresses. Subject Subject prefix used for every alert. Security note: keep logging.json out of source control if it contains SMTP credentials, or load credentials from environment variables in a custom sink wrapper. Initialization Example using FishMMO.Logging; using System.Threading.Tasks; class Program { static async Task Main() { // Optional: register a custom sink type before initialization. Log.RegisterLoggerFactory( "MyCustomLoggerConfig", (cfg, logCallback) => new MyCustomLogger((MyCustomLoggerConfig)cfg, logCallback)); await Log.Initialize("logging.json"); await Log.Info("Bootstrap", "Application started."); try { // ... your code ... } catch (System.Exception ex) { await Log.Critical("Bootstrap", "Unhandled exception", ex); throw; } finally { await Log.Shutdown(); } } } Extending — Adding a Custom Sink Implement ILoggerConfig with the fields you need. Implement ILogger and accept your config in its constructor: public sealed class MyCustomLogger : ILogger { public MyCustomLogger(MyCustomLoggerConfig cfg, Action logCallback) { ... } public Task LogAsync(LogEntry entry) { ... } } Register a factory before Log.Initialize: Log.RegisterLoggerFactory("MyCustomLoggerConfig", (cfg, cb) => new MyCustomLogger((MyCustomLoggerConfig)cfg, cb)); Reference it from logging.json: { "Type": "MyCustom", "Config": { ... } } Build dotnet build FishMMO-Logger.sln -c Release The output FishMMO-Logger.dll is consumed by the other server projects via ProjectReference, and copied into the Unity dependencies folder for use by the Unity client and headless server builds. Flow Diagram flowchart LR App["App code
Log.Info / Warn / Error"] --> Facade[Log static facade] Facade -->|"filter by LogLevel"| Dispatcher{Dispatch} Dispatcher --> FileSink[FileLogger
